### 2.2.4 Functional Requirements Tables

This section provides detailed functional requirements for each feature, including requirement specifications, acceptance criteria, technical parameters, and validation rules.

#### 2.2.4.1 F-001: Unified Test Automation Framework Requirements

| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|----------------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-001-RQ-001 | pytest configuration with pytest-bdd, pytest-playwright, pytest-xdist plugins | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-001-RQ-002 | Gherkin feature file discovery from features/ directory with .feature extension | Must-Have | Low |
| F-001-RQ-003 | Step definition modules in step_definitions/ with automatic registration | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-001-RQ-004 | Centralized fixture definitions in conftest.py for browser context, httpx client, MCP client | Must-Have | High |
| F-001-RQ-005 | Parallel test execution via pytest-xdist with isolated browser contexts | Should-Have | High |
| F-001-RQ-006 | Async test support via pytest-asyncio for httpx API tests | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-001-RQ-007 | Test timeout management via pytest-timeout to prevent hanging tests | Should-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**F-001-RQ-001:** Given pytest.ini configured with pytest-bdd, pytest-playwright, pytest-xdist plugins, When `pytest --version` executed, Then all plugins show as registered and active.

**F-001-RQ-002:** Given .feature files exist in features/ directory, When `pytest --collect-only` executed, Then all Gherkin scenarios discovered and listed.

**F-001-RQ-004:** Given conftest.py defines browser_context, api_client, mcp_client fixtures, When test requests any fixture, Then fixture initializes successfully without errors.

**F-001-RQ-005:** Given pytest-xdist installed with 4 workers, When `pytest -n 4` executed, Then tests run in parallel across workers with no shared state conflicts.

**Technical Specifications:**

| Parameter | Input | Output | Performance Criteria |
|-----------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| Test Discovery | features/ directory path | List of discovered test scenarios | < 2 seconds for 100 .feature files |
| Fixture Initialization | Fixture name request | Initialized fixture object | < 500ms per fixture |
| Parallel Execution | Worker count (pytest -n X) | Test results from X workers | Linear speedup up to CPU core count |

**Data Requirements:**
- pytest.ini configuration file with plugin registration and feature directory paths
- conftest.py with fixture definitions using pytest.fixture decorator
- features/ directory structure with .feature files following Gherkin syntax
- step_definitions/ modules with @given, @when, @then decorated functions

#### 2.2.4.2 F-002: FastAPI MCP (Deterministic) Requirements

| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|----------------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-002-RQ-001 | FastAPI application with JSON-RPC endpoints for MCP tool invocation | Must-Have | High |
| F-002-RQ-002 | `seed_user` tool: Create test users with configurable attributes (username, email, role) | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-002-RQ-003 | `build_payload` tool: Construct request bodies from templates with parameter substitution | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-002-RQ-004 | `reset_env` tool: Restore environment to baseline state (database reset, cache clear) | Must-Have | High |
| F-002-RQ-005 | `query_state` tool: Inspect current environment state (user count, data records) | Should-Have | Low |
| F-002-RQ-006 | JWT token authentication for MCP endpoint access | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-002-RQ-007 | Health check endpoint returning server status and uptime | Must-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**F-002-RQ-002:** Given MCP client authenticated, When `seed_user` invoked with {username: "testuser", email: "test@example.com", role: "admin"}, Then user created in system and user_id returned.

**F-002-RQ-003:** Given payload template "create_order" exists, When `build_payload` invoked with template name and parameters, Then valid JSON request body returned matching template structure.

**F-002-RQ-004:** Given tests have modified environment state, When `reset_env` invoked, Then all test data deleted, database restored to baseline, and success status returned within 5 seconds.

**F-002-RQ-006:** Given invalid JWT token, When MCP endpoint accessed, Then 401 Unauthorized response returned with error message.

**Technical Specifications:**

| Tool | Input Parameters | Output Response | Performance Criteria |
|------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| seed_user | {username: str, email: str, role: str} | {user_id: str, status: "created"} | < 200ms per user |
| build_payload | {template: str, params: dict} | {payload: dict} | < 50ms per payload |
| reset_env | {} | {status: "reset", duration_ms: int} | < 5000ms complete reset |
| query_state | {query_type: str} | {result: dict} | < 100ms per query |

**Data Requirements:**
- JWT secret key for token signing/verification (from environment variable)
- Payload templates stored as JSON schemas with parameter placeholders
- Database connection string for state management (optional SQLAlchemy integration)
- Baseline environment snapshot for reset operations

| F-007-RQ-003 | Gherkin steps implemented at business logic level (no UI details) | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-004 | Fresh browser context per test for isolation and parallelization | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-005 | Typed API client wrappers in api_clients/ with Pydantic models | Should-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-006 | Pre-commit hooks for code quality enforcement (ruff, mypy) | Should-Have | Low |
| F-007-RQ-007 | Documentation: Architecture decision records (ADRs) for pattern choices | Should-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**F-007-RQ-001:** Given pages/login_page.py exists, When LoginPage class inspected, Then class contains typed methods (login(username: str, password: str) -> None) without CSS/XPath selectors.

**F-007-RQ-002:** Given Page Object method needs to locate button, When locator defined, Then method uses page.get_by_role("button", name="Submit") instead of page.locator(".btn-submit").

**F-007-RQ-003:** Given Gherkin step "When user logs in with valid credentials", When step implementation inspected, Then code calls LoginPage.login(username, password), not page.click("#login-button").

**F-007-RQ-004:** Given conftest.py defines browser_context fixture with scope="function", When multiple tests run in parallel, Then each test receives unique browser context with no shared state.

**Technical Specifications:**

| Pattern | Implementation | Benefit | Validation Method |
|---------|---------------|---------|-------------------|
| Page Object | Class per page with typed methods | UI changes isolated to Page Objects | mypy type checking passes |
| Stable Locators | Role/label/test-id priority | Tests survive UI refactoring | Locator review in pre-commit |
| Business-Level Gherkin | High-level Given/When/Then | Non-technical stakeholders understand | PM review approval |
| Test Isolation | Fresh context per test | Parallel execution without flakes | pytest-xdist runs succeed |

**Data Requirements:**
- Page Object class templates with locator strategy guidelines
- Pre-commit configuration (.pre-commit-config.yaml) with ruff, mypy hooks
- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) documenting pattern rationale
- Code review checklist enforcing maintainability standards

### 2.2.6 Implementation Considerations

This section documents critical technical, performance, security, and operational considerations for each feature to guide implementation teams.

#### 2.2.6.1 Cross-Feature Technical Constraints

**Python Version Requirements:**
- Minimum Python 3.9 required (Playwright 1.55.0 dropped Python 3.8 support)
- Recommended Python 3.11 or 3.12 for optimal performance and type hinting
- All features must maintain backward compatibility with Python 3.9

**Concurrency and Parallelization:**
- All features must support pytest-xdist parallel execution (F-001, F-005, F-007)
- No shared mutable state between tests; use fixtures with function scope (F-007)
- MCP servers must handle concurrent requests from parallel test workers (F-002, F-003)

**Environment Configuration:**
- All runtime configuration via environment variables, never hardcoded (F-002, F-003, F-004, F-005)
- .env file for local development, GitHub Actions secrets for CI (F-005)
- Configuration validation on application startup with clear error messages

#### 2.2.6.2 Performance Requirements by Feature

**F-001: Unified Test Automation Framework**
- Test discovery: < 2 seconds for 100 .feature files
- Fixture initialization: < 500ms per fixture (browser_context, api_client, mcp_client)
- Parallel speedup: Linear scaling up to CPU core count with pytest-xdist

**F-002: FastAPI MCP (Deterministic)**
- Tool invocation latency: < 200ms for seed_user, < 50ms for build_payload
- Environment reset: < 5 seconds for complete state cleanup
- Concurrent request handling: 50+ requests/second across parallel test workers

**F-003: Playwright MCP (Exploration)**
- Browser control latency: < 500ms for click/type interactions
- Screenshot capture: < 1000ms for full-page screenshots
- Page structure extraction: < 2000ms for complete DOM analysis

**F-004: LLM-Assisted Test Authoring**
- Gherkin generation: < 5 seconds per scenario (Ollama local)
- Edge case suggestion: < 3 seconds per analysis
- Hosted API fallback: < 10 seconds accounting for network latency

**F-005: GitHub Actions CI/CD Integration**
- Environment setup: < 2 minutes (Python install, dependencies, browsers)
- Test execution: < 10 minutes for 100 tests with parallel execution
- Report generation and publishing: < 2 minutes total

**F-006: Allure Reporting & Observability**
- Report generation: < 30 seconds for 1000 test results
- Report page load: < 5 seconds initial load, < 1 second for navigation
- Artifact lazy loading: < 2 seconds per screenshot/trace

**F-007: Maintainable Test Architecture**
- Page Object method calls: No measurable overhead vs. direct Playwright API
- Locator resolution: < 100ms for role/label-based selectors
- Type checking: < 10 seconds for entire codebase with mypy

#### 2.2.6.3 Scalability Considerations

**Test Suite Growth:**
- Framework must support 500+ test scenarios without performance degradation (F-001)
- Allure reports must handle 5000+ test results with historical trends (F-006)
- MCP servers must scale to 20+ concurrent test worker connections (F-002, F-003)

**Data Volume:**
- MCP build_payload must support payloads up to 10MB (F-002)
- Allure artifact storage must accommodate 100MB+ of screenshots/traces per test run (F-006)
- LLM token limits: Ensure prompts stay within model context windows (F-004)

**CI/CD Scalability:**
- GitHub Actions workflow must support matrix execution across 3 browsers × 2 Python versions (F-005)
- Workflow must complete within 15-minute timeout for rapid feedback (F-005)
- Report retention must not exceed GitHub Pages 1GB storage limit (F-006)

#### 2.2.6.4 Security Implications

**Authentication and Authorization:**
- MCP servers require JWT token authentication; tokens must never be committed to repository (F-002, F-003)
- GitHub Actions secrets used for FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN and LLM API keys (F-005)
- Token rotation strategy documented for production environments

**Data Protection:**
- Test data must not contain production PII; use synthetic data via Faker (F-002)
- LLM prompts must not expose sensitive application details or credentials (F-004)
- Allure reports published to GitHub Pages must not contain sensitive data (F-006)

**Dependency Security:**
- All dependencies pinned to specific versions in requirements.txt (Section 0.3)
- Regular security scanning via GitHub Dependabot for vulnerability detection
- Pre-commit hooks include security linting via ruff (F-007)

**Browser Security:**
- Playwright browser contexts run in isolated sandboxes (F-001, F-003, F-007)
- Headless mode prevents UI-based attacks in CI environments (F-005)
- No browser extensions or plugins loaded to minimize attack surface

#### 2.2.6.5 Maintenance Requirements

**Dependency Updates:**
- Quarterly review and update of all Python packages (Section 0.3)
- Playwright browser binaries automatically updated via `playwright install` (F-001)
- Pre-commit hook updates managed via `pre-commit autoupdate` (F-007)

**Test Maintenance:**
- Page Objects isolate UI changes; update locators in one place when UI changes (F-007)
- Gherkin scenarios reviewed quarterly for business logic accuracy (F-001)
- MCP payload templates updated when API contracts change (F-002)

**Infrastructure Maintenance:**
- GitHub Actions workflow updated when GitHub Actions runner images change (F-005)
- Allure report retention pruned monthly to prevent storage bloat (F-006)
- LLM model updates evaluated quarterly for improved generation quality (F-004)

**Documentation Maintenance:**
- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) updated when architectural patterns change (F-007)
- README.md updated with new setup instructions when dependencies change
- This Technical Specification updated when feature scope or requirements change

#### 2.2.6.6 Monitoring and Observability

**Test Execution Metrics:**
- Allure reports provide test duration trends, pass/fail rates, flakiness detection (F-006)
- GitHub Actions workflow logs capture pytest output, MCP server logs (F-005)
- Custom Allure steps provide visibility into MCP tool invocations (F-002, F-006)

**MCP Server Health:**
- Health check endpoints (/health) expose server uptime, request counts, error rates (F-002, F-003)
- uvicorn access logs capture all MCP tool invocations with timestamps (F-002, F-003)
- Prometheus metrics endpoint (optional) for advanced monitoring integration

**CI/CD Pipeline Metrics:**
- GitHub Actions provides workflow duration, success rate, artifact size metrics (F-005)
- Allure historical trends show test execution time changes over 30 days (F-006)
- GitHub commit status checks provide at-a-glance pass/fail visibility

**LLM Usage Tracking:**
- Token consumption logged for cost monitoring (F-004)
- Gherkin generation quality tracked via human review approval rates (F-004)
- Ollama vs. OpenAI usage split monitored for cost optimization

## 2.3 Functional Requirements Framework

### 2.3.1 Requirements Documentation Standards

This section defines the <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">operational standards for documenting, validating, and maintaining functional requirements across all seven features of the test automation framework</span>. All requirements follow a standardized structure to ensure consistency, traceability, and testability.

#### Functional Requirements Structure

Each functional requirement is documented with the following attributes:

| Attribute | Description | Format |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| **Requirement ID** | Unique hierarchical identifier | F-XXX-RQ-YYY (Feature-Requirement) |
| **Description** | Clear, concise requirement statement | Action-oriented, testable description |
| **Acceptance Criteria** | Measurable pass/fail conditions | Given/When/Then format where applicable |
| **Priority** | Business criticality classification | Must-Have / Should-Have / Could-Have |
| **Complexity** | Implementation effort assessment | High / Medium / Low |

#### Technical Specifications Template

For each functional requirement, the following technical specifications are documented:

- **Input Parameters**: Data types, formats, validation rules, constraints, and default values
- **Output/Response**: Expected outputs, response formats, data structures, and success/error states
- **Performance Criteria**: Response time targets (p50, p95, p99), throughput requirements, and resource utilization limits
- **Data Requirements**: Data sources, persistence mechanisms, validation rules, and lifecycle management

#### Validation Rules Framework

Each requirement specifies validation across four dimensions:

- **Business Rules**: Business logic governing feature behavior, conditions, constraints, and decision trees
- **Data Validation**: Input validation rules (format, range, type checking), output validation, and error handling
- **Security Requirements**: Authentication, authorization, data protection, encryption, and audit logging
- **Compliance Requirements**: Regulatory, legal, organizational policies, and quality standards

#### Requirements Traceability

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All functional requirements maintain bidirectional traceability:</span>

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Upstream Traceability**: Each requirement links to its originating source in Agent Action Plan Section 0.1.3</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Downstream Traceability**: Requirements link to implementation files (Section 0.5), test cases, and documentation</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Lateral Traceability**: Dependencies and integration points documented in Feature Relationships (Section 2.2.5)</span>

### 2.3.2 Functional Requirements Catalog (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Current Requirement Count: 49 Requirements across 7 Features**</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This section provides comprehensive functional requirements for all features identified in the Agent Action Plan v0.1. Each feature's requirements include detailed acceptance criteria derived from the Special Instructions (Section 0.7), technical specifications, and validation rules. All requirements are testable, traceable, and aligned with the architectural constraints documented in Section 0.7.1.</span>

#### 2.3.2.1 F-001: Unified Test Automation Framework Requirements

| Req ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|--------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-001-RQ-001 | pytest configuration with pytest-bdd, pytest-playwright, pytest-xdist plugins registered and active | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-001-RQ-002 | Gherkin feature file discovery from features/ directory with .feature extension | Must-Have | Low |
| F-001-RQ-003 | Step definition modules in step_definitions/ with automatic registration via pytest-bdd | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-001-RQ-004 | Centralized fixture definitions in conftest.py for browser_context, api_client, mcp_client | Must-Have | High |
| F-001-RQ-005 | Parallel test execution via pytest-xdist with isolated browser contexts (no shared state) | Must-Have | High |
| F-001-RQ-006 | Async test support via pytest-asyncio for httpx API tests | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-001-RQ-007 | Test timeout management via pytest-timeout to prevent hanging tests | Should-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-001-RQ-001: pytest Plugin Registration**
- **Given** pytest.ini configured with `[pytest]` section including `plugins = pytest-bdd pytest-playwright pytest-xdist`
- **When** developer executes `pytest --version` command
- **Then** all three plugins (pytest-bdd, pytest-playwright, pytest-xdist) show as registered and active in version output
- **And** plugin versions match requirements.txt specifications (pytest-bdd 8.1.0, pytest-playwright 0.6.2, pytest-xdist 3.6.1)

**F-001-RQ-002: Feature File Discovery**
- **Given** .feature files exist in features/ directory with valid Gherkin syntax
- **When** developer executes `pytest --collect-only` command
- **Then** all Gherkin scenarios are discovered and listed in collection output
- **And** scenarios show correct file path and line numbers
- **And** discovery completes in < 2 seconds for 100 .feature files

**F-001-RQ-004: Fixture Availability**
- **Given** conftest.py defines browser_context fixture with function scope
- **And** conftest.py defines api_client fixture returning configured httpx.AsyncClient
- **And** conftest.py defines mcp_client fixture with FastAPI MCP connection
- **When** test function requests any of these fixtures as parameters
- **Then** fixture initializes successfully without errors
- **And** fixture provides expected interface (browser_context.new_page(), api_client.post(), mcp_client.invoke_tool())
- **And** fixture initialization completes in < 500ms per fixture

**F-001-RQ-005: Parallel Test Isolation**
- **Given** pytest-xdist installed with configuration for 4 parallel workers
- **And** each test receives fresh browser_context fixture with function scope (per Section 0.7.4)
- **When** developer executes `pytest -n 4` to run tests in parallel
- **Then** tests run concurrently across 4 workers without shared state conflicts
- **And** all tests pass regardless of execution order
- **And** test suite completes 3-4x faster than sequential execution
- **And** no race conditions or flaky test failures occur

**Technical Specifications**

| Parameter | Input | Output | Performance Criteria |
|-----------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| Test Discovery | features/ directory path from pytest.ini | List of discovered Scenario objects | < 2 seconds for 100 .feature files |
| Fixture Initialization | Fixture name as test function parameter | Initialized fixture object (BrowserContext, AsyncClient, MCPClient) | < 500ms per fixture |
| Parallel Execution | Worker count via `-n X` flag | Test results from X workers with isolated contexts | Linear speedup up to CPU core count |
| Timeout Enforcement | pytest-timeout configuration in pytest.ini | Test aborted after timeout with clear error | Default 30s per test, configurable |

**Data Requirements**
- `pytest.ini` configuration file with plugin registration and feature directory paths
- `conftest.py` with fixture definitions using `@pytest.fixture` decorator
- `features/` directory structure containing .feature files following Gherkin syntax
- `step_definitions/` modules with `@given`, `@when`, `@then` decorated functions

**Validation Rules**
- **Business Rules**: Tests must execute via pytest only; MCP servers are supporting services not test runners (Section 0.7.1)
- **Data Validation**: All .feature files must pass Gherkin syntax validation before test execution
- **Security Requirements**: No sensitive credentials in test code; all secrets via environment variables
- **Compliance Requirements**: Minimum 80% code coverage per Section 2.1.2.4

#### 2.3.2.2 F-002: FastAPI MCP (Deterministic) Requirements

| Req ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|--------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-002-RQ-001 | FastAPI application exposing JSON-RPC endpoints for MCP tool invocation | Must-Have | High |
| F-002-RQ-002 | `seed_user` tool: Create test users with configurable attributes (username, email, role) | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-002-RQ-003 | `build_payload` tool: Construct request bodies from templates with parameter substitution | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-002-RQ-004 | `reset_env` tool: Restore environment to baseline state (database reset, cache clear) | Must-Have | High |
| F-002-RQ-005 | `query_state` tool: Inspect current environment state (user count, data records) | Should-Have | Low |
| F-002-RQ-006 | JWT token authentication for MCP endpoint access with 401 Unauthorized on invalid tokens | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-002-RQ-007 | Health check endpoint returning server status, uptime, and readiness state | Must-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-002-RQ-002: seed_user Tool**
- **Given** MCP client authenticated with valid JWT token
- **And** test invokes `seed_user` tool via `mcp_client.invoke_tool("seed_user", {...})`
- **When** tool receives parameters `{username: "testuser", email: "test@example.com", role: "admin"}`
- **Then** new user created in system with specified attributes
- **And** response returns `{user_id: "uuid-string", status: "created", email: "test@example.com"}`
- **And** user persists for query via `query_state` tool
- **And** operation completes in < 200ms
- **And** no hardcoded test data exists in test files (per Section 0.7.3)

**F-002-RQ-003: build_payload Tool**
- **Given** payload template "create_order" exists in MCP server templates directory
- **And** template defines structure `{"customer_id": "{{customer_id}}", "items": [{{items}}], "total": {{total}}}`
- **When** test invokes `build_payload` with template name "create_order" and parameters `{customer_id: "123", items: [...], total: 99.99}`
- **Then** tool returns valid JSON request body with parameters substituted into template
- **And** response matches template structure with all placeholders replaced
- **And** Pydantic validation passes for returned payload
- **And** operation completes in < 50ms

**F-002-RQ-004: reset_env Tool**
- **Given** tests have modified environment state (created users, data records)
- **When** test suite invokes `reset_env` tool at teardown
- **Then** all test data deleted from system
- **And** database restored to baseline snapshot state
- **And** caches cleared (Redis, application caches)
- **And** response returns `{status: "reset", duration_ms: 3500}`
- **And** complete reset operation finishes in < 5000ms
- **And** subsequent tests execute from known-good state

**F-002-RQ-006: JWT Authentication**
- **Given** MCP server requires JWT token for all tool endpoints
- **When** client attempts to invoke tool with invalid or missing JWT token
- **Then** server responds with `401 Unauthorized` status
- **And** response includes error message: `{"detail": "Invalid or missing authentication token"}`
- **And** no tool execution occurs
- **And** security event logged for audit trail

**Technical Specifications**

| Tool | Input Parameters | Output Response | Performance Criteria |
|------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| seed_user | `{username: str, email: str, role: str, password: Optional[str]}` | `{user_id: str, status: "created", email: str}` | < 200ms per user creation |
| build_payload | `{template: str, params: dict}` | `{payload: dict}` validated against template schema | < 50ms per payload construction |
| reset_env | `{}` (no parameters) | `{status: "reset", duration_ms: int, records_deleted: int}` | < 5000ms complete environment reset |
| query_state | `{query_type: str, filters: Optional[dict]}` | `{result: dict, count: int}` | < 100ms per query |

**Data Requirements**
- JWT secret key for token signing/verification (from environment variable `FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN`)
- Payload templates stored as JSON schemas in `templates/` directory with `{{placeholder}}` syntax
- Database connection string for state management (optional SQLAlchemy 2.0.38 integration)
- Baseline environment snapshot for reset operations (database dump or migration scripts)

**Validation Rules**
- **Business Rules**: MCP server provides data/state management only; no test execution logic (Section 0.7.1)
- **Data Validation**: All MCP tool parameters validated via Pydantic models before processing
- **Security Requirements**: JWT tokens never committed to repository; stored in GitHub Actions secrets (Section 0.7.6)
- **Compliance Requirements**: All MCP tool invocations logged with timestamps for audit trail

#### 2.3.2.3 F-003: Playwright MCP (Exploration) Requirements

| Req ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|--------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-003-RQ-001 | `navigate` tool: Navigate browser to specified URL with page load confirmation | Must-Have | Low |
| F-003-RQ-002 | `click` tool: Click element using role-based selector or data-testid | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-003-RQ-003 | `type` tool: Input text into form fields with selector validation | Must-Have | Low |
| F-003-RQ-004 | `screenshot` tool: Capture page screenshot returning base64 or file path | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-003-RQ-005 | `get_page_structure` tool: Extract DOM structure with semantic elements and accessibility attributes | Must-Have | High |
| F-003-RQ-006 | Session management: Isolated browser contexts for concurrent LLM agents | Should-Have | High |
| F-003-RQ-007 | Gherkin generation endpoint: Convert exploration session to .feature file with Given/When/Then steps | Should-Have | High |

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-003-RQ-001: navigate Tool**
- **Given** Playwright MCP server running and accessible at `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL`
- **When** LLM agent invokes `navigate` tool with `{url: "https://example.com"}`
- **Then** browser navigates to specified URL
- **And** page load event fires and completes
- **And** response returns `{status: "loaded", url: "https://example.com", duration_ms: 2300}`
- **And** page load completes within 5 seconds timeout
- **And** navigation errors (404, 500) returned in response with status "error"

**F-003-RQ-002: click Tool (Stable Selectors)**
- **Given** page contains button with `role="button"` and `name="Submit"`
- **When** LLM agent invokes `click` tool with `{selector: {role: "button", name: "Submit"}}`
- **Then** click event triggered on button element
- **And** response confirms action: `{status: "clicked", element: "button[role='button'][name='Submit']"}`
- **And** operation completes in < 500ms
- **And** CSS class-based selectors avoided (per Section 0.7.2 locator priority)
- **And** ARIA roles prioritized over XPath expressions

**F-003-RQ-005: get_page_structure Tool**
- **Given** page fully loaded with semantic HTML elements (headings, buttons, links, forms)
- **When** LLM agent invokes `get_page_structure` tool
- **Then** JSON structure returned containing:
  - All headings (h1-h6) with text content and hierarchy
  - All interactive elements (buttons, links) with role and accessible name
  - All form fields with label associations and input types
  - All landmark regions (nav, main, aside) with ARIA roles
- **And** accessibility attributes included (aria-label, aria-describedby)
- **And** DOM analysis completes in < 2000ms
- **And** structure enables LLM to understand page semantics for test generation

**F-003-RQ-007: Gherkin Generation**
- **Given** LLM exploration session with sequence of interactions:
  1. `navigate` to "/login"
  2. `type` into email field
  3. `type` into password field
  4. `click` on submit button
- **When** Gherkin generation endpoint invoked with session history
- **Then** .feature file generated with structure:
  ```gherkin
  Scenario: User logs in with valid credentials
    Given the user is on the login page
    When the user enters valid credentials
    Then the user is successfully logged in
  ```
- **And** steps are business-readable, not UI-specific (Section 0.7.2)
- **And** file includes LLM generation metadata and pending_review status (Section 0.7.8)
- **And** generation completes in < 5 seconds

**Technical Specifications**

| Tool | Input Parameters | Output Response | Performance Criteria |
|------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| navigate | `{url: str, wait_until: Optional[str]}` | `{status: "loaded\|error", url: str, duration_ms: int}` | < 5000ms page load (configurable timeout) |
| click | `{selector: dict, timeout: Optional[int]}` | `{status: "clicked\|error", element: str}` | < 500ms element interaction |
| type | `{selector: dict, text: str, delay: Optional[int]}` | `{status: "typed\|error", element: str}` | < 300ms per form field |
| screenshot | `{full_page: bool, format: str}` | `{image_data: str, format: "base64\|png", size_bytes: int}` | < 1000ms screenshot capture |
| get_page_structure | `{include_hidden: bool}` | `{structure: dict, element_count: int}` | < 2000ms DOM analysis |

**Data Requirements**
- Browser context pool for managing concurrent LLM agent sessions
- WebSocket connection state tracking for streaming interactions
- Gherkin templates for scenario generation with business-level step patterns
- Exploration session history (interaction log, timestamps, page states, outcomes)

**Validation Rules**
- **Business Rules**: Playwright MCP is development-only; disabled in CI by default (Section 0.7.5)
- **Data Validation**: All selector objects validated for role/label/testid priority (Section 0.7.2)
- **Security Requirements**: Browser contexts sandboxed; no access to system resources
- **Compliance Requirements**: Generated Gherkin requires human review before commitment (Section 0.7.8)

#### 2.3.2.4 F-004: LLM-Assisted Test Authoring Requirements

| Req ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|--------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-004-RQ-001 | LLM provider abstraction supporting Ollama (local) and OpenAI-compatible APIs | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-004-RQ-002 | Gherkin scenario generation from natural language input or exploration logs | Must-Have | High |
| F-004-RQ-003 | Edge case suggestion based on scenario analysis or application inspection | Should-Have | High |
| F-004-RQ-004 | Test variation generation for parameterized testing with Examples table | Should-Have | Medium |
| F-004-RQ-005 | Human review workflow: Generated scenarios tagged with "pending_review" status | Must-Have | Low |
| F-004-RQ-006 | Metadata tracking: Generation timestamp, LLM model, review status, assumptions | Should-Have | Low |
| F-004-RQ-007 | Token counting and cost estimation for hosted LLM usage with budget alerts | Should-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-004-RQ-001: LLM Provider Abstraction**
- **Given** environment variable `LLM_PROVIDER` set to "ollama"
- **When** LLM client initialized via `LLMClient.create()`
- **Then** Ollama client created with connection to `localhost:11434` (default port)
- **And** client validates connection with health check request
- **And** no API costs incurred for local Ollama execution
- **Given** environment variable `LLM_PROVIDER` set to "openai"
- **When** LLM client initialized
- **Then** OpenAI client created with API key from `LLM_API_KEY` environment variable
- **And** client supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or Anthropic Claude via OpenAI-compatible endpoints

**F-004-RQ-002: Gherkin Scenario Generation**
- **Given** natural language input: "User logs in with valid credentials and views dashboard"
- **When** LLM invokes `generate_gherkin` function with input text
- **Then** .feature file generated with structure:
  ```gherkin
  # Generated by LLM on 2025-10-07
  Feature: User Authentication
  
    Scenario: User logs in with valid credentials
      Given the user has a registered account
      When the user logs in with valid credentials
      Then the user is redirected to the dashboard
      And the dashboard displays user information
  
  # LLM Assumptions:
  # - Authentication uses email/password
  # - Dashboard is default landing page after login
  
  # Open Questions:
  # - Should test cover "remember me" functionality?
  # - Should test verify specific dashboard widgets?
  ```
- **And** scenario is business-readable without UI implementation details (Section 0.7.2)
- **And** scenario includes 3-7 steps per Section 0.7.2 guidelines
- **And** file includes LLM assumptions and open questions (Section 0.7.8)
- **And** generation completes in < 5 seconds for local Ollama

**F-004-RQ-003: Edge Case Suggestion**
- **Given** Gherkin scenario for user login flow:
  ```gherkin
  Scenario: User logs in with valid credentials
    Given the user is on the login page
    When the user enters valid credentials
    Then the user is successfully logged in
  ```
- **When** developer invokes `suggest_edge_cases` function with scenario text
- **Then** LLM returns edge case suggestions:
  - Invalid password (incorrect credentials)
  - Expired session (session timeout)
  - Locked account (multiple failed attempts)
  - Missing credentials (empty email or password)
  - SQL injection attempt (security validation)
  - XSS attempt (input sanitization)
- **And** suggestions include rationale and business impact
- **And** analysis completes in < 3 seconds

**F-004-RQ-005: Human Review Workflow**
- **Given** LLM generates Gherkin scenario via `generate_gherkin` function
- **When** scenario saved to `features/` directory
- **Then** file includes YAML frontmatter:
  ```yaml
  ---
  status: pending_review
  generated_by: llm
  model: ollama/llama2
  timestamp: 2025-10-07T10:30:00Z
  reviewed_by: null
  ---
  ```
- **And** file name includes `_draft` suffix: `login_draft.feature`
- **And** scenario NOT executed by pytest until review status changed to "approved"
- **And** pre-commit hook warns if draft scenarios exist in commit
- **And** human reviewer must rename file and update status before merging

**Technical Specifications**

| Function | Input Parameters | Output Response | Performance Criteria |
|----------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| generate_gherkin | `{input_text: str, context: dict, model: str}` | `{scenario: str, confidence: float, assumptions: list[str]}` | < 5 seconds local Ollama, < 10 seconds hosted API |
| suggest_edge_cases | `{scenario: str, context: dict}` | `{suggestions: list[EdgeCase], rationale: dict}` | < 3 seconds per analysis |
| generate_variations | `{scenario: str, params: list[str]}` | `{examples_table: str, scenarios: list[str]}` | < 5 seconds per variation set |
| estimate_tokens | `{prompt: str, model: str}` | `{tokens: int, cost_usd: float, model: str}` | < 100ms calculation using tiktoken |

**Data Requirements**
- LLM API credentials (`OLLAMA_URL` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` from environment variables)
- Gherkin scenario templates and examples for few-shot prompting
- Edge case taxonomy database (common failure patterns, security vulnerabilities)
- Review workflow state stored in YAML frontmatter (pending/approved/rejected)
- Token usage logs for cost monitoring and budget alerts

**Validation Rules**
- **Business Rules**: LLM is helper for discovery and generation, NOT test runner (Section 0.7.1)
- **Data Validation**: All generated Gherkin validated against pytest-bdd parser before saving
- **Security Requirements**: No production credentials or PII in LLM prompts; sanitize inputs
- **Compliance Requirements**: All LLM-generated content requires human review before execution (Section 0.7.8)

#### 2.3.2.5 F-005: GitHub Actions CI/CD Integration Requirements

| Req ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|--------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-005-RQ-001 | Workflow triggers: push to main/develop branches, pull request creation/update | Must-Have | Low |
| F-005-RQ-002 | Matrix strategy: Parallel execution across browsers (chromium, firefox, webkit) | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-005-RQ-003 | FastAPI MCP server startup as background service with health check validation | Must-Have | High |
| F-005-RQ-004 | pytest execution with pytest-xdist 4 parallel workers for faster feedback | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-005-RQ-005 | Allure report generation from pytest results with artifact upload | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-005-RQ-006 | Test failure notifications via GitHub commit status checks and PR comments | Must-Have | Low |
| F-005-RQ-007 | GitHub Pages publishing for Allure reports with 30-day history retention | Should-Have | Medium |

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-005-RQ-002: Browser Matrix Execution**
- **Given** workflow YAML configured with matrix strategy:
  ```yaml
  strategy:
    matrix:
      browser: [chromium, firefox, webkit]
  ```
- **When** workflow triggered by push or pull request
- **Then** three parallel jobs execute, one per browser engine
- **And** each job runs identical pytest suite with `--browser ${{ matrix.browser }}`
- **And** all three jobs must pass for overall workflow success
- **And** results aggregated in final Allure report showing browser-specific pass/fail

**F-005-RQ-003: MCP Server Startup and Health Check**
- **Given** workflow includes MCP server startup step:
  ```yaml
  - name: Start FastAPI MCP Server
    run: |
      ./mcp_servers/scripts/start_fastapi_mcp.sh &
      sleep 5
      curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1
  ```
- **When** workflow reaches MCP startup step
- **Then** FastAPI MCP server starts as background service on port 8000
- **And** health check endpoint polled with retry logic (max 30 seconds)
- **And** health check returns `200 OK` response: `{"status": "healthy", "uptime_seconds": 5}`
- **And** if health check fails after 30 seconds, workflow fails with clear error message
- **And** server logs captured in workflow artifacts for debugging

**F-005-RQ-004: Parallel Test Execution**
- **Given** pytest configured with pytest-xdist plugin
- **And** workflow step executes: `pytest -n 4 --browser chromium --alluredir=allure-results`
- **When** tests run in GitHub Actions runner
- **Then** pytest spawns 4 parallel worker processes
- **And** each worker receives isolated browser context (per Section 0.7.4)
- **And** test suite completes 3-4x faster than sequential execution
- **And** for 100 tests, total execution time < 10 minutes
- **And** no shared state conflicts or race conditions occur

**F-005-RQ-006: Test Failure Notifications**
- **Given** test execution completes with at least one failing test
- **When** workflow reaches notification step
- **Then** GitHub commit status shows "failure" with ❌ icon
- **And** pull request comment added with failure summary:
  - Total tests: 150
  - Passed: 148
  - Failed: 2
  - Link to Allure report
- **And** failing test names and error messages included in comment
- **And** screenshot attachments for UI test failures embedded in comment

**Technical Specifications**

| Workflow Stage | Input | Output | Performance Criteria |
|----------------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| Environment Setup | Python version 3.11, requirements-dev.txt | Configured runner with dependencies | < 2 minutes (with caching) |
| MCP Server Startup | start_fastapi_mcp.sh script, env vars | Running server on port 8000 | < 30 seconds to ready state |
| Test Execution | `pytest -n 4` command with browser flag | Test results in XML/JSON format | < 10 minutes for 100 tests |
| Report Generation | allure-results/ directory | HTML report in allure-report/ | < 2 minutes generation |
| Artifact Upload | allure-report/ directory | GitHub Actions artifact (ZIP) | < 1 minute upload |

**Data Requirements**
- Workflow YAML definition (`.github/workflows/test.yml`)
- Repository secrets: `FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` (auto-provided)
- Browser binaries cached across workflow runs using `actions/cache`
- Python dependency cache for faster setup (pip cache or Poetry cache)
- Environment variables: `BASE_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `HEADLESS=true`

**Validation Rules**
- **Business Rules**: CI runs FastAPI MCP only; Playwright MCP disabled by default (Section 0.7.5)
- **Data Validation**: All environment variables validated at workflow start; missing vars fail fast
- **Security Requirements**: Secrets never logged in workflow output; masked in GitHub Actions logs
- **Compliance Requirements**: Test suite must pass in CI before merge (branch protection rules)

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-006-RQ-001: pytest-allure Integration**
- **Given** pytest.ini configured with:

  ```ini
  [pytest]
  addopts = --alluredir=allure-results
  ```
- **And** allure-pytest 2.15.0 installed

**F-006-RQ-003: Artifact Attachment (Actionable Reports)**

- **And** screenshot attached to Allure report via `allure.attach(screenshot, attachment_type=allure.attachment_type.PNG)`

  ```python
  @allure.step("Seed user via MCP: {username}")
  def seed_user_with_logging(mcp_client, username, email, role):
  ```

#### 2.3.2.7 F-007: Maintainable Test Architecture Requirements

| Req ID | Description | Priority | Complexity |
|--------|-------------|----------|------------|
| F-007-RQ-001 | Page Object classes in pages/ directory with typed methods using type hints | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-002 | Locator strategies: Prioritize get_by_role, get_by_label, get_by_test_id over CSS/XPath | Must-Have | Low |
| F-007-RQ-003 | Gherkin steps implemented at business logic level without UI implementation details | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-004 | Fresh browser context per test for isolation and pytest-xdist parallelization | Must-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-005 | Typed API client wrappers in api_clients/ with Pydantic models for request/response | Should-Have | Medium |
| F-007-RQ-006 | Pre-commit hooks for code quality enforcement (ruff linting, mypy type checking) | Should-Have | Low |
| F-007-RQ-007 | Documentation: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) documenting pattern rationale | Should-Have | Low |

**Acceptance Criteria**

**F-007-RQ-001: Page Object Pattern**
- **Given** UI test requires interaction with login page
- **And** file `tests/pages/login_page.py` exists with class:
  ```python
  class LoginPage(BasePage):
      def login(self, username: str, password: str) -> None:
          self.page.get_by_label("Email").fill(username)
          self.page.get_by_label("Password").fill(password)
          self.page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign In").click()
      
      def is_logged_in(self) -> bool:
          return self.page.get_by_role("button", name="Logout").is_visible()
  ```
- **When** developer inspects Page Object methods
- **Then** methods use type hints for parameters and return values
- **And** methods contain NO CSS selectors (e.g., `.btn-submit`, `#login-button`)
- **And** methods contain NO XPath expressions
- **And** methods delegate to ARIA role-based selectors (Section 0.7.2 priority)
- **And** mypy type checking passes without errors

**F-007-RQ-002: Stable Locator Strategies (Priority Order)**
- **Given** page object needs to locate interactive element
- **When** developer writes locator code
- **Then** locator selection follows priority order:
  1. **ARIA roles and accessible names** (highest priority):
     ```python
     page.get_by_role("button", name="Submit")
     page.get_by_role("textbox", name="Email")
     ```
  2. **data-testid attributes** (second choice):
     ```python
     page.get_by_test_id("submit-button")
     ```
  3. **Semantic labels** (form labels, button text):
     ```python
     page.get_by_label("Email Address")
     page.get_by_text("Submit Order")
     ```
  4. **Avoid CSS classes entirely** unless semantic:
     ```python
     # ✗ AVOID: page.locator(".btn.btn-primary.submit")
     ```
  5. **Avoid XPath expressions entirely**:
     ```python
     # ✗ AVOID: page.locator("//div[@class='form']//button[1]")
     ```
- **And** pre-commit hook validates locator strategies using ruff custom rule

**F-007-RQ-003: Business-Readable Gherkin (High-Level Steps)**
- **Given** Gherkin scenario describes user updating profile:
  ```gherkin
  Scenario: User updates profile information
    Given the user is logged in as an administrator
    When the user updates their email address
    Then the system confirms the email change
  ```
- **And** step definition for "user updates their email address":
  ```python
  @when("the user updates their email address")
  def update_email_address(profile_page: ProfilePage, new_email: str):
      profile_page.update_email(new_email)  # Delegates to Page Object
  ```
- **When** non-technical stakeholder (product manager) reads scenario
- **Then** stakeholder understands scenario without technical knowledge
- **And** scenario describes WHAT happens, not HOW it's implemented (Section 0.7.2)
- **And** step definition is 1-5 lines maximum (Section 0.7.6 "short step code")
- **And** no CSS selectors, coordinates, or HTTP details in Gherkin

**F-007-RQ-004: Test Isolation for Parallel Execution**
- **Given** conftest.py defines browser_context fixture:
  ```python
  @pytest.fixture
  def browser_context(browser: Browser):
      # Fresh context per test (function scope)
      context = browser.new_context()
      yield context
      context.close()
  ```
- **And** tests use browser_context fixture, not shared session-scoped context
- **When** tests run in parallel via `pytest -n 4`
- **Then** each test receives fresh browser context
- **And** each context has isolated state (cookies, local storage, session storage)
- **And** tests pass regardless of execution order
- **And** no flakiness from shared state (per Section 0.7.4)
- **And** test suite achieves >95% success rate in CI (Section 0.7.10 success criteria)

**Technical Specifications**

| Pattern | Implementation | Benefit | Validation Method |
|---------|---------------|---------|-------------------|
| Page Object | Class per page in pages/ with typed methods | UI changes isolated to Page Objects, reduces test maintenance by 40-60% | mypy type checking passes, ruff linting enforces patterns |
| Stable Locators | Role/label/test-id priority, avoid CSS/XPath | Tests survive UI refactoring without brittle selector failures | Pre-commit hook validates locator strategies |
| Business-Level Gherkin | High-level Given/When/Then, no implementation details | Non-technical stakeholders understand tests, living documentation | Product manager review approval in PR process |
| Test Isolation | Fresh browser_context per test (function scope) | Parallel execution without flakiness, pytest-xdist compatible | pytest-xdist runs pass consistently in CI >95% success rate |

**Data Requirements**
- Page Object class templates with locator strategy guidelines in `docs/page-object-template.py`
- Pre-commit configuration (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`) with ruff, mypy, custom locator validation hooks
- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in `docs/adr/` documenting rationale for:
  - ADR-001: Page Object Pattern adoption
  - ADR-002: Locator strategy prioritization
  - ADR-003: Browser context isolation approach
- Code review checklist enforcing maintainability standards

**Validation Rules**
- **Business Rules**: Tests must be readable, with short step code and stable selectors (Section 0.7.6)
- **Data Validation**: All Page Object methods type-checked; mypy strict mode enabled
- **Security Requirements**: No hardcoded credentials in Page Objects; use MCP seed_user for test data
- **Compliance Requirements**: All new Page Objects require ADR documentation and code review approval

This section documents the dependencies and integration points between features, providing comprehensive visibility into how functional requirements interact across the test automation framework.

**Dependency Relationships:**

- **F-005** (CI/CD) orchestrates F-001, F-002, and F-006 in automated pipeline
- **F-006** (Allure Reporting) integrates with F-001 and is published by F-005

#### 2.3.3.2 Requirements Integration Matrix

| Source Requirement | Dependent Requirement | Integration Point | Traceability |
|--------------------|----------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| F-001-RQ-004 (fixtures) | F-002-RQ-001 (MCP endpoints) | mcp_client fixture in conftest.py | Section 0.5, conftest.py implementation |
| F-001-RQ-005 (parallel execution) | F-007-RQ-004 (browser context isolation) | pytest-xdist + function-scoped contexts | Section 0.7.4 isolation requirements |
| F-002-RQ-002 (seed_user) | F-007-RQ-003 (business-level Gherkin) | MCP tools eliminate hardcoded data in steps | Section 0.7.3 data management |

### 2.3.5 Implementation Considerations and Constraints

This section documents critical technical, performance, security, and operational considerations that must be addressed during implementation of functional requirements.

#### 2.3.5.1 Cross-Cutting Constraints

**Python Version Requirements:**
- Minimum Python 3.9 required (Playwright 1.55.0 dropped Python 3.8 support per F-001-RQ-001)
- Recommended Python 3.11 or 3.12 for optimal performance, improved error messages, and enhanced type hinting
- All features (F-001 through F-007) must maintain backward compatibility with Python 3.9

**Concurrency and Thread Safety:**
- All functional requirements support pytest-xdist parallel execution (F-001-RQ-005, F-007-RQ-004)
- No shared mutable state between tests; fixtures use function scope for isolation (F-007-RQ-004)
- MCP servers (F-002, F-003) must handle concurrent requests from parallel pytest workers without race conditions

**Environment Configuration Management:**
- All runtime configuration via environment variables, never hardcoded values (Section 0.7.9)
- `.env` file for local development, GitHub Actions secrets for CI (F-005-RQ-006)
- Configuration validation on application startup with clear error messages and fast-fail behavior

#### 2.3.5.2 Performance Requirements by Feature

| Feature | Critical Performance Requirements | Acceptance Threshold | Monitoring Method |
|---------|-----------------------------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| **F-001** | Test discovery: < 2 seconds for 100 .feature files | 2000ms | Allure duration trends |
| **F-001** | Fixture initialization: < 500ms per fixture | 500ms | Allure step timing |
| **F-002** | MCP seed_user: < 200ms per user creation | 200ms | MCP server logs |
| **F-002** | MCP reset_env: < 5 seconds complete reset | 5000ms | CI workflow logs |
| **F-003** | Playwright click: < 500ms element interaction | 500ms | Playwright traces |
| **F-004** | Gherkin generation (Ollama): < 5 seconds | 5000ms | LLM client metrics |
| **F-005** | CI environment setup: < 2 minutes | 120 seconds | GitHub Actions timing |
| **F-005** | Test execution (100 tests): < 10 minutes | 600 seconds | Allure report summary |
| **F-006** | Allure report generation: < 30 seconds for 1000 results | 30 seconds | Workflow step duration |
| **F-007** | Page Object method calls: No measurable overhead | N/A | Performance profiling |

#### 2.3.5.3 Security Requirements and Compliance

**Authentication and Authorization (F-002-RQ-006, F-003-RQ-006):**
- MCP servers require JWT token authentication; tokens NEVER committed to repository
- GitHub Actions secrets used for `FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN`, `LLM_API_KEY` (F-005-RQ-006)
- Token rotation strategy documented for production-like environments

**Data Protection (F-002-RQ-002, F-004-RQ-005):**
- Test data must NOT contain production PII; use synthetic data via Faker library
- LLM prompts must NOT expose sensitive application details, credentials, or business logic
- Allure reports published to GitHub Pages must NOT contain sensitive data (F-006-RQ-007)

**Dependency Security (All Features):**
- All dependencies pinned to specific versions in requirements files (Section 0.3)
- Regular security scanning via GitHub Dependabot for vulnerability detection
- Pre-commit hooks include security linting via ruff (F-007-RQ-006)

**Browser Security (F-001, F-003, F-007):**
- Playwright browser contexts run in isolated sandboxes (F-007-RQ-004)
- Headless mode in CI prevents UI-based attacks (F-005-RQ-001, `HEADLESS=true`)
- No browser extensions or plugins loaded to minimize attack surface

#### 2.3.5.4 Maintenance and Operational Requirements

**Dependency Update Strategy:**
- Quarterly review and update of all Python packages documented in Section 0.3
- Playwright browser binaries automatically updated via `playwright install` (F-001-RQ-001)
- Pre-commit hook updates managed via `pre-commit autoupdate` (F-007-RQ-006)

**Test Maintenance Burden Reduction:**
- Page Objects isolate UI changes; update locators in one place when UI changes (F-007-RQ-001)
- Stable locator strategies (F-007-RQ-002) reduce test maintenance by 40-60%
- Gherkin scenarios reviewed quarterly for business logic accuracy (F-001-RQ-002)

**Infrastructure Maintenance:**
- GitHub Actions workflow updated when runner images change (F-005-RQ-001)
- Allure report history pruned monthly to prevent storage bloat (F-006-RQ-007)
- LLM model updates evaluated quarterly for improved generation quality (F-004-RQ-001)

**Documentation Maintenance:**
- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) updated when patterns change (F-007-RQ-007)
- README.md updated with new setup instructions when dependencies change
- This Technical Specification updated when feature scope or requirements evolve

### 2.3.6 Requirements Validation and Acceptance

This section defines the validation framework and acceptance criteria that determine when each functional requirement is considered complete and production-ready.

#### 2.3.6.1 Definition of Done

A functional requirement is considered "Done" when all of the following criteria are satisfied:

**Implementation Completeness:**
1. Code implementation complete per requirement specification
2. All acceptance criteria met with objective verification
3. Unit tests written with minimum 80% code coverage (Section 2.1.2.4)
4. Integration tests demonstrate end-to-end functionality

**Quality Assurance:**
1. Code passes all pre-commit hooks (ruff linting, mypy type checking) per F-007-RQ-006
2. Tests pass consistently in CI with >95% success rate (Section 0.7.10)
3. No flaky tests; all tests deterministic and parallel-friendly (F-001-RQ-005, F-007-RQ-004)
4. Allure reports show clear pass/fail with actionable failure diagnostics (F-006-RQ-003)

**Documentation:**
1. Implementation documented in Technical Specification Section 0.5
2. Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) created for significant patterns (F-007-RQ-007)
3. README.md updated with usage examples if requirement adds user-facing functionality
4. Inline code comments for complex logic following Python docstring conventions

**Traceability:**
1. Requirement linked to originating source in Agent Action Plan Section 0.1.3
2. Test cases reference requirement ID in test names or docstrings
3. Allure reports tag tests with feature ID and requirement ID (F-006-RQ-002)
4. Requirements Traceability Matrix updated (Section 2.3.4)

#### 2.3.6.2 Acceptance Testing Framework

| Validation Type | Method | Tool/Process | Success Criteria |
|-----------------|--------|--------------|------------------|
| **Functional Validation** | Execute acceptance criteria Given/When/Then | pytest with scenarios | All acceptance criteria pass |
| **Performance Validation** | Measure response times, throughput | Allure duration reports, MCP logs | Metrics within thresholds (Section 2.3.5.2) |
| **Security Validation** | Token validation, secret scanning | GitHub secret scanning, pre-commit hooks | No secrets in commits, authentication required |
| **Usability Validation** | Product manager review of Gherkin | Human review workflow (F-004-RQ-005) | Non-technical stakeholder understands scenarios |
| **Integration Validation** | Cross-feature testing | Integration test suites | All integration points function correctly |
| **Regression Validation** | Full test suite execution | CI/CD pipeline (F-005) | No regressions; all existing tests pass |

#### 2.3.6.3 Success Criteria from Agent Action Plan

The following success criteria from Section 0.7.10 define project-level completion:

1. **Framework Setup (F-001)**: Developer clones repo, runs `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`, executes `pytest` successfully within 10 minutes
2. **Test Authoring (F-001, F-007)**: Developer writes new Gherkin scenario and implements steps using Page Objects in < 30 minutes
3. **CI/CD Integration (F-005, F-006)**: Tests run automatically in GitHub Actions, generate Allure report, complete in < 15 minutes
4. **MCP Integration (F-002, F-003)**: Tests use MCP server for data/state; no hardcoded test data exists in repository
5. **LLM Generation (F-004)**: Developer uses LLM to generate draft scenarios, reviews, and commits approved versions
6. **Test Stability (F-001, F-007)**: Tests pass consistently (>95% success rate) in CI without flakiness
7. **Reporting Quality (F-006)**: Test failures include screenshot, trace, clear error message for rapid debugging
8. **Documentation Completeness**: New team member gets started using only README.md and docs/ directory

**Failure Criteria (Must Avoid):**
- ❌ Tests fail randomly in CI (flakiness indicates shared state or timing issues)
- ❌ Hardcoded test data found in test files (violates F-002 MCP integration)
- ❌ LLM executes tests autonomously without human approval (violates Section 0.7.1)
- ❌ Page Objects use brittle CSS/XPath selectors (violates F-007-RQ-002)
- ❌ Gherkin scenarios contain implementation details (violates F-007-RQ-003)
- ❌ Tests cannot run in parallel (violates F-001-RQ-005, F-007-RQ-004)
- ❌ MCP servers contain test execution logic (violates Section 0.7.1 separation of concerns)

#### Detailed Dependency Analysis

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001: Unified Test Automation Framework (Foundational Feature)</span>**
- **Prerequisite Features**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">None (foundational feature)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Dependent Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-002, F-003, F-005, F-006 (all integration and infrastructure features depend on this foundation)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Provides core pytest-based testing infrastructure with Playwright, httpx, and pytest-bdd integration. All other features extend or integrate with this base framework.</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest.ini configuration, conftest.py fixture definitions, features/ directory structure, step_definitions/ modules</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-002: FastAPI MCP (Deterministic)</span>**
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Prerequisite Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (requires pytest fixtures and test execution context)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Dependent Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-005 (CI/CD pipeline requires MCP server for deterministic test data)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP client fixture (defined in conftest.py) integrates with F-001's fixture system. Tests invoke MCP tools for data seeding, eliminating hardcoded test data.</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">mcp_client fixture in conftest.py, httpx client for JSON-RPC communication, JWT token authentication (FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN environment variable)</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-003: Playwright MCP (Exploration)</span>**
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Prerequisite Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (leverages Playwright browser automation infrastructure)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Dependent Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-004 (LLM agents use Playwright MCP for exploration sessions that generate Gherkin scenarios)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Provides browser automation tools (navigate, click, type, screenshot, get_page_structure) accessible to LLM agents for exploratory testing and test scenario discovery.</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright browser contexts from F-001, WebSocket connections for streaming interactions, Gherkin generation endpoints</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-004: LLM-Assisted Test Authoring</span>**
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Prerequisite Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (generates .feature files for pytest-bdd), F-003 (uses exploration sessions as input for scenario generation)</span>
- **Dependent Features**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">None (terminal feature in dependency chain)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Analyzes exploration sessions from F-003 to generate Gherkin scenarios, edge case suggestions, and test variations. Supports dual LLM providers (Ollama local, OpenAI-compatible hosted).</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP session history, LLM API clients (Ollama/OpenAI), human review workflow, YAML frontmatter for metadata tracking</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-005: GitHub Actions CI/CD Integration</span>**
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Prerequisite Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (executes pytest test suite), F-002 (starts FastAPI MCP server for deterministic data management)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Dependent Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-006 (CI/CD workflow generates and publishes Allure reports)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Orchestrates complete test pipeline: MCP server startup (F-002), pytest execution with parallel workers (F-001), Allure report generation (F-006). Ensures consistent, reproducible test execution in CI.</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">.github/workflows/test.yml workflow definition, GitHub Actions secrets (FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN), matrix strategy for browser/Python version combinations, artifact upload for reports</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-006: Allure Reporting & Observability</span>**
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Prerequisite Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (pytest-allure integration captures test execution data), F-005 (CI/CD workflow publishes reports to GitHub Pages)</span>
- **Dependent Features**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">None (terminal feature in dependency chain)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Captures test execution metadata, screenshots, traces, and HTTP logs during pytest execution (F-001). CI/CD workflow (F-005) generates HTML reports and publishes to GitHub Pages for stakeholder visibility.</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest.ini Allure configuration, conftest.py hooks for artifact capture, allure-results/ directory, GitHub Pages publishing step in workflow</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-007: Maintainable Test Architecture & Best Practices</span>**
- **Prerequisite Features**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">None (establishes architectural patterns)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Dependent Features</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (framework consumes Page Objects, stable locators, and isolation patterns)</span>
- **Rationale**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Defines and enforces architectural patterns (Page Object Model, stable locator strategies, business-readable Gherkin, test isolation) that F-001 implements and all tests follow.</span>
- **Integration Requirements**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pages/ directory with Page Object classes, pre-commit hooks (ruff, mypy), Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), browser_context fixture with function scope</span>

| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**F-005 ↔ F-006**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Report generation and publishing in workflow</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Workflow → Allure generate command → GitHub Pages deployment</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">allure-results/ directory, allure-report/ artifact, GitHub Pages configuration</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">.github/workflows/test.yml (report generation step)</span> |

### 2.4.4 Dependency Chains and Critical Paths

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Understanding dependency chains is critical for implementation planning, impact analysis, and troubleshooting. The following chains represent sequential dependencies that must be satisfied.</span>

#### Primary Dependency Chains

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Chain 1: Core Testing to CI/CD Reporting</span>**
```
<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-007 (Architecture) → F-001 (Framework) → F-002 (MCP Data) → F-005 (CI/CD) → F-006 (Reporting)</span>
```
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Critical Path</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This represents the minimum viable pipeline for automated testing with reporting</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Implementation Order</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Must implement F-007 patterns first, then F-001 framework, then F-002 for data management, followed by F-005 CI/CD orchestration, and finally F-006 reporting</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Failure Impact</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">If any feature in this chain fails, the entire CI/CD pipeline is non-functional</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Chain 2: LLM-Assisted Test Generation</span>**
```
<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (Framework) → F-003 (Playwright MCP) → F-004 (LLM Authoring) → F-001 (Generated .feature files)</span>
```
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Critical Path</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This chain enables AI-assisted test scenario discovery and generation</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Implementation Order</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 must be operational, then F-003 provides browser automation for LLM exploration, then F-004 generates scenarios that feed back into F-001</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Failure Impact</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">If F-003 or F-004 fail, manual test authoring is still possible; this chain is optional for core testing capabilities</span>

#### Parallel Dependencies

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The following features can be implemented in parallel after their prerequisites are satisfied:</span>

- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">After F-001 is complete</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-002, F-003, and F-006 can be developed in parallel</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">After F-001 + F-002 are complete</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-005 can be implemented</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">After F-001 + F-003 are complete</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-004 can be implemented</span>

### 2.4.5 Cross-Cutting Concerns and Common Services

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Several services and utilities are shared across multiple features, providing cross-cutting functionality.</span>

#### Logging and Observability

- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">loguru Logger</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Centralized structured logging used by all features (F-001 through F-007) for consistent log formatting, rotation, and filtering</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Custom Allure Steps</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP tool invocations (F-002 seed_user, build_payload, reset_env; F-003 navigate, click, type) wrapped in @allure.step decorators for visibility in F-006 reports</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Pytest Fixtures</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Shared test setup/teardown mechanisms across all features, defined in conftest.py (F-001), including browser_context, api_client, mcp_client fixtures</span>

#### Data Management

- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP State Management</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Centralized by F-002 FastAPI MCP server, consumed by all test features (F-001, F-007) to eliminate hardcoded test data and ensure deterministic test execution</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test Data Generators</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Faker library integration used by F-002 (seed_user for synthetic user data) and F-007 (test data patterns in Page Objects)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment Reset</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-002 reset_env tool ensures clean state between test runs, critical for parallel execution (F-001, F-007) and CI/CD reliability (F-005)</span>

#### Code Quality and Enforcement

- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Pre-commit Hooks</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Enforce F-007 maintainability standards (ruff linting, mypy type checking, locator strategy validation) across all Python code in F-001 through F-007</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Type Checking</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">mypy strict mode configuration applies to F-001 (test code), F-002/F-003 (MCP servers with FastAPI), F-004 (LLM client abstractions), F-007 (Page Objects with type hints)</span>
- **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Linting Rules</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">ruff configuration enforces consistent code style, security best practices, and import sorting across all features</span>
