## 2.5 Implementation Considerations Framework

**Status: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Initial Constraints Defined per Agent Action Plan v0.1</span>**

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This section documents critical technical constraints, performance requirements, scalability considerations, security implications, and maintenance requirements derived from the Agent Action Plan Special Instructions (Section 0.7) and Dependency Inventory (Section 0.3). All implementation considerations are traceable to source requirements and enforce architectural patterns essential for test framework stability, maintainability, and reliability.</span>

### 2.5.1 Technical Constraints by Feature

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Technical constraints represent non-negotiable architectural requirements that ensure framework integrity, test isolation, and long-term maintainability. These constraints are derived from Agent Action Plan Section 0.7 (Special Instructions) and must be enforced through automated validation where possible.</span>

#### 2.5.1.1 F-001: Unified Test Automation Framework Constraints

**Platform and Runtime Constraints**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Python Version** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Python 3.9+ minimum, 3.11+ recommended</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright 1.55.0 dropped Python 3.8 support; Python 3.11+ provides enhanced type hints and performance improvements</span> | CI matrix tests Python 3.9, 3.11, 3.12 |
| **Test Runner** | pytest 8.4.2 exclusively | MCP servers are supporting services, NOT test runners (Section 0.7.1) | Pre-commit hook validates no test execution logic in MCP servers |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Configuration Management**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment variables only, no hardcoded values</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Configuration via BASE_URL, API_BASE_URL, HEADLESS, MCP endpoints (Section 0.7.9)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Linting rule detects hardcoded URLs/credentials</span> |
| **Fixture Scope** | Function scope for browser_context, session scope for browser launch only | Test isolation for parallel execution without shared state (Section 0.7.4) | Integration tests verify context isolation |

**Architectural Constraints**

- **Separation of Concerns**: pytest executes tests; MCP servers provide data/state only (Section 0.7.1)
- **No Shared Mutable State**: Tests cannot depend on execution order or previous test side effects (Section 0.7.4)
- **Plugin Compatibility**: Must support pytest-bdd 8.1.0, pytest-playwright 0.6.2, pytest-xdist 3.6.1 simultaneously
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Browser Context Isolation**: Each test receives fresh browser context with isolated cookies, storage, and cache (Section 0.7.4)</span>

#### 2.5.1.2 F-002: FastAPI MCP (Deterministic) Constraints

**Data Management Constraints**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **No Hardcoded Test Data** | All test data via MCP seed_user, build_payload tools | Zero hardcoded emails, passwords, or API request bodies in test files (Section 0.7.3) | Pre-commit grep search for common test data patterns |
| **Environment Reset** | reset_env tool restores baseline state < 5 seconds | Tests execute from known-good state; no database pollution between runs | Performance tests validate reset duration |
| **Authentication** | JWT token authentication required for all MCP endpoints | Prevent unauthorized tool invocation; tokens from environment variables only | Security tests verify 401 on invalid tokens |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**CI Environment Behavior**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP always enabled in CI; required for all test runs</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic data management mandatory for reproducible CI test results (Section 0.7.5)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">GitHub Actions workflow validates MCP health check before pytest execution</span> |

**State Management Constraints**

- **Idempotency**: Multiple invocations of seed_user with same parameters must be idempotent or explicitly versioned
- **Concurrent Access**: Support 20+ concurrent connections from pytest-xdist workers without race conditions
- **Template Validation**: All build_payload templates validated via Pydantic schemas before use
- **Audit Trail**: All MCP tool invocations logged with timestamps, parameters, and results for debugging

#### 2.5.1.3 F-003: Playwright MCP (Exploration) Constraints

**Development-Only Constraint**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Environment Restriction**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Development-only; disabled in CI by default unless PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED=true</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP used for exploration and test generation, not required for test execution (Section 0.7.5)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">GitHub Actions workflow excludes Playwright MCP startup; tests must not fail if unavailable</span> |
| **Session Isolation** | Each LLM agent receives isolated browser context | Concurrent explorations must not interfere with each other | Integration tests verify multi-session concurrency |
| **Generated Content Review** | All .feature files tagged pending_review; human approval required | LLM is helper for discovery, not autonomous test creator (Section 0.7.8) | Pre-commit hook warns on pending_review files in commits |

**Browser Control Constraints**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Stable Locator Priority**: Tools prioritize role-based selectors (get_by_role, get_by_label, get_by_test_id); prohibit CSS classes and XPath (Section 0.7.2)</span>
- **Timeout Management**: All browser interactions (navigate, click, type) include configurable timeouts (default 5s for page load, 500ms for interactions)
- **Error Handling**: Browser errors (404, 500, timeouts) returned as structured responses, never thrown exceptions
- **Resource Cleanup**: Browser contexts closed after exploration session completion; no resource leaks

#### 2.5.1.4 F-004: LLM-Assisted Test Authoring Constraints

**LLM Provider Constraints**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Provider Abstraction** | Support Ollama (local) and OpenAI-compatible APIs via environment variable LLM_PROVIDER | Enable cost-free local development with Ollama; production flexibility with hosted models | Integration tests verify both provider types |
| **Human Review Workflow** | Generated scenarios include metadata (timestamp, model, status: pending_review) | LLM is helper for generation, NOT test runner or decision maker (Section 0.7.1) | YAML frontmatter required in all generated .feature files |
| **Token Management** | Token counting via tiktoken before API calls; budget alerts at 80% threshold | Control API costs for hosted LLM usage | Usage monitoring dashboard tracks token consumption |

**Content Quality Constraints**

- **Business Readability**: Generated Gherkin must be high-level, business-focused; no UI implementation details (Section 0.7.2)
- **Assumptions Documentation**: All generated scenarios include LLM assumptions and open questions sections (Section 0.7.8)
- **Validation**: Generated .feature files must pass pytest-bdd Gherkin parser before saving
- **No Autonomous Execution**: LLM never executes tests directly; only generates scenarios for human review

#### 2.5.1.5 F-005: GitHub Actions CI/CD Constraints

**CI Environment Constraints**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **MCP Server Availability** | FastAPI MCP must pass health check before pytest execution begins | Tests depend on deterministic data management; failure = workflow abort | Workflow step validates /health endpoint returns 200 OK |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Playwright MCP Exclusion**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP NOT started in CI unless explicitly enabled via workflow flag</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Exploration server is development tool, not CI requirement (Section 0.7.5)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Workflow YAML review confirms no Playwright MCP startup step</span> |
| **Secrets Management** | All credentials via GitHub Actions secrets; never committed to repository | Prevent credential exposure in logs, commits, or artifacts | Pre-commit hook scans for common secret patterns |
| **Execution Timeout** | Workflow must complete within 15 minutes for rapid feedback | Balance comprehensive testing with developer productivity | Workflow timeout configured at 15 minutes |

**Parallelization Constraints**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Matrix Execution**: Tests run across 3 browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) with 4 parallel workers per browser (pytest-xdist)</span>
- **Resource Limits**: GitHub Actions runners provide 2 CPU cores; pytest-xdist configured for 4 workers to maximize concurrency
- **Browser Context Isolation**: Each worker receives isolated browser contexts; no shared state across workers (Section 0.7.4)
- **Cache Optimization**: Python dependencies and Playwright browsers cached across runs to reduce setup time

#### 2.5.1.6 F-006: Allure Reporting Constraints

**Report Quality Constraints**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Actionable Failures** | Test failures must include screenshot, browser trace, and clear error message | Enable rapid debugging without local reproduction (Section 0.7.6) | Spot checks on failure reports verify artifact presence |
| **Data Sanitization** | Reports must NOT contain production PII, credentials, or sensitive business data | GitHub Pages reports are public; prevent data exposure | Pre-publish script validates no sensitive data patterns |
| **Historical Retention** | 30-day report history for trend analysis; older data pruned to prevent storage bloat | Balance historical trends with GitHub Pages 1GB storage limit | Monthly cleanup job prunes allure-history/ directory |

**Performance Constraints**

- **Generation Speed**: Report generation completes < 30 seconds for 1000 test results
- **Page Load**: Initial report page load < 5 seconds; navigation < 1 second
- **Artifact Lazy Loading**: Screenshots and traces load on-demand, not upfront page load
- **File Size**: Individual report artifacts capped at 10MB; compressed for transfer

#### 2.5.1.7 F-007: Maintainable Test Architecture Constraints

**Locator Strategy Constraints**

| Constraint Type | Specification | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------------|---------------|-----------|-------------------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Prohibited Selectors**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">CSS class-based selectors and XPath expressions explicitly forbidden in Page Objects</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Brittle selectors cause test failures on UI refactoring; stable selectors survive changes (Section 0.7.2)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Pre-commit ruff rule detects .locator() calls with CSS/XPath patterns</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Locator Priority Order**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">1. ARIA roles/labels (get_by_role, get_by_label), 2. data-testid, 3. Semantic text, 4. Avoid CSS/XPath entirely</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Accessibility-first locators are most stable and semantically meaningful (Section 0.7.2)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Code review checklist verifies locator strategy compliance</span> |
| **Page Object Typing** | All Page Object methods use type hints; mypy strict mode enabled | Catch interface errors at development time, not runtime | mypy pre-commit hook enforces type checking |

**Test Isolation Constraints**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Fresh Browser Context**: browser_context fixture uses function scope; new context per test for isolation (Section 0.7.4)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No Session Scope**: Session-scoped browser fixtures prohibited; causes shared state and flakiness</span>
- **Deterministic Execution**: Tests pass regardless of execution order; no dependencies between tests
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Parallel Compatibility**: All tests compatible with pytest-xdist -n auto for maximum parallelization</span>

**Gherkin Quality Constraints**

- **Business-Level Steps**: Gherkin steps describe WHAT (user actions, outcomes), not HOW (clicks, selectors) (Section 0.7.2)
- **Step Length**: Step definitions limited to 1-5 lines; delegate to Page Objects or API clients (Section 0.7.6)
- **Scenario Length**: Scenarios limited to 3-7 steps maximum for readability (Section 0.7.2)
- **No Implementation Details**: CSS selectors, XPath, HTTP status codes, coordinates forbidden in Gherkin

### 2.5.2 Performance Requirements by Feature

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Performance requirements are derived from Agent Action Plan dependency specifications (Section 0.3) and operational constraints. These thresholds ensure responsive test execution, rapid CI feedback, and optimal resource utilization across parallel test workers.</span>

#### 2.5.2.1 F-001: Framework Performance Boundaries

**Test Discovery and Initialization**

| Operation | Performance Target | Measurement Method | Constraint Source |
|-----------|-------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Feature file discovery | < 2 seconds for 100 .feature files | pytest --collect-only execution time | pytest-bdd 8.1.0 parser performance |
| Fixture initialization | < 500ms per fixture (browser_context, api_client, mcp_client) | Allure step timing for fixture setup | Fixture overhead must be negligible |
| Browser context creation | < 300ms per context | Playwright trace timing | Playwright 1.55.0 context initialization |

**Parallel Execution Performance**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Parallel Speedup**: Linear scaling up to 4 workers (pytest-xdist 3.6.1 capability)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Worker Isolation**: No performance degradation from cross-worker interference; isolated Playwright contexts prevent contention</span>
- **Test Throughput**: 100 tests complete < 10 minutes with 4 workers (vs. 30-40 minutes sequential)
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Context Overhead**: Function-scoped browser_context adds < 500ms per test vs. session scope (acceptable for isolation guarantee)</span>

#### 2.5.2.2 F-002: MCP Server Performance Boundaries

**Tool Invocation Latency**

| MCP Tool | Performance Target | Rationale | Validation Method |
|----------|-------------------|-----------|-------------------|
| seed_user | < 200ms per user creation | Frequent operation in test setup; must not bottleneck test execution | MCP server logs track p50/p95/p99 latency |
| build_payload | < 50ms per payload construction | Template substitution is CPU-bound; should be near-instantaneous | Performance profiling of Pydantic validation |
| reset_env | < 5000ms complete environment reset | Infrequent operation (between test suites); acceptable latency for state cleanup | Integration tests measure reset duration |
| query_state | < 100ms per state query | Debugging/validation operation; low-frequency use case | API endpoint timing in Allure reports |

**Concurrency Performance**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Concurrent Request Handling**: Support 20+ concurrent connections from pytest-xdist workers without degradation</span>
- **Request Throughput**: 50+ requests/second sustained for parallel test execution
- **Connection Pooling**: httpx AsyncClient connection pooling minimizes overhead for repeated MCP calls
- **Database Contention**: SQLAlchemy 2.0.38 async ORM prevents database lock contention across workers

#### 2.5.2.3 F-003: Playwright MCP Performance Boundaries

**Browser Control Latency**

| Operation | Performance Target | Rationale | Validation Method |
|-----------|-------------------|-----------|-------------------|
| navigate | < 5000ms page load (configurable timeout) | Page load time varies by application; timeout prevents hanging | Playwright navigation timing API |
| click | < 500ms element interaction | UI interactions should be near-instantaneous for responsive feel | Playwright actionability checks + click timing |
| type | < 300ms per form field | Text input is frequent operation; must not slow exploration | Character-by-character typing with optional delay |
| screenshot | < 1000ms full-page screenshot capture | Visual capture for LLM context; acceptable latency for quality | Playwright screenshot API timing |
| get_page_structure | < 2000ms complete DOM analysis | Semantic extraction is compute-intensive; acceptable for exploration use case | DOM traversal and parsing profiling |

**Session Management Performance**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Context Creation**: < 400ms per isolated browser context for LLM agent session</span>
- **Concurrent Sessions**: Support 5+ concurrent LLM agent explorations without resource exhaustion
- **WebSocket Latency**: < 100ms round-trip for streaming interactions via websockets 14.1
- **Gherkin Generation**: < 5 seconds to convert exploration session to .feature file with business-readable steps

#### 2.5.2.4 F-004: LLM Generation Performance Boundaries

**LLM Invocation Latency**

| LLM Operation | Local (Ollama) Target | Hosted (OpenAI) Target | Constraint Source |
|---------------|----------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| generate_gherkin | < 5 seconds per scenario | < 10 seconds per scenario | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Ollama 0.4.8 local inference; hosted API includes network latency</span> |
| suggest_edge_cases | < 3 seconds per analysis | < 5 seconds per analysis | Edge case taxonomy lookup + LLM suggestion generation |
| generate_variations | < 5 seconds per variation set | < 10 seconds per variation set | Parameterization logic + scenario templating |
| estimate_tokens | < 100ms token calculation | N/A (pre-API call estimate) | tiktoken 0.9.0 local tokenization performance |

**Resource Management**

- **Token Budget Monitoring**: Alert at 80% of configured monthly token budget to prevent cost overruns
- **Context Window Management**: Ensure prompts stay within model limits (e.g., 4096 tokens for smaller models)
- **Caching**: Cache LLM responses for identical prompts to reduce redundant API calls
- **Batch Processing**: Batch multiple scenario generation requests when possible to reduce API overhead

#### 2.5.2.5 F-005: CI/CD Pipeline Performance Boundaries

**Workflow Stage Timing**

| Pipeline Stage | Performance Target | Rationale | Optimization Strategy |
|----------------|-------------------|-----------|----------------------|
| Environment setup | < 2 minutes (Python install + dependencies) | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Cached dependencies (pip cache) and browser binaries reduce redundant downloads</span> | actions/cache for pip and Playwright browsers |
| MCP server startup | < 30 seconds to health check ready | FastAPI MCP must be available before pytest execution | Health check polling with retry logic |
| Test execution | < 10 minutes for 100 tests with 4 workers | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest-xdist 3.6.1 parallelization provides 3-4x speedup over sequential execution</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Maximize worker count within GitHub Actions runner CPU limits (2 cores)</span> |
| Report generation | < 2 minutes for Allure HTML report | Report generation should not dominate overall workflow time | Allure CLI optimizations for large result sets |
| Artifact upload | < 1 minute for report ZIP upload | GitHub Actions artifact storage upload speed | Compress artifacts before upload |

**Overall Pipeline Performance**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Total Execution Time**: Complete workflow (setup → test → report) < 15 minutes for rapid feedback</span>
- **Matrix Parallelization**: 3 browser jobs (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) run concurrently; total time = longest browser job, not sum
- **Failure Fast**: Detect and report test failures immediately; don't wait for all tests to complete
- **Cache Hit Rate**: Target > 90% cache hit rate for dependencies and browsers to minimize setup time

#### 2.5.2.6 F-006: Allure Reporting Performance Boundaries

**Report Generation Performance**

| Report Operation | Performance Target | Rationale | Validation Method |
|------------------|-------------------|-----------|-------------------|
| Report generation | < 30 seconds for 1000 test results | Report generation in CI should not dominate workflow time | Allure CLI execution time in workflow logs |
| Historical trend calculation | < 10 seconds for 30-day history | Trend analysis adds value; acceptable latency for historical context | Allure history processing timing |
| Report page load | < 5 seconds initial load, < 1 second navigation | Interactive reports require responsive UI for usability | Browser DevTools Network timing |
| Artifact lazy loading | < 2 seconds per screenshot/trace file | On-demand loading prevents upfront page load bloat | Allure viewer fetch timing |

**Storage and Transfer Performance**

- **Artifact Compression**: Screenshots compressed to WebP format for 30-50% size reduction vs. PNG
- **Incremental History**: Only new test results added to history; full history not regenerated each run
- **GitHub Pages Deploy**: < 2 minutes to publish report to GitHub Pages after generation
- **Artifact Retention**: Prune reports older than 30 days automatically to prevent storage bloat

#### 2.5.2.7 F-007: Architecture Pattern Performance Impact

**Page Object Overhead**

| Pattern | Performance Impact | Mitigation | Validation |
|---------|-------------------|------------|------------|
| Page Object method calls | < 10ms overhead vs. direct Playwright API | Thin wrapper methods with minimal logic | Performance profiling shows negligible impact |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Stable locator resolution (role/label)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">< 100ms for ARIA role-based selectors</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright optimizes get_by_role with native browser queries</span> | Locator resolution timing in Playwright traces |
| Type checking (mypy) | < 10 seconds for entire codebase | Incremental type checking on changed files only | mypy execution time in pre-commit hook |

**Test Isolation Overhead**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Function-Scoped Context**: +500ms per test vs. session-scoped context (acceptable for isolation guarantee)</span>
- **Fixture Teardown**: Context cleanup adds < 200ms per test; prevents resource leaks
- **Parallel Execution Benefit**: Isolation enables pytest-xdist parallelization; 3-4x speedup outweighs per-test overhead
- **No Shared State**: Eliminates flaky tests from race conditions; debugging time savings >> execution time cost

### 2.5.3 Scalability Considerations by Feature

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Scalability considerations define the framework's growth capacity across test suite size, data volume, concurrent users, and infrastructure demands. These projections guide resource planning and identify scaling limits requiring architectural evolution.</span>

#### 2.5.3.1 Test Suite Growth Scalability

**Vertical Scalability (Single Repository)**

| Growth Dimension | Current Target | 12-Month Projection | Scaling Strategy |
|------------------|---------------|---------------------|------------------|
| **Feature Files** | 50-100 .feature files | 300-500 .feature files | pytest-bdd discovery optimizations; potential split into feature modules |
| **Test Scenarios** | 200-300 scenarios | 800-1200 scenarios | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest-xdist parallelization scales linearly up to CPU core count; cloud runners enable 8+ workers</span> |
| **Page Objects** | 20-30 page classes | 100-150 page classes | Page Object inheritance hierarchy reduces duplication; base patterns shared |
| **MCP Payload Templates** | 10-20 templates | 50-100 templates | Template organization by feature area; lazy loading of templates |

**Horizontal Scalability (Multi-Repository)**

- **Shared Test Libraries**: Extract common Page Objects, fixtures, and utilities into shared Python package
- **Feature-Specific Repositories**: Split test suites by product feature area if monorepo exceeds 1000 scenarios
- **Distributed Execution**: Pytest-xdist supports distributed execution across multiple machines for massive test suites
- **Selective Execution**: Tag-based test selection enables running only relevant tests per code change

#### 2.5.3.2 Data Volume Scalability

**MCP Server Data Handling**

| Data Type | Current Capacity | Scaling Limit | Mitigation Strategy |
|-----------|-----------------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Test Users (seed_user)** | 100 users per test run | 10,000 users | Database indexing on user lookup fields; connection pooling |
| **Payload Templates** | 10MB total template library | 100MB template library | Template caching; lazy loading; compression |
| **Environment State** | 1GB database snapshot for reset_env | 10GB database snapshot | Incremental state reset; partition data by feature area |
| **Query Results** | 1000 records per query_state call | 100,000 records with pagination | Implement pagination API; cursor-based result streaming |

**Allure Report Data Volume**

- **Test Results**: Current 200 tests/run → Target 2000 tests/run; Allure handles 10,000+ results efficiently
- **Artifacts**: Current 50MB artifacts/run → Target 500MB/run; lazy loading prevents browser memory issues
- **Historical Data**: 30-day retention at 500MB/day = 15GB total; prune older data or migrate to archival storage
- **GitHub Pages Limit**: 1GB storage cap; implement artifact compression and selective retention (failures only)

#### 2.5.3.3 Concurrent User Scalability

**Development Team Growth**

| User Type | Current Scale | 12-Month Projection | Infrastructure Impact |
|-----------|--------------|---------------------|----------------------|
| **Local Developers** | 5-10 developers | 20-50 developers | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local Ollama for LLM (no API costs); local MCP servers (no shared resources)</span> |
| **CI Concurrent Jobs** | 3 browser matrix jobs | 9 jobs (3 browsers × 3 Python versions) | GitHub Actions concurrent job limits; consider self-hosted runners |
| **LLM Agent Sessions** | 1-2 concurrent explorations | 10-20 concurrent explorations | Playwright MCP server resource limits; consider containerized scaling |

**MCP Server Concurrent Load**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Pytest-xdist Workers**: Current 4 workers → Target 16 workers (8-core CI runners); MCP server must handle 16+ concurrent connections</span>
- **FastAPI Concurrency**: uvicorn 0.34.0 async workers scale to hundreds of concurrent requests; no bottleneck expected
- **Database Connections**: SQLAlchemy 2.0.38 connection pooling; pool size = worker count + buffer
- **WebSocket Connections**: Playwright MCP websockets 14.1 supports 100+ concurrent connections per server

#### 2.5.3.4 Infrastructure Scalability

**CI/CD Scalability**

| Infrastructure Component | Current Setup | Scaling Strategy | Cost Consideration |
|-------------------------|--------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **GitHub Actions Runners** | GitHub-hosted (2 CPU cores) | Self-hosted runners (8+ CPU cores) for large test suites | Self-hosted runners reduce cost at scale |
| **Browser Binary Storage** | Cached in GitHub Actions (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit = 500MB) | Shared cache across workflow runs; pre-bake into custom runner images | Cache hit rate > 90% target |
| **Allure Report Hosting** | GitHub Pages (1GB limit) | Migrate to S3/CloudFront for unlimited storage and CDN performance | GitHub Pages free; S3 incurs storage costs |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**MCP Server Hosting**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local (dev) + GitHub Actions service (CI)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Containerized deployment (Docker) for consistent environments; Kubernetes for multi-tenant scaling</span> | Container orchestration adds operational complexity |

**Database Scalability (Optional SQLAlchemy Integration)**

- **Connection Pooling**: Pool size scales with pytest-xdist worker count (e.g., 16 workers = 20 connection pool size)
- **Read Replicas**: Separate read-only replicas for query_state operations to reduce load on primary database
- **Sharding Strategy**: Partition test data by feature area if single database exceeds capacity
- **In-Memory Databases**: SQLite in-memory mode for fast reset_env operations (trade persistence for speed)

### 2.5.4 Security Implications by Feature

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Security implications address authentication, authorization, data protection, credential management, and threat mitigation requirements. All security controls are derived from Agent Action Plan Section 0.7 constraints and industry best practices for test framework security.</span>

#### 2.5.4.1 Authentication and Authorization

**MCP Server Authentication**

| Security Control | Implementation | Threat Mitigated | Validation Method |
|-----------------|----------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **JWT Token Authentication** | python-jose 3.3.0 for token signing/verification (F-002, F-003) | Unauthorized access to test data seeding and environment manipulation | Security tests verify 401 Unauthorized on invalid/missing tokens |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Token Storage**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment variables only (FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN); GitHub Actions secrets in CI</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Token exposure in version control or logs</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Pre-commit hook scans for hardcoded tokens; GitHub secret scanning enabled</span> |
| **Token Rotation** | Manual rotation via environment variable update; automated rotation for production environments | Long-lived token compromise | Document token rotation procedures in ops runbook |
| **Scope Limitation** | Tokens scoped to test environment only; no production data access | Lateral movement to production systems | Network segmentation between test and production environments |

**LLM API Key Management**

- **API Key Storage**: LLM_API_KEY in environment variables; never committed to repository (Section 0.7.9)
- **Provider Isolation**: Ollama local provider requires no API key; OpenAI-compatible providers use per-developer keys
- **Cost Controls**: Token budget monitoring alerts at 80% threshold; rate limiting prevents runaway API costs
- **Key Revocation**: Document API key revocation procedures for compromised keys

#### 2.5.4.2 Data Protection

**Test Data Security**

| Data Type | Protection Mechanism | Rationale | Validation Method |
|-----------|---------------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Test User Credentials** | Synthetic data only via Faker; no production credentials | Prevent production account compromise from test data exposure | Grep scan for common production email domains (e.g., @company.com) |
| **API Request Payloads** | Template-based generation via build_payload; no real customer data | Protect PII and sensitive business data from test artifacts | Pydantic validation ensures test data schema compliance |
| **Database Snapshots** | Anonymized baseline snapshots for reset_env; no production data | Compliance with GDPR, CCPA data protection regulations | Data masking scripts for snapshot creation |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Allure Reports**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Sanitize screenshots and logs before attachment; no sensitive data in public GitHub Pages reports</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Public report hosting exposes test artifacts; prevent data leaks</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Pre-publish script validates no PII patterns (emails, SSNs, credit cards)</span> |

**Credential Management**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No Hardcoded Secrets**: Linting rules detect hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens in code (Section 0.7.9)</span>
- **Password Hashing**: passlib 1.7.4 for password hashing in MCP seed_user operations (bcrypt algorithm)
- **.env File Security**: .env file in .gitignore; never committed; template .env.example with placeholder values
- **CI Secret Masking**: GitHub Actions automatically masks secrets in workflow logs

#### 2.5.4.3 Browser Security

**Playwright Browser Isolation**

| Security Control | Implementation | Threat Mitigated | Validation Method |
|-----------------|----------------|------------------|-------------------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Context Sandboxing**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Fresh browser context per test with isolated storage, cookies, cache (Section 0.7.4)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Cross-test data leakage; session hijacking</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Integration tests verify context isolation; storage cleared between tests</span> |
| **Headless Mode in CI** | HEADLESS=true environment variable in GitHub Actions (Section 0.7.9) | UI-based attacks; resource exhaustion from GUI rendering | CI workflow configuration review |
| **No Extensions** | Playwright browser contexts launched without extensions or plugins | Extension-based malware or data exfiltration | Browser launch configuration audit |
| **Network Isolation** | Test environments network-isolated from production; no external API access | Test-induced data corruption in production systems | Network policy verification |

**LLM Exploration Security**

- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Sanitize user inputs to LLM prompts; validate generated Gherkin against expected format
- **Exploration Scope Limitation**: Playwright MCP limited to test environments only; never production URLs
- **Session Recording**: Log all LLM exploration interactions for security audit trail
- **Human Review**: All LLM-generated scenarios require human approval before execution (Section 0.7.8)

#### 2.5.4.4 Dependency Security

**Vulnerability Management**

| Security Practice | Implementation | Threat Mitigated | Validation Method |
|------------------|----------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Dependency Pinning** | All packages pinned to specific versions in requirements.txt (Section 0.3) | Supply chain attacks via compromised package updates | Dependency diff review in PRs |
| **Security Scanning** | GitHub Dependabot alerts for known vulnerabilities in dependencies | Exploitation of known CVEs in dependencies | Dependabot alert triage and patching workflow |
| **Pre-commit Security Linting** | ruff 0.9.3 with security-focused rules (e.g., S101 for assert usage) | Common security anti-patterns in test code | Pre-commit hook execution on every commit |
| **Quarterly Dependency Review** | Manual review of all dependencies for security advisories and updates | Zero-day vulnerabilities in outdated packages | Scheduled dependency update pull requests |

**Supply Chain Security**

- **Package Hash Verification**: Use pip --require-hashes for deterministic installs (optional for enhanced security)
- **Private Package Registry**: Host internal packages in private PyPI registry if applicable
- **SBOM Generation**: Generate Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for compliance and vulnerability tracking
- **License Compliance**: Ensure all dependencies use permissive licenses compatible with project requirements

#### 2.5.4.5 Audit and Compliance

**Audit Trail Requirements**

| Audit Event | Logging Mechanism | Retention Period | Purpose |
|-------------|------------------|------------------|---------|
| **MCP Tool Invocations** | FastAPI access logs with tool name, parameters, timestamps | 30 days | Debug test failures; detect abuse patterns |
| **LLM API Calls** | Token usage logs with prompt metadata (no prompt content) | 90 days | Cost monitoring; usage attribution |
| **CI Workflow Executions** | GitHub Actions workflow logs with test results | 90 days (GitHub retention) | Compliance audit trail; failure analysis |
| **Allure Report Access** | GitHub Pages access logs (if custom hosting) | 30 days | Monitor report usage; detect unauthorized access |

**Compliance Requirements**

- **GDPR Compliance**: Ensure test data contains no real EU resident PII; anonymize or synthesize all user data
- **SOC 2 Controls**: Implement access controls, audit logging, and change management for test infrastructure
- **HIPAA (if applicable)**: No protected health information (PHI) in test data or reports
- **PCI DSS (if applicable)**: No real credit card numbers in test payloads; use test card numbers only

### 2.5.5 Maintenance Requirements by Feature

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Maintenance requirements define ongoing operational activities necessary to keep the test framework healthy, secure, and aligned with evolving application changes. These procedures ensure long-term framework sustainability and reduce technical debt accumulation.</span>

#### 2.5.5.1 Dependency Maintenance

**Quarterly Dependency Update Cycle**

| Dependency Category | Update Frequency | Update Procedure | Risk Mitigation |
|--------------------|-----------------|------------------|-----------------|
| **Core Testing (pytest, Playwright)** | Quarterly (or on critical security patches) | Review release notes → Update requirements.txt → Run full test suite → Deploy to CI | Maintain staging environment for update validation before production |
| **MCP Servers (FastAPI, uvicorn)** | Quarterly | Update server dependencies → Run MCP integration tests → Deploy to dev → CI rollout | Health check validation before pytest execution in CI |
| **LLM Libraries (openai, ollama)** | Monthly (rapid iteration in LLM space) | Test backward compatibility with existing prompts → Update → Validate generation quality | Pin to stable releases; avoid bleeding-edge versions |
| **Development Tools (ruff, mypy, pre-commit)** | Monthly | Update pre-commit hooks → Run against full codebase → Fix lint/type errors → Commit | Use `pre-commit autoupdate` for automated updates |

**Playwright Browser Binary Updates**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Update Trigger**: Quarterly or when Playwright version updates (Playwright 1.55.0 requires specific browser versions)</span>
- **Update Command**: `playwright install` to download latest browser binaries for Chromium, Firefox, WebKit
- **CI Cache Invalidation**: Update GitHub Actions cache key to force browser binary refresh
- **Compatibility Testing**: Run visual regression tests to detect rendering changes across browser versions

#### 2.5.5.2 Test Maintenance Procedures

**Page Object Maintenance**

| Maintenance Activity | Trigger | Procedure | Frequency |
|---------------------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Locator Updates**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Application UI refactoring breaks tests</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Update Page Object locators (maintain role/label priority); run affected tests; commit</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">As needed (stable locators minimize frequency)</span> |
| **Method Refactoring** | Code duplication across Page Objects | Extract common patterns to BasePage class; refactor duplicates; validate with tests | Monthly code review |
| **Type Hint Updates** | mypy errors from API changes | Update method signatures and return types; run mypy validation; commit | Immediate (pre-commit enforces) |
| **Documentation** | New Page Objects added or existing modified | Update docstrings with usage examples; regenerate API docs | Per PR requirement |

**Gherkin Scenario Maintenance**

- **Quarterly Business Logic Review**: Product managers review scenarios for accuracy; deprecate obsolete scenarios
- **Scenario Consolidation**: Merge duplicate scenarios; extract common steps into Background sections
- **Step Definition Cleanup**: Remove unused step definitions; refactor long steps into Page Object methods
- **LLM-Generated Scenario Migration**: Convert pending_review scenarios to approved status after human validation

#### 2.5.5.3 MCP Server Maintenance

**FastAPI MCP (Deterministic) Maintenance**

| Maintenance Activity | Frequency | Procedure | Validation |
|---------------------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| **Payload Template Updates** | As API contracts change | Update template schemas in templates/ directory; validate with Pydantic models | Integration tests verify template generation |
| **Database Schema Migrations** | Per application schema change | Create Alembic migration scripts; test reset_env functionality | Run reset_env in staging environment |
| **Health Check Enhancements** | Quarterly | Add new health metrics (response time, request count, error rate) | CI workflow validates health check response |
| **Log Rotation** | Weekly (automated) | Archive MCP server logs > 7 days old; compress and store | Disk space monitoring |

**Playwright MCP (Exploration) Maintenance**

- **Session Cleanup**: Purge orphaned browser contexts daily; ensure no resource leaks
- **Gherkin Template Updates**: Refine generation templates based on human review feedback; improve business readability
- **WebSocket Connection Monitoring**: Track connection failures; implement reconnection logic if needed
- **Browser Binary Sync**: Ensure Playwright MCP uses same browser versions as test framework for consistency

#### 2.5.5.4 CI/CD Pipeline Maintenance

**GitHub Actions Workflow Maintenance**

| Maintenance Activity | Frequency | Procedure | Validation |
|---------------------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| **Runner Image Updates** | Quarterly (or on GitHub Actions updates) | Review GitHub Actions changelog → Update runner versions → Test workflow | Full test suite execution on updated runners |
| **Secrets Rotation** | Quarterly (or on suspected compromise) | Rotate FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN, LLM_API_KEY → Update GitHub secrets → Validate workflow | CI workflow success after rotation |
| **Cache Optimization** | Monthly | Analyze cache hit rates → Adjust cache keys → Monitor improvement | Cache hit rate > 90% target |
| **Workflow Timeout Tuning** | Quarterly | Review average workflow duration → Adjust timeout limits → Balance safety vs. speed | Workflow completes within 15-minute target |

**Allure Report Maintenance**

- **Historical Data Pruning**: Monthly job deletes reports > 30 days old to prevent storage bloat
- **GitHub Pages Deployment**: Quarterly review of deployment configuration; ensure report accessibility
- **Artifact Size Optimization**: Compress screenshots and traces; monitor artifact size trends
- **Categories Configuration**: Update categories.json to reflect new failure patterns and defect types

#### 2.5.5.5 Documentation Maintenance

**Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)**

| Documentation Type | Update Trigger | Procedure | Storage Location |
|-------------------|---------------|-----------|------------------|
| **ADRs** | Architectural pattern change or new pattern adoption | Create new ADR following template; document rationale, alternatives, decision | docs/adr/ directory |
| **README.md** | Setup procedure change or dependency update | Update installation steps, environment variables, usage examples | Repository root |
| **Technical Specification** | Feature scope change or requirement evolution | Update affected sections; track changes with highlighting; version control | docs/technical-specification.md |
| **API Documentation** | Page Object or MCP server API change | Regenerate Sphinx/MkDocs API docs; publish to documentation site | docs/api/ |

**Training and Onboarding Documentation**

- **Developer Onboarding Guide**: Update when setup procedures change; target 10-minute setup time (Section 0.7.10)
- **Test Authoring Guide**: Refresh examples when new patterns adopted; include Page Object and Gherkin best practices
- **Troubleshooting Runbook**: Document common failures and resolutions; update as new issues discovered
- **Video Tutorials**: Record screen captures for complex procedures (e.g., LLM-assisted test authoring workflow)

#### 2.5.5.6 Monitoring and Alerting Maintenance

**Test Framework Health Monitoring**

| Metric | Threshold | Alert Trigger | Remediation Procedure |
|--------|-----------|---------------|----------------------|
| **Test Success Rate** | < 95% in CI (Section 0.7.10) | Immediate alert on Slack/email | Investigate flaky tests; add to quarantine if needed |
| **Test Execution Duration** | > 15 minutes for full suite | Daily trend monitoring; alert on 20% increase | Optimize slow tests; increase pytest-xdist workers |
| **MCP Server Response Time** | p95 > 1000ms for any tool | Alert on sustained degradation | Profile slow operations; optimize database queries |
| **Allure Report Size** | > 500MB per run | Weekly monitoring | Implement artifact compression; reduce screenshot frequency |

**Cost Monitoring (LLM Usage)**

- **Token Budget Tracking**: Alert at 80% of monthly token budget for hosted LLM usage
- **Ollama vs. OpenAI Mix**: Monitor usage split; optimize for cost-effective local development
- **API Error Rate**: Track LLM API failures; switch providers or throttle on sustained errors
- **Generation Quality**: Track human approval rate for LLM-generated scenarios; retrain prompts if < 70% approval

#### 2.5.5.7 Quarterly Framework Review

**Review Checklist**

- [ ] **Dependency Audit**: Review all dependencies for updates, security vulnerabilities, license compliance
- [ ] **Performance Baseline**: Run performance benchmarks; compare against historical data; identify regressions
- [ ] **Test Coverage Analysis**: Generate coverage reports; identify untested code paths; prioritize coverage improvements
- [ ] **Flakiness Analysis**: Review Allure historical trends; quarantine or fix flaky tests
- [ ] **Documentation Completeness**: Audit documentation for accuracy; update outdated sections
- [ ] **Architecture Alignment**: Validate framework still aligns with Agent Action Plan constraints (Section 0.7)
- [ ] **Team Feedback**: Conduct developer survey on framework usability; prioritize improvement areas
- [ ] **Cost Review**: Analyze LLM API costs, CI runner costs, storage costs; optimize spending

**Continuous Improvement Process**

- **Retrospectives**: Quarterly retrospective on test framework effectiveness; action items tracked
- **Innovation Time**: Allocate 10% of team capacity for framework enhancements and experimentation
- **Industry Best Practices**: Monitor pytest, Playwright, and BDD community for emerging patterns
- **Framework Roadmap**: Maintain 6-month roadmap for framework improvements aligned with application evolution

### 2.5.6 Cross-Feature Integration Considerations

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Cross-feature integration considerations address dependencies, shared components, and coordination requirements between features. Understanding these integration points is critical for system-level design and change impact analysis.</span>

#### 2.5.6.1 Critical Integration Points

**F-001 (Framework) ↔ F-002 (FastAPI MCP)**

| Integration Point | Implementation | Impact | Risk Mitigation |
|------------------|----------------|--------|-----------------|
| **MCP Client Fixture** | conftest.py defines mcp_client fixture returning authenticated httpx AsyncClient | All tests depend on MCP for test data; fixture failure = widespread test failures | Health check validation in fixture initialization; clear error messages on MCP unavailability |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Environment Variable Configuration**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FASTAPI_MCP_URL and FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN from .env file or CI secrets</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Missing environment variables cause fixture initialization failures</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Fail-fast validation on startup with clear error messages</span> |
| **Tool Invocation Pattern** | Tests call mcp_client.invoke_tool("seed_user", {...}); results used in test logic | MCP server downtime blocks test execution | Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures |

**F-001 (Framework) ↔ F-007 (Architecture)**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Browser Context Isolation**: F-007 defines function-scoped browser_context fixture; F-001 ensures pytest-xdist compatibility</span>
- **Page Object Integration**: Step definitions (F-001) delegate to Page Objects (F-007); tight coupling requires coordination
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Locator Strategy Enforcement**: F-007 prohibits CSS/XPath; F-001 validates via pre-commit hooks</span>
- **Type Safety**: F-007 enables mypy strict mode; F-001 test code must comply with type hints

**F-005 (CI/CD) ↔ F-002 (FastAPI MCP)**

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**MCP Server Startup in CI**: Workflow starts FastAPI MCP as background service before pytest execution (Section 0.7.5)</span>
- **Health Check Polling**: Workflow retries health check endpoint until ready or 30-second timeout
- **Log Capture**: MCP server logs captured as workflow artifacts for debugging CI failures
- **Secret Management**: FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN from GitHub Actions secrets; injected as environment variable

**F-003 (Playwright MCP) ↔ F-004 (LLM Authoring)**

- **Exploration Session Handoff**: Playwright MCP logs interactions; LLM ingests logs to generate Gherkin scenarios
- **Selector Strategy Alignment**: Playwright MCP prioritizes role-based selectors; LLM generates .feature files without CSS/XPath
- **Session History Format**: Structured JSON format for interactions enables LLM parsing and scenario generation
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Development-Only Constraint**: Both features disabled in CI by default; optional enablement via feature flags</span>

#### 2.5.6.2 Shared Component Dependencies

**Playwright Contexts (F-001, F-003, F-007)**

| Shared Component | Features | Coordination Required | Impact |
|-----------------|----------|----------------------|--------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Browser Context Lifecycle**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (test execution), F-003 (exploration), F-007 (isolation pattern)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All must use function-scoped contexts; consistent launch options</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Shared BaseBrowserContext class ensures consistency</span> |
| **Browser Binary Versions** | F-001, F-003 | Same Playwright version ensures identical browser binaries | Dependency pinning in requirements.txt prevents version drift |
| **Headless Mode Configuration** | F-001, F-003 | HEADLESS=true in CI; configurable in local dev | Environment variable convention documented |

**httpx Client (F-001, F-002)**

- **API Testing**: F-001 uses httpx for API tests; F-002 uses httpx for MCP client communication
- **Connection Pooling**: Shared httpx.AsyncClient instance in fixtures reduces overhead
- **Timeout Configuration**: Consistent timeout settings across API and MCP calls
- **Retry Logic**: Shared tenacity retry decorator for transient network failures

**Pydantic Models (F-002, F-007)**

- **MCP Payload Validation**: F-002 uses Pydantic for build_payload template validation
- **API Client Typing**: F-007 uses Pydantic for typed API client request/response models
- **Schema Evolution**: Breaking changes to Pydantic models require coordination across features
- **Validation Consistency**: Shared validation rules ensure uniform error handling

| Environment Variable | Features | Purpose | Default Value |
|---------------------|----------|---------|---------------|

| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FASTAPI_MCP_URL</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-001 (MCP client fixture), F-002 (server), F-005 (CI)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP server endpoint</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">http://localhost:8000</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">F-003 (server), F-004 (LLM integration)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP server endpoint (dev-only)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">http://localhost:8001</span> |

**pytest.ini Shared Configuration**

- **Feature Discovery**: F-001 depends on pytest-bdd feature file path configuration
- **Timeout Settings**: F-001 pytest-timeout configuration applies to all tests across features

### 2.5.7 Implementation Priority and Sequencing

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Implementation sequencing ensures features are developed in dependency order, minimizing integration risks and enabling incremental validation. This section defines the recommended implementation phases based on feature dependencies documented in Section 2.2.5.1.</span>

#### Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1-2)
- **F-001**: Unified Test Automation Framework (pytest + Playwright + Gherkin foundation)
- **F-007**: Maintainable Test Architecture (Page Object patterns, fixture definitions)
- **Rationale**: Establish core testing infrastructure before integrations

#### Phase 2: Data Management (Weeks 3-4)
- **F-002**: FastAPI MCP (Deterministic) (test data seeding and environment reset)
- **Rationale**: Enable deterministic testing before CI/CD and reporting

#### Phase 3: CI/CD and Reporting (Weeks 5-6)
- **F-005**: GitHub Actions CI/CD Integration (automated test execution)
- **F-006**: Allure Reporting & Observability (test result visualization)
- **Rationale**: Automate execution and reporting before advanced features

#### Phase 4: Advanced Features (Weeks 7-8)
- **F-003**: Playwright MCP (Exploration) (LLM-assisted exploration)
- **F-004**: LLM-Assisted Test Authoring (Gherkin generation)
- **Rationale**: Add AI-assisted capabilities after stable foundation

### 2.5.8 Success Criteria and Validation

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Implementation considerations are validated through the success criteria defined in Agent Action Plan Section 0.7.10. Each feature's implementation must satisfy these criteria before being considered production-ready.</span>

**Critical Success Metrics**

1. **Framework Setup**: Developer setup completes in < 10 minutes (F-001, F-002)
2. **Test Authoring Speed**: New scenario authoring in < 30 minutes (F-001, F-007)
3. **CI Execution Time**: Full test suite completes in < 15 minutes (F-005)
4. **Test Stability**: > 95% success rate in CI with no flakiness (F-001, F-007)
5. **Data Management**: Zero hardcoded test data in repository (F-002)
6. **Report Quality**: Failures include screenshot, trace, clear error (F-006)
7. **LLM Integration**: Draft scenarios generated in < 5 seconds (F-004)
8. **Documentation**: New team member onboards using docs/ only (All features)

**Validation Checklist per Section 2.3.6**

- [ ] All acceptance criteria met with objective verification
- [ ] Performance requirements satisfied per Section 2.5.2
- [ ] Security controls implemented per Section 2.5.4
- [ ] Integration points validated per Section 2.5.6
- [ ] Maintenance procedures documented per Section 2.5.5
- [ ] <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Architectural constraints enforced per Section 2.5.1</span>

## 2.6 Requirements Traceability Framework

### 2.6.1 Traceability Matrix Overview

The Requirements Traceability Framework establishes bidirectional traceability linking strategic business objectives to concrete implementation artifacts, ensuring comprehensive coverage and facilitating impact analysis for requirement changes. This framework connects the five Core Objectives defined in Section 0.1.1 to the seven Features documented in Section 2.2, their 49 Functional Requirements detailed in Section 2.3, and the corresponding test cases that validate implementation completeness.

**Traceability Dimensions:**

- **Forward Traceability**: Business objectives flow down through features to requirements and test cases
- **Backward Traceability**: Each test case traces up through requirements to originating business objectives
- **Lateral Traceability**: Cross-feature dependencies and integration points documented in Section 2.2.5
- **Version Control**: All requirement changes tracked in GitHub repository history per CI/CD framework (Section 0.1.3 #8)

### 2.6.2 Core Objectives to Features Mapping

This section maps the five strategic Core Objectives from the Agent Action Plan (Section 0.1.1) to the seven implemented Features, establishing the foundation for end-to-end traceability.

| Core Objective | Feature ID | Feature Name | Relationship |
|----------------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| **Core Objective #1**: Unified Test Automation Framework | F-001 | Unified Test Automation Framework | Direct implementation |
| **Core Objective #2**: Deterministic Test Execution with MCP Integration | F-002 | FastAPI MCP (Deterministic) | Primary implementation |
| **Core Objective #2**: Deterministic Test Execution with MCP Integration | F-003 | Playwright MCP (Exploration) | Secondary implementation |
| **Core Objective #3**: LLM-Assisted Test Authoring | F-004 | LLM-Assisted Test Authoring | Direct implementation |
| **Core Objective #4**: Enterprise CI/CD Integration | F-005 | GitHub Actions CI/CD Integration | Primary implementation |
| **Core Objective #4**: Enterprise CI/CD Integration | F-006 | Allure Reporting & Observability | Supporting implementation |
| **Core Objective #5**: Maintainable Test Architecture | F-007 | Maintainable Test Architecture & Best Practices | Direct implementation |

### 2.6.3 Comprehensive Traceability Matrix

This matrix provides complete traceability from Core Objectives through Features and Functional Requirements to Test IDs, enabling comprehensive requirement coverage validation and change impact analysis.

**Note on Test IDs**: Test identifiers correspond to pytest markers and test discovery patterns. Tests are organized using pytest's marker system (`@pytest.mark.feature_id`, `@pytest.mark.requirement_id`) to enable selective test execution and traceability reporting. Full test implementation details are documented in Section 0.5 (Technical Implementation) with test coverage requirements specified in Section 2.1.2.4 (minimum 80% code coverage).

### 2.6.4 Requirement Version Control and Change Management

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All requirement changes are tracked through GitHub version control, providing comprehensive audit trails and facilitating collaborative requirement evolution.</span>

**Version Control Framework:**

- **Repository**: All requirements documented in this Technical Specification are version-controlled in the project's GitHub repository
- **Change Tracking**: Requirement modifications captured through Git commit history with descriptive commit messages
- **Change Authors**: GitHub commit attribution identifies individuals responsible for requirement changes
- **Change Rationale**: Commit messages and pull request descriptions document justification for requirement modifications
- **Impact Analysis**: Pull request reviews assess feature and component impacts before merging changes

**Change Management Process:**

1. **Requirement Modification Proposal**: Changes proposed via pull request with clear description of modification rationale
2. **Stakeholder Review**: Technical leads and product managers review proposed changes for business alignment
3. **Impact Assessment**: Traceability matrix consulted to identify affected features, requirements, and test cases
4. **Approval**: Pull request approved by designated reviewers before merging
5. **Version Update**: Technical Specification updated with change details and traceability matrix refreshed
6. **Communication**: Changes communicated to development team through GitHub notifications and documentation updates

**Traceability Maintenance:**

- When requirements change, affected entries in the traceability matrix are updated to reflect new relationships
- Test cases linked to modified requirements are reviewed and updated as needed to maintain coverage
- Historical requirement versions accessible through GitHub commit history for audit purposes

### 2.6.5 Test ID Convention and pytest Marker Integration

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test IDs documented in the traceability matrix correspond directly to pytest markers, enabling selective test execution, traceability reporting, and comprehensive test organization.</span>

**pytest Marker Convention:**

Test cases are organized using a hierarchical marker system that maps to the traceability framework:

```python
# Feature-level marker
@pytest.mark.f001  # Marks test as validating F-001 (Unified Test Automation Framework)

#### Requirement-level marker
@pytest.mark.f001_rq001  # Marks test as validating F-001-RQ-001 (pytest plugin configuration)

#### Combined markers for comprehensive traceability
@pytest.mark.f001
@pytest.mark.f001_rq004
def test_browser_context_fixture_initialization(browser_context):
    """
    Test ID: TC-F001-RQ004
    Validates that browser_context fixture initializes successfully
    and provides expected Playwright BrowserContext interface.
    """
    assert browser_context is not None
    page = browser_context.new_page()
    assert page is not None
```

**Selective Test Execution:**

The marker system enables targeted test execution for specific features or requirements:

```bash
# Execute all tests for Feature F-001
pytest -m f001

#### Execute tests for specific requirement
pytest -m f001_rq004

#### Execute tests for multiple features
pytest -m "f001 or f002"

#### Execute tests excluding specific features
pytest -m "not f003"
```

**Traceability Reporting:**

pytest markers integrate with Allure reporting to provide visual traceability in test reports:

```python
@allure.feature("F-001: Unified Test Automation Framework")
@allure.story("F-001-RQ-004: Centralized Fixtures")
@pytest.mark.f001
@pytest.mark.f001_rq004
def test_mcp_client_fixture_authentication():
    """
    Test ID: TC-F001-RQ004
    Validates MCP client fixture authenticates successfully using JWT token.
    """
    pass
```

This integration ensures that Allure reports display clear traceability from business objectives through features to individual test cases, facilitating requirement coverage analysis and test result communication to stakeholders.

### 2.6.6 Traceability Matrix Maintenance

**Maintenance Responsibilities:**

- **Technical Leads**: Ensure traceability matrix updated when requirements change or new features added
- **Test Engineers**: Update Test ID mappings when test cases created, modified, or deprecated
- **Product Managers**: Validate that Core Objectives remain aligned with business goals during quarterly reviews

**Maintenance Triggers:**

- New feature requests approved and added to Feature Catalog (Section 2.2)
- Functional requirements modified or added (Section 2.3)
- Test cases created, updated, or removed
- Core Objectives revised based on business strategy changes

**Validation Activities:**

- **Quarterly Traceability Audits**: Verify all requirements have corresponding test coverage per Section 2.1.2.4 (minimum 80% code coverage)
- **Pull Request Reviews**: Validate traceability matrix consistency when requirements or tests change
- **CI/CD Integration**: Automated validation that all marked tests execute successfully
- **Coverage Gap Analysis**: Identify requirements lacking adequate test coverage and prioritize test creation

### 2.7.1 Technology Stack Assumptions (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Based on the comprehensive Dependency Inventory analysis (Section 0.3) and Agent Action Plan (Section 0.1), the following technology choices are confirmed and established as the foundation for this test automation framework:</span>

**Core Testing Framework:**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**pytest 8.4.2**: Primary test framework and runner with Python 3.9+ support</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**pytest-bdd 8.1.0**: Gherkin/BDD support using official Gherkin parser</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Playwright 1.55.0**: Browser automation library (Python 3.9+ required)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**pytest-playwright 0.6.2**: Playwright integration for pytest ecosystem</span>

**API Testing Infrastructure:**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**httpx 0.28.1**: Modern async/sync HTTP client for API testing capabilities</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Pydantic 2.10.5**: Data validation and typing for API models with enhanced performance</span>

**MCP Server Components:**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**FastAPI 0.118.0**: Web framework for MCP server implementation with modern async support</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**uvicorn 0.34.0**: ASGI server runtime for FastAPI MCP servers</span>

**LLM Integration:**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**OpenAI 1.59.8**: API client supporting OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible endpoints</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Ollama 0.4.8**: Local LLM client for development without API costs</span>

**Greenfield Project Context:**

This specification documents a greenfield project (per Section 1.1.1) building an enterprise-grade test automation solution from scratch. The minimal repository state (single README.md) is intentional and aligns with the project's foundational phase. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Implementation guidance is derived from the Agent Action Plan (Section 0.1) which establishes architectural patterns, technical constraints, and integration requirements that form the baseline requirement documentation for this framework.</span>

### 2.7.2 Architectural Constraints (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The following architectural constraints are mandated by the Agent Action Plan (Section 0.1.2) and define the core separation of concerns within the test automation framework:</span>

#### 2.7.2.1 Test Execution Architecture

**Constraint: pytest as Primary Test Runner**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Tests must execute inside pytest with Playwright as the browser automation engine</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP servers run as supporting services alongside the test runner, not as the execution engine itself</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM agents serve as helpers for test discovery and generation, never directly executing tests</span>
- This ensures fast, reliable test execution using battle-tested pytest infrastructure

**Rationale:** Maintains deterministic test execution while leveraging AI capabilities for authoring assistance without introducing non-determinism into the test runner.

#### 2.7.2.2 Business-Readable Test Scenarios

**Constraint: High-Level Gherkin Requirements**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All Gherkin scenarios must be written in plain language understandable by non-technical stakeholders</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Gherkin steps must remain high-level, focusing on business actions and outcomes rather than UI implementation details</span>
- Given/When/Then statements must describe behavior at the business domain level
- No UI mechanics (e.g., "click button at coordinates x,y") permitted in Gherkin files

**Rationale:** Ensures feature files serve as living documentation accessible to product owners, business analysts, and QA teams without technical expertise.

#### 2.7.2.3 Environment-Specific MCP Server Deployment

**Constraint: Differential MCP Server Usage by Environment**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Production/CI pipelines: FastAPI MCP server only (for deterministic data/state management)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Development environment: Both FastAPI and Playwright MCP servers available</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP server requires explicit opt-in for CI usage when needed for specific scenarios</span>

**Rationale:** Optimizes CI pipeline performance while preserving exploratory testing capabilities in development.

### 2.7.3 Implementation Constraints (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The following implementation-level constraints enforce maintainability, stability, and scalability requirements mandated in Section 0.1.2:</span>

#### 2.7.3.1 Selector Stability Requirements

**Constraint: Stable Locator Strategy Enforcement**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Page Object Pattern mandatory for all UI interactions</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Selector priority order: ARIA roles/accessible names first, then data-testid attributes</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Fragile CSS class names and complex XPath expressions prohibited</span>
- All selectors must be resilient to minor UI styling changes

**Rationale:** Reduces test flakiness and maintenance burden by avoiding brittle locators that break with cosmetic application changes.

#### 2.7.3.2 Test Data Management

**Constraint: Zero Hard-Coded Test Data**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">No hard-coded test data permitted in test files or step definitions</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All test users must be created via MCP `seed_user` tool</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Request payloads must be constructed via MCP `build_payload` tool</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment state must be reset via MCP `reset_env` tool before test suites</span>

**Rationale:** Ensures test data freshness, eliminates data coupling between tests, and centralizes test data management for easier maintenance.

#### 2.7.3.3 Test Isolation and Parallelization

**Constraint: Deterministic, Parallel-Friendly Test Design**
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Each test must receive a fresh Playwright browser context</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">No shared mutable state permitted between tests</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Tests must not rely on execution order</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Parallel execution must not cause flakiness or race conditions</span>

**Rationale:** Enables reliable parallel test execution with pytest-xdist, reducing CI pipeline duration while maintaining test determinism.

#### 2.7.3.4 Configuration Externalization

**Constraint: Environment Variable-Based Configuration**

All runtime configuration must be externalized through environment variables per Section 0.1.2:

| Environment Variable | Purpose | Required In |
|---------------------|---------|-------------|
| `BASE_URL` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Web application base URL for UI tests</span> | All environments |
| `API_BASE_URL` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">REST API endpoint base URL</span> | All environments |
| `HEADLESS` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Boolean flag for headless browser execution</span> | CI/production |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM provider selection (openai/ollama)</span> | Development |
| `LLM_MODEL` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Model identifier for LLM requests</span> | Development |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Authentication key for hosted LLM services</span> | Development (hosted) |
| `FASTAPI_MCP_URL` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP server endpoint URL</span> | All environments |
| `FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Authentication token for MCP server access</span> | All environments |
| `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL` | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP server endpoint (optional)</span> | Development only |

**Rationale:** Enables environment-specific configuration without code changes, supporting multiple deployment targets (local, staging, production) with identical codebase.
