### 5.2.4 CI/CD & Reporting Layer

<span>The CI/CD & Reporting Layer orchestrates automated test execution in GitHub Actions pipelines and generates comprehensive HTML reports with Allure. This layer manages MCP server lifecycle, pytest execution with parallel workers, artifact collection, and report publishing to GitHub Pages or artifact storage.</span>

#### 5.2.4.1 GitHub Actions Workflows

**Purpose and Responsibilities:**

<span>GitHub Actions workflows provide automated CI/CD pipelines for test execution, code quality checks, and report generation. Workflows manage prerequisite service startup (FastAPI MCP server), pytest execution with matrix strategies for browser/Python version combinations, artifact collection for debugging, and deployment of test reports to GitHub Pages.</span>

**Technologies and Frameworks:**

<span>GitHub Actions platform with custom workflow configurations:</span>

- <span>**GitHub Actions:** CI/CD platform with workflow orchestration, matrix strategies, service containers, and artifact storage
- **Docker:** Container runtime for MCP server service containers
- **GitHub Pages:** Static site hosting for Allure HTML reports

**Key Interfaces and APIs:**

<span>Workflow YAML definitions configure CI/CD pipelines:</span>

**Test Execution Workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml):**

```yaml
name: Test Execution

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      browser:
        description: 'Browser to test'
        required: true
        default: 'chromium'
        type: choice
        options:
          - chromium
          - firefox
          - webkit
          - all

env:
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/ms-playwright

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test (${{ matrix.browser }}, Python ${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        browser: [chromium, firefox, webkit]
        python-version: ['3.9', '3.11', '3.12']
    
    services:
      fastapi-mcp:
        image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/fastapi-mcp:latest
        ports:
          - 8000:8000
        env:
          AUTH_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.MCP_AUTH_SECRET }}
          APP_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.APP_BASE_URL }}
          APP_API_URL: ${{ secrets.APP_API_URL }}
          APP_ADMIN_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.APP_ADMIN_EMAIL }}
          APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: 'pip'
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
      
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: |
          playwright install --with-deps ${{ matrix.browser }}
      
      - name: Wait for FastAPI MCP server
        run: |
          timeout 60 bash -c 'until curl -f http://localhost:8000/health; do sleep 2; done'
      
      - name: Run tests
        env:
          BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.APP_BASE_URL }}
          API_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.APP_API_URL }}
          FASTAPI_MCP_URL: http://localhost:8000
          MCP_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MCP_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          HEADLESS: true
          BROWSER: ${{ matrix.browser }}
        run: |
          pytest \
            --browser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
            --headed=false \
            --tracing=retain-on-failure \
            --screenshot=only-on-failure \
            --video=retain-on-failure \
            --alluredir=allure-results \
            --maxfail=5 \
            -n auto \
            tests/
      
      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: allure-results-${{ matrix.browser }}-py${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: allure-results/
          retention-days: 30
      
      - name: Upload traces
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: traces-${{ matrix.browser }}-py${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: test-results/
          retention-days: 30
      
      - name: Upload coverage
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.11' && matrix.browser == 'chromium'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: ./coverage.xml
          flags: unittests
          name: codecov-umbrella
```

**Allure Report Generation Workflow (.github/workflows/allure-report.yml):**

<span>Separate workflow generates and publishes Allure HTML reports:</span>

```yaml
name: Allure Report

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Test Execution"]
    types:
      - completed

permissions:
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  generate-report:
    name: Generate Allure Report
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' }}
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Download all test results
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: allure-results
          pattern: allure-results-*
          merge-multiple: true
      
      - name: Download Allure history
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          ref: gh-pages
          path: gh-pages
      
      - name: Copy Allure history
        if: always()
        run: |
          mkdir -p allure-results/history
          if [ -d "gh-pages/allure-report/history" ]; then
            cp -r gh-pages/allure-report/history/* allure-results/history/
          fi
      
      - name: Generate Allure report
        uses: simple-elf/allure-report-action@master
        with:
          allure_results: allure-results
          allure_history: allure-history
          keep_reports: 30
      
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: allure-history
          publish_branch: gh-pages
          destination_dir: allure-report
```

**Code Quality Workflow (.github/workflows/lint.yml):**

on:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

#### 5.2.4.2 Allure Reporting Integration

**Purpose and Responsibilities:**

<span>Allure reporting provides enterprise-grade HTML test reports with comprehensive diagnostics including screenshots, traces, browser logs, API request/response details, and test history trends. Allure integrates with pytest through the allure-pytest plugin, capturing test metadata throughout execution and generating interactive HTML reports published to GitHub Pages.</span>

**Technologies and Frameworks:**

<span>Allure reporting stack includes:</span>

- <span>**allure-pytest 2.15.0:** pytest plugin capturing test results, attachments, and metadata
- **Allure Commandline 2.24.0:** Report generation tool producing HTML reports from test results
- **GitHub Pages:** Static site hosting for report publishing

**Key Interfaces and APIs:**

<span>Allure integration through pytest plugin decorators and attachments:</span>

**Allure Decorators:**

```python
import allure
from allure_commons.types import AttachmentType

@allure.feature("User Management")
@allure.story("User Creation")
@allure.severity(allure.severity_level.CRITICAL)
@allure.tag("smoke", "regression")
@allure.link("https://jira.example.com/ISSUE-123", name="Related Issue")
def test_create_user(api_client, mcp_client):
    """Test user creation with comprehensive Allure reporting."""
    
    with allure.step("Generate test data via MCP"):
        user_payload = mcp_client.build_payload(
            template="create_user",
            params={"role": "editor"}
        )
        allure.attach(
            json.dumps(user_payload, indent=2),
            name="Generated Payload",
            attachment_type=AttachmentType.JSON
        )
    
    with allure.step("Create user via API"):
        response = api_client.create_user(CreateUserRequest(**user_payload))
        # API client automatically attaches request/response
    
    with allure.step("Verify user creation"):
        assert response.email == user_payload["email"]
        assert response.is_active is True
```

**Allure Attachment Utilities (tests/helpers/allure_utils.py):**

```python
import allure
from allure_commons.types import AttachmentType
from playwright.sync_api import Page
import json

def attach_screenshot(page: Page, name: str = "Screenshot"):
    """Attach page screenshot to Allure report."""
    screenshot_bytes = page.screenshot()
    allure.attach(
        screenshot_bytes,
        name=name,
        attachment_type=AttachmentType.PNG
    )

def attach_console_logs(page: Page):
    """Attach browser console logs to Allure report."""
    console_logs = []
    for msg in page.context.console_messages:
        console_logs.append(f"[{msg.type}] {msg.text}")
    
    allure.attach(
        "\n".join(console_logs),
        name="Browser Console Logs",
        attachment_type=AttachmentType.TEXT
    )

def attach_trace(trace_path: str):
    """Attach Playwright trace file to Allure report."""
    with open(trace_path, "rb") as f:
        allure.attach(
            f.read(),
            name="Playwright Trace",
            attachment_type=AttachmentType.ZIP,
            extension=".zip"
        )

def attach_api_request(method: str, url: str, payload: dict):
    """Attach API request details to Allure report."""
    request_details = {
        "method": method,
        "url": url,
        "payload": payload
    }
    allure.attach(
        json.dumps(request_details, indent=2),
        name=f"{method} Request",
        attachment_type=AttachmentType.JSON
    )

def attach_api_response(status_code: int, response_body: dict):
    """Attach API response details to Allure report."""
    response_details = {
        "status_code": status_code,
        "body": response_body
    }
    allure.attach(
        json.dumps(response_details, indent=2),
        name="API Response",
        attachment_type=AttachmentType.JSON
    )
```

**Data Persistence Requirements:**

<span>Allure generates and persists comprehensive report data:</span>

- **Allure Results:** JSON result files written to `allure-results/` directory during test execution
- **Attachments:** Screenshots, traces, logs embedded in result files or stored as separate files
- **HTML Reports:** Generated HTML reports published to `allure-report/` directory on GitHub Pages
- **History:** Trend data preserved across report generations for historical analysis

**Scaling Considerations:**

<span>Allure reporting scales through efficient artifact management:</span>

**Attachment Optimization:**

- Selective screenshot capture (only on failure by default)

**Report History:**

**Parallel Report Generation:**

Allure merges results from parallel pytest workers automatically, producing unified reports from distributed test execution.

### 5.2.6 Component State Transition Diagram

<span>The following state diagram illustrates the lifecycle of test execution components from initialization through cleanup:</span>

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Initialization: pytest invocation
    
    Initialization --> SessionSetup: Load configuration
    SessionSetup --> MCPConnection: Initialize session fixtures
    
    MCPConnection --> EnvironmentReset: Connect to FastAPI MCP
    EnvironmentReset --> TestDiscovery: reset_env() called
    
    TestDiscovery --> TestExecution: Discover .feature files
    
    state TestExecution {
        [*] --> FunctionSetup
        FunctionSetup --> BrowserContextCreation: Create fixtures
        BrowserContextCreation --> UserSeeding: Browser context isolated
        UserSeeding --> StepExecution: seed_user() via MCP
        
        StepExecution --> GivenStep: Execute scenario
        GivenStep --> WhenStep: Setup complete
        WhenStep --> ThenStep: Action executed
        ThenStep --> Assertions: Outcome validated
        
        Assertions --> Success: All assertions pass
        Assertions --> Failure: Assertion fails
        
        Success --> Cleanup
        Failure --> DiagnosticCapture
        
        DiagnosticCapture --> ScreenshotCapture: Capture diagnostics
        ScreenshotCapture --> TraceCollection: Screenshot saved
        TraceCollection --> ConsoleLogCollection: Trace archived
        ConsoleLogCollection --> AllureAttachment: Console logs captured
        AllureAttachment --> Cleanup: Attach to Allure
        
        Cleanup --> [*]: Close browser context
    }
    
    TestExecution --> NextTest: More tests
    TestExecution --> SessionTeardown: All tests complete
    
    NextTest --> TestExecution: Isolated context
    
    SessionTeardown --> ReportGeneration: Close all resources
    ReportGeneration --> AllureReport: Generate HTML report
    AllureReport --> GitHubPages: Publish report
    GitHubPages --> [*]: Pipeline complete
    
    note right of EnvironmentReset
        MCP server ensures
        clean starting state
    end note
    
    note right of BrowserContextCreation
        Per-test isolation
        for parallel safety
    end note
    
    note right of DiagnosticCapture
        Comprehensive failure
        diagnostics for debugging
    end note
```

### 5.2.7 Key Component Design Patterns

<span>The component architecture implements several proven design patterns ensuring maintainability and scalability:</span>

**Page Object Pattern:**<span>Encapsulates UI interactions behind semantic interfaces with stable ARIA-based locators, isolating implementation details from test logic.</span>

**Repository Pattern:**<span>API clients provide typed access to REST endpoints with Pydantic validation, abstracting HTTP communication details.</span>

**Dependency Injection:**<span>pytest fixtures manage component lifecycle and dependencies, enabling flexible configuration and test isolation.</span>

**Strategy Pattern:**<span>LLM client abstraction enables provider switching (Ollama vs. OpenAI) through environment configuration without code changes.</span>

**Facade Pattern:**<span>MCP servers provide simplified interfaces to complex data management and browser automation operations.</span>

**Observer Pattern:**<span>Allure plugin observes pytest execution lifecycle through hooks, capturing test events and artifacts automatically.</span>

**Builder Pattern:**<span>MCP build_payload tool constructs complex request payloads from templates with parameter substitution.</span>

## 5.3 Technical Decisions and Rationale

### 5.3.1 Test Framework Core Technology Decisions

#### 5.3.1.1 pytest + pytest-bdd vs. Alternative Test Frameworks

**Decision:** Adopt pytest 8.4.2 with pytest-bdd 8.1.0 as the primary test execution framework

**Rationale:**

The test automation framework requires a Python-based test runner that supports BDD (Behavior-Driven Development) with Gherkin syntax, advanced fixture management for browser context isolation, and extensive plugin ecosystem integration. Three primary alternatives were evaluated:

| Framework | Advantages | Disadvantages | Decision Factor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **pytest + pytest-bdd (Selected)** | Industry-standard fixture system, native pytest plugin integration, 8,000+ plugins available, pytest-xdist for parallel execution | Fixture learning curve for beginners | Superior fixture dependency injection enables per-test browser context isolation |
| **unittest + behave** | Python stdlib unittest module, behave mature BDD framework | No fixture system comparable to pytest, limited async support, parallel execution requires custom implementation | Insufficient isolation capabilities for browser contexts |
| **Robot Framework** | Keyword-driven testing, non-programmer friendly, built-in reporting | Performance overhead, Python integration less natural, difficult async support | Poor fit for modern async API testing with httpx |
| **nose2** | unittest extension with plugins | Stagnant development, smaller ecosystem than pytest | Lacks active maintenance and pytest-bdd equivalent |

**pytest + pytest-bdd Selected Because:**

1. **Fixture Dependency Injection:** pytest's fixture system enables sophisticated resource management patterns critical for test isolation:

   ```python
   # Function-scoped browser context ensures per-test isolation
   @pytest.fixture
   def context(browser: Browser) -> BrowserContext:
       context = browser.new_context()
       yield context
       context.close()  # Automatic cleanup
   ```

2. **pytest-bdd Native Integration:** pytest-bdd 8.1.0 implements Gherkin as a pytest plugin, providing full access to pytest fixtures, markers, and plugins within step definitions:

   ```python
   @when("the user logs in with valid credentials")
   def user_logs_in(page: Page, test_user: dict, login_page: LoginPage):
       # Full access to pytest fixtures in step definitions
       login_page.login(test_user["email"], "password")
   ```

3. **Async/Await Support:** pytest-asyncio 0.25.2 enables async test functions and fixtures, essential for httpx async API testing and FastAPI MCP server interactions:

   ```python
   @pytest.mark.asyncio
   async def test_concurrent_api_calls(async_api_client: httpx.AsyncClient):
       responses = await asyncio.gather(*[
           async_api_client.get(f"/users/{i}") for i in range(10)
       ])
   ```

4. **Parallel Execution:** pytest-xdist 3.6.1 provides robust parallel test execution with intelligent load balancing, reducing test suite execution time by 60-80%:

   ```bash
   pytest -n auto  # Automatic worker count based on CPU cores
   ```

5. **Plugin Ecosystem:** pytest's 8,000+ plugins include pytest-playwright 0.6.2 for browser fixture management, allure-pytest 2.15.0 for enterprise reporting, and pytest-httpx 0.35.0 for httpx mocking

**Trade-offs Accepted:**

- **Learning Curve:** pytest fixture scopes (`function`, `class`, `module`, `session`) require understanding dependency injection patterns, mitigated by comprehensive documentation and team training
- **Magic Fixtures:** pytest discovers fixtures automatically, which can be confusing without explicit imports, mitigated by following fixture naming conventions and using `conftest.py` hierarchies

**Justification:**

pytest 8.4.2 with pytest-bdd 8.1.0 represents the optimal foundation for a test automation framework requiring deterministic test isolation, async API testing, business-readable BDD scenarios, and parallel execution capabilities. The fixture system's dependency injection pattern is specifically designed to solve the per-test browser context isolation requirement, eliminating shared state and enabling safe parallel execution.

#### 5.3.1.2 Playwright vs. Selenium WebDriver

**Decision:** Adopt Playwright 1.55.0 for cross-browser UI automation

**Rationale:**

The framework requires a browser automation library providing stable locator strategies (ARIA roles, semantic selectors), automatic waiting mechanisms, comprehensive debugging tools (traces, screenshots), and cross-browser support (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). Two primary alternatives were evaluated:

| Criteria | Playwright 1.55.0 (Selected) | Selenium WebDriver 4.x | Decision Factor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Locator Strategies** | ARIA role-based selectors native: `page.get_by_role("button", name="Submit")` | CSS/XPath primary, ARIA requires complex selectors | Playwright prioritizes accessibility-based locators reducing brittleness |
| **Automatic Waiting** | Built-in actionability checks (visible, stable, enabled) | Explicit waits required via WebDriverWait | Playwright eliminates 80% of wait-related flakiness |
| **Browser Context Isolation** | Native isolated contexts with independent cookies/storage | Requires separate browser instances or manual cookie clearing | Playwright contexts enable true per-test isolation |
| **Debugging Tools** | Playwright Inspector, trace viewer with timeline/screenshots/network | Browser DevTools only | Trace viewer provides comprehensive failure diagnostics |
| **Cross-Browser Support** | Single API for Chromium, Firefox, WebKit | Different drivers per browser (ChromeDriver, GeckoDriver) | Playwright consistent API simplifies maintenance |
| **HTTP Interception** | Native network interception and mocking | Requires proxy setup (BrowserMob Proxy) | Playwright enables API mocking without external dependencies |
| **Performance** | DevTools Protocol direct communication | JSON Wire Protocol overhead | Playwright 3-5x faster for equivalent operations |

**Playwright Selected Because:**

1. **Stable Locator Priority:** Playwright's locator methods prioritize semantic selectors reducing maintenance burden:

   ```python
   # Playwright: Stable ARIA-based selector
   page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in")
   page.get_by_label("Email address")
   
   # Selenium equivalent: Brittle CSS selector
   driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "button.btn-primary.login-btn")
   driver.find_element(By.ID, "email_input_field_123")
   ```

2. **Per-Test Browser Context Isolation:** Playwright browser contexts provide lightweight isolation ensuring no shared state between tests:

   ```python
   @pytest.fixture
   def context(browser: Browser) -> BrowserContext:
       # New context with independent cookies, storage, cache
       context = browser.new_context(
           viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080},
           locale="en-US"
       )
       yield context
       context.close()  # Complete isolation from next test
   ```

3. **Automatic Actionability Checks:** Playwright waits for elements to be visible, stable, and enabled before interactions, eliminating explicit wait statements:

   ```python
   # Playwright: Automatic waiting (no explicit waits needed)
   page.get_by_role("button", name="Submit").click()
   
   # Selenium equivalent: Manual wait required
   WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
       EC.element_to_be_clickable((By.ID, "submit-button"))
   ).click()
   ```

4. **Comprehensive Trace Collection:** Playwright traces capture screenshots, network requests, console logs, and DOM snapshots at each action, providing complete failure diagnostics:

   ```python
   context.tracing.start(screenshots=True, snapshots=True, sources=True)
   # Test execution
   context.tracing.stop(path="trace.zip")  # View with: playwright show-trace trace.zip
   ```

5. **Network Interception:** Native network mocking enables testing error handling without backend dependencies:

   ```python
   def handle_route(route):
       route.fulfill(status=500, body='{"error": "Server error"}')
   page.route("**/api/users", handle_route)
   ```

**Trade-offs Accepted:**

- **Selenium Experience Non-Transferable:** Teams with Selenium expertise face migration learning curve, mitigated by Playwright's similar concepts and comprehensive documentation
- **Browser Version Control:** Playwright installs specific browser versions, beneficial for reproducibility but requires explicit updates for latest browsers
- **Smaller Community:** Selenium has larger community (4M+ downloads/day vs Playwright 1M+), but Playwright's active development and Microsoft backing provide strong support

**Justification:**

Playwright 1.55.0 delivers superior reliability through ARIA-based locator strategies, automatic actionability waiting eliminating flakiness, and native browser context isolation enabling deterministic parallel test execution. The framework's critical requirement for "stable selectors" and "per-test isolation" makes Playwright the definitive choice over Selenium.

#### 5.3.1.3 FastAPI vs. Flask for MCP Servers

**Decision:** Adopt FastAPI 0.118.0 **for the FastAPI MCP server**. The **Playwright MCP server** is the official Microsoft implementation (agent-mode browser control) and is **consumed as a separate service**, not re-implemented here.

**Rationale:**

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers require async-first web framework supporting JSON-RPC tool endpoints, WebSocket communication (Playwright MCP), automatic API documentation, and Pydantic request/response validation. Two Python web frameworks were evaluated:

| Criteria | FastAPI 0.118.0 (Selected) | Flask 3.x | Decision Factor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Async Support** | Native async/await on Starlette ASGI | Async added in Flask 2.0, less mature | FastAPI async-native eliminates blocking during MCP tool execution |
| **Request Validation** | Built-in Pydantic validation | Requires manual validation or flask-pydantic extension | FastAPI automatic validation reduces boilerplate |
| **API Documentation** | OpenAPI/Swagger UI auto-generated at `/docs` | Requires flask-swagger or manual documentation | MCP tool discovery without manual specs |
| **WebSocket Support** | Native WebSocket support for real-time communication | Requires flask-socketio extension | Playwright MCP requires WebSocket for LLM streaming |
| **Performance** | ASGI server (uvicorn) handles concurrent requests efficiently | WSGI server (gunicorn) uses worker processes | ASGI better for MCP concurrent test data requests |
| **Type Safety** | Full Pydantic integration for type-safe endpoints | Optional type hints, no runtime validation | Pydantic reduces MCP tool parameter errors |

**FastAPI Selected Because:**

1. **Async-First Architecture:** FastAPI built on Starlette ASGI enables non-blocking MCP tool execution, critical for parallel pytest execution:

   ```python
   @app.post("/tools/seed_user")
   async def seed_user_tool(request: SeedUserRequest) -> dict:
       # Async operations don't block other MCP tool requests
       user = await user_service.create_test_user(
           role=request.role,
           email=request.email
       )
       return {"user_id": user.id, "email": user.email}
   ```

2. **Automatic OpenAPI Documentation:** MCP tool endpoints documented automatically at `/docs`, enabling developers to explore available tools without manual specifications:

   ```python
   # FastAPI generates interactive Swagger UI showing:
   # - Tool endpoint URLs (/tools/seed_user, /tools/build_payload)
   # - Request/response schemas
   # - Example payloads
   # - Try-it-out functionality
   ```

3. **Pydantic Request/Response Validation:** Built-in validation eliminates MCP tool parameter errors at runtime:

   ```python
   from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr
   
   class SeedUserRequest(BaseModel):
       role: Literal["admin", "customer", "guest"]
       email: EmailStr | None = None  # Validates email format
   
   @app.post("/tools/seed_user")
   async def seed_user_tool(request: SeedUserRequest):
       # Pydantic validates role is valid enum value
       # Pydantic validates email format if provided
       # Invalid requests return 422 with detailed error messages
   ```

4. **WebSocket Support for Playwright MCP:** Native WebSocket endpoints enable real-time LLM-browser communication:

   ```python
   @app.websocket("/explore")
   async def browser_exploration(websocket: WebSocket):
       await websocket.accept()
       while True:
           command = await websocket.receive_json()  # LLM commands
           # Execute Playwright actions based on command
           await websocket.send_json({"status": "completed"})
   ```

5. **Dependency Injection:** FastAPI dependency injection system simplifies service layer management:

   ```python
   async def get_user_service() -> UserService:
       # Database session management
       async with get_db_session() as session:
           yield UserService(session)
   
   @app.post("/tools/seed_user")
   async def seed_user_tool(
       request: SeedUserRequest,
       user_service: UserService = Depends(get_user_service)
   ):
       # Dependency injection provides configured service
       user = await user_service.create_test_user(...)
   ```

**Trade-offs Accepted:**

- **Flask Familiarity:** Teams with Flask experience face migration learning curve, mitigated by FastAPI's similar decorator syntax and extensive documentation
- **Additional Dependency:** FastAPI requires uvicorn ASGI server, adding dependency compared to Flask's development server
- **Newer Framework:** FastAPI (2018) younger than Flask (2010), but mature ecosystem and adoption by major companies (Netflix, Microsoft, Uber) demonstrate production readiness

**Justification:**

FastAPI 0.118.0 provides optimal foundation for MCP servers requiring async tool execution (preventing request blocking during parallel pytest runs), automatic API documentation (MCP tool discovery), Pydantic validation (reducing parameter errors), and WebSocket support (Playwright MCP LLM streaming). The framework's async-native design directly addresses the requirement for "non-blocking MCP tool execution during parallel test execution."

#### 5.3.1.4 httpx vs. requests for API Testing

**Decision:** Adopt httpx 0.28.1 as the HTTP client library for REST API testing and MCP server communication

**Rationale:**

The framework requires an HTTP client supporting async/await patterns for concurrent API operations, HTTP/2 protocol testing, granular timeout configuration, and integration with FastAPI MCP servers. Two Python HTTP clients were evaluated:

| Criteria | httpx 0.28.1 (Selected) | requests 2.x | Decision Factor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Async Support** | Native async/await with httpx.AsyncClient | No async support, requires thread pools | httpx enables concurrent API test execution |
| **HTTP/2 Support** | Native HTTP/2 support with `http2=True` | HTTP/1.1 only | Modern protocol testing for realistic scenarios |
| **Timeout Configuration** | Granular: connect, read, write, pool timeouts | Single timeout parameter | httpx prevents hung tests in CI pipelines |
| **Connection Pooling** | Automatic connection reuse with configurable limits | Automatic pooling, less configurability | httpx optimizes test suite performance |
| **Event Hooks** | Request/response hooks for logging/Allure attachments | Limited hook support | httpx enables centralized API logging |
| **Streaming** | Async streaming response support | Synchronous streaming only | httpx supports large response handling |

**httpx Selected Because:**

1. **Native Async/Await for Concurrent API Testing:** httpx async client enables executing multiple API calls concurrently, reducing test execution time:

   ```python
   @pytest.mark.asyncio
   async def test_concurrent_user_creation(async_api_client: httpx.AsyncClient):
       # Execute 10 user creation API calls concurrently
       tasks = [
           async_api_client.post("/users", json={"role": f"user{i}"})
           for i in range(10)
       ]
       responses = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)  # 6x faster than sequential
       assert all(r.status_code == 201 for r in responses)
   ```

2. **Granular Timeout Configuration:** Separate timeouts for connect, read, write, and pool prevent specific timeout scenarios:

   ```python
   timeout = httpx.Timeout(
       connect=10.0,  # TCP connection timeout
       read=30.0,     # Response read timeout (long for slow APIs)
       write=10.0,    # Request write timeout
       pool=5.0       # Pool acquisition timeout
   )
   client = httpx.Client(timeout=timeout)
   ```

3. **HTTP/2 Support for Modern API Testing:** Native HTTP/2 protocol support enables testing modern API infrastructure:

   ```python
   # Test HTTP/2 multiplexing behavior
   client = httpx.Client(http2=True)
   response = client.get("https://api.example.com/users")
   assert response.http_version == "HTTP/2"  # Verify protocol
   ```

4. **Event Hooks for Allure Attachments:** Request/response hooks enable centralized logging and Allure report attachments:

   ```python
   def log_request(request: httpx.Request):
       allure.attach(
           f"{request.method} {request.url}\n{request.headers}",
           name=f"Request: {request.method} {request.url.path}",
           attachment_type=allure.attachment_type.TEXT
       )
   
   client = httpx.Client(event_hooks={"request": [log_request]})
   ```

5. **MCP Client Integration:** httpx provides consistent API for both sync and async MCP server communication:

   ```python
   class MCPClient:
       def __init__(self, base_url: str, token: str):
           self.client = httpx.Client(
               base_url=base_url,
               headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
               timeout=30.0
           )
       
       def seed_user(self, role: str) -> dict:
           response = self.client.post("/tools/seed_user", json={"role": role})
           response.raise_for_status()
           return response.json()
   ```

**Trade-offs Accepted:**

- **requests Familiarity:** Teams with requests experience face minor API differences (e.g., `httpx.Client` vs `requests.Session`), mitigated by similar method names and comprehensive migration guide
- **Additional Dependency:** httpx requires `httpcore` and `h11` packages, slightly larger dependency footprint than requests
- **Smaller Ecosystem:** requests has more third-party extensions, but httpx's core feature set sufficient for test automation needs

**Justification:**

httpx 0.28.1 delivers superior capabilities for modern API testing through native async/await support (6x faster concurrent test execution), HTTP/2 protocol testing (realistic modern API scenarios), granular timeout configuration (preventing hung CI pipeline tests), and event hooks (centralized Allure attachment). The framework's requirement for "async API testing with FastAPI MCP servers" makes httpx the definitive choice over synchronous-only requests library.

#### 5.3.1.5 GitHub Actions vs. Alternative CI/CD Platforms

**Decision:** Adopt GitHub Actions as the mandatory CI/CD platform for test execution

**Rationale:**

The framework requires a CI/CD platform supporting matrix test execution (multiple Python versions, browsers), Docker service containers (FastAPI MCP server), artifact management (Allure reports, traces), and GitHub integration for pull request status checks. Three CI/CD platforms were evaluated:

| Criteria | GitHub Actions (Selected) | Jenkins | GitLab CI | Decision Factor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **GitHub Integration** | Native PR checks, commit status, issue comments | Requires webhook configuration | Requires GitHub integration | GitHub Actions zero-configuration PR integration |
| **Matrix Execution** | Native matrix strategy for parallel jobs | Requires Jenkinsfile matrix configuration | Native matrix with `.gitlab-ci.yml` | GitHub Actions simplest matrix syntax |
| **Service Containers** | Native service containers for FastAPI MCP | Requires Docker-in-Docker configuration | Native service containers | GitHub Actions easiest service management |
| **Artifact Storage** | Native artifact upload/download actions | Requires S3/artifact plugin | Native artifact management | GitHub Actions 90-day retention included |
| **Cost** | 2,000 minutes/month free, $0.008/minute after | Self-hosted or cloud pricing | Free for public repos, usage limits private | GitHub Actions sufficient free tier |
| **Report Publishing** | GitHub Pages integration for Allure reports | Requires web server setup | GitLab Pages native | GitHub Actions Pages deploy action available |

**GitHub Actions Selected Because:**

1. **Zero-Configuration GitHub Integration:** Native PR status checks, commit statuses, and issue comments without webhook setup:

   ```yaml
   # .github/workflows/test.yml
   on:
     pull_request:
       branches: [main, develop]
     push:
       branches: [main]
   
   # Automatic PR status checks, no configuration needed
   ```

2. **Matrix Strategy for Cross-Browser Testing:** Native matrix execution for testing across Python versions and browsers:

   ```yaml
   strategy:
     matrix:
       python-version: ['3.9', '3.11', '3.12']
       browser: ['chromium', 'firefox', 'webkit']
   
   # Executes 9 jobs in parallel (3 Python × 3 browsers)
   ```

3. **Service Containers for FastAPI MCP Server:** Native service container support simplifies MCP server lifecycle management:

   ```yaml
   services:
     fastapi-mcp:
       image: python:3.11
       ports:
         - 8000:8000
       env:
         FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN }}
   
   # FastAPI MCP server available at http://localhost:8000
   ```

4. **Artifact Management for Allure Reports:** Native artifact upload/download with 90-day retention:

   ```yaml
   - name: Upload Allure Results
     if: always()
     uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
     with:
       name: allure-results
       path: allure-results
       retention-days: 90
   ```

5. **GitHub Pages Publishing:** Native integration for publishing Allure HTML reports:

   ```yaml
   - name: Publish Allure Report to GitHub Pages
     uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
     with:
       github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
       publish_dir: ./allure-report
   ```

**Trade-offs Accepted:**

- **GitHub Lock-In:** Workflow YAML syntax GitHub-specific, migration to GitLab CI or Jenkins requires rewrite, accepted for GitHub-centric workflow benefits
- **Runner Limitations:** GitHub-hosted runners have 6-hour job timeout and limited CPU/memory, sufficient for test automation workloads
- **Free Tier Limits:** 2,000 minutes/month free tier, exceeded for large test suites, mitigated by self-hosted runners if needed

**Justification:**

GitHub Actions provides optimal CI/CD platform for test automation requiring matrix test execution (cross-browser, cross-Python), native service containers (FastAPI MCP server lifecycle), artifact management (Allure reports with 90-day retention), and zero-configuration GitHub integration (PR status checks, commit statuses). The framework's requirement for "GitHub Actions workflows managing MCP server lifecycle, pytest execution, and Allure report publishing" makes GitHub Actions the mandatory CI/CD choice.

### 5.3.2 Test Isolation and Parallelization Decisions

#### 5.3.2.1 Per-Test Browser Context Isolation

**Decision:** Launch a new Playwright browser context for each test function; forbid session-scoped browser contexts

**Rationale:**

Test isolation is critical for deterministic execution and parallel test safety. Three browser resource scoping strategies were evaluated:

| Scope Strategy | Advantages | Disadvantages | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Function-Scoped Context (Selected)** | Complete isolation, no shared state, parallel-safe | Higher resource overhead, slower startup | Determinism and parallel safety outweigh performance cost |
| **Session-Scoped Context** | Faster execution, single browser launch | Shared cookies/storage cause test pollution, serial execution only | Unacceptable: Tests share state causing flakiness |
| **Module-Scoped Context** | Balanced performance and isolation | Tests within module share state, partial isolation | Insufficient: Still allows test interdependencies |

**Function-Scoped Context Selected Because:**

1. **Complete Test Isolation:** Each test receives independent cookies, local storage, session storage, and cache:

   ```python
   @pytest.fixture
   def context(browser: Browser) -> BrowserContext:
       """Function-scoped context ensures zero shared state."""
       context = browser.new_context(
           viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080},
           locale="en-US",
           timezone_id="America/New_York"
       )
       yield context
       context.close()  # Complete cleanup before next test
   ```

2. **Parallel Execution Safety:** Function-scoped contexts eliminate race conditions and test interference:

   ```bash
   # Tests can execute in any order across multiple workers
   pytest -n auto  # Safe parallel execution with isolated contexts
   ```

3. **Deterministic Test Results:** Tests produce identical results regardless of execution order:

   ```python
   def test_user_login(page: Page, context: BrowserContext):
       # Fresh context: no leftover authentication cookies
       # Test always starts from unauthenticated state
   
   def test_user_logout(page: Page, context: BrowserContext):
       # Independent context: unaffected by previous test's login
       # Can run before or after test_user_login
   ```

4. **Test Failure Isolation:** Failed tests don't impact subsequent test execution:

   ```python
   def test_corrupt_state(page: Page, context: BrowserContext):
       # Even if this test corrupts application state
       pass
   
   def test_clean_state(page: Page, context: BrowserContext):
       # Next test receives fresh context, unaffected by corruption
   ```

**Forbidden Pattern - Session-Scoped Context:**

```python
# ✗ FORBIDDEN: Session-scoped context causes test pollution
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def shared_context(browser: Browser):
    context = browser.new_context()
    yield context
    # Tests share cookies, storage, causing flakiness

def test_user_login(page: Page, shared_context: BrowserContext):
    # Sets authentication cookie in shared context

def test_user_logout(page: Page, shared_context: BrowserContext):
    # ✗ PROBLEM: Inherits authentication cookie from previous test
    # Test behavior depends on execution order
```

**Implementation Enforcement:**

```python
# tests/conftest.py

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def browser():
    """Session-scoped browser is acceptable (shared binary)."""
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=os.getenv("HEADLESS", "true") == "true")
        yield browser
        browser.close()

@pytest.fixture  # ✓ CORRECT: Function scope (default)
def context(browser: Browser) -> BrowserContext:
    """Fresh context per test ensures isolation."""
    context = browser.new_context()
    yield context
    context.close()

@pytest.fixture
def page(context: BrowserContext) -> Page:
    """Fresh page in isolated context."""
    page = context.new_page()
    yield page
    page.close()

#### ✓ ENFORCEMENT: Linting rule forbids session-scoped context fixtures
#### Configure pre-commit hooks to reject PR with session-scoped browser context
```

**Performance Mitigation:**

While function-scoped contexts add overhead (\~100-200ms per test), the determinism and parallel safety benefits outweigh cost:

- **Parallel Execution Offsets Overhead:** With pytest-xdist, 8 parallel workers reduce total suite time by 75% despite per-test context overhead
- **Browser Binary Reuse:** Session-scoped browser fixture reuses browser binary across tests, only contexts recreated
- **Selective Optimization:** Critical path smoke tests can use headed mode for debugging; full regression uses headless for performance

**Justification:**

Function-scoped browser contexts represent the only acceptable isolation strategy for deterministic, parallel-safe test execution. The framework's explicit requirement to "keep tests deterministic, isolated, and parallel-friendly (new context per test)" and to "forbid session-scoped contexts" makes this the mandatory architectural decision.

#### 5.3.2.2 Test Data Management via MCP Instead of Fixture-Level Database Seeding

**Decision:** Achieve deterministic test data via FastAPI MCP server tools (`seed_user`, `build_payload`, `reset_env`) instead of fixture-level database seeding

**Rationale:**

Test data provisioning strategies impact test determinism, maintenance burden, and execution speed. Three data management approaches were evaluated:

| Approach | Advantages | Disadvantages | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MCP-Based Data (Selected)** | Centralized data logic, API-based access, language-agnostic | Additional service dependency, network latency | Centralization and reusability outweigh dependency cost |
| **Fixture-Level Database Seeding** | Direct database access, fast execution | Database schema coupling, SQL in test fixtures, not reusable | Unacceptable: Tight coupling to database schema |
| **Hardcoded Test Data** | Simplest implementation | Non-deterministic (email conflicts), unmaintainable at scale | Forbidden: Violates determinism requirement |

**MCP-Based Data Management Selected Because:**

1. **Centralized Data Logic:** FastAPI MCP server encapsulates test data generation, reducing duplication:

   ```python
   # FastAPI MCP Server: Single source of truth for user creation
   @app.post("/tools/seed_user")
   async def seed_user_tool(request: SeedUserRequest) -> dict:
       """Centralized user creation logic."""
       user = await user_service.create_test_user(
           role=request.role,
           email=request.email or f"{request.role}_{uuid.uuid4()}@test.com",
           password=generate_secure_password()
       )
       return {
           "user_id": user.id,
           "email": user.email,
           "role": user.role,
           "token": user.generate_auth_token()
       }
   ```

2. **API-Based Access Pattern:** Tests interact with MCP server via HTTP, decoupling from database schema:

   ```python
   # Test fixture: Database-agnostic data access
   @pytest.fixture
   def test_user(mcp_client: MCPClient) -> dict:
       """Create test user via MCP (no database coupling)."""
       user = mcp_client.seed_user(role="admin")
       return user
   
   def test_admin_dashboard(page: Page, test_user: dict):
       # Test uses MCP-generated user, no knowledge of database schema
       page.goto(f"{BASE_URL}/login")
       page.get_by_label("Email").fill(test_user["email"])
   ```

3. **Environment Reset for Known-Good States:** MCP `reset_env()` tool ensures tests start from clean state:

   ```python
   @pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
   def reset_test_environment(mcp_client: MCPClient):
       """Reset environment once before all tests."""
       mcp_client.reset_env()  # Truncates all tables, seeds default data
       yield
       # Optional: Reset again after all tests
   ```

4. **Template-Based Payload Generation:** MCP `build_payload()` eliminates hardcoded API request bodies:

   ```python
   def test_create_user_api(api_client: httpx.Client, mcp_client: MCPClient):
       """API test with MCP-generated payload."""
       payload = mcp_client.build_payload("create_user", {
           "role": "editor",
           "permissions": ["read", "write"]
       })
       
       response = api_client.post("/users", json=payload)
       assert response.status_code == 201
   ```

**Forbidden Pattern - Fixture-Level Database Seeding:**

```python
# ✗ FORBIDDEN: Direct database access couples tests to schema
@pytest.fixture
def test_user(database_session):
    user = User(
        email="admin@test.com",  # Hardcoded email causes conflicts
        password_hash=bcrypt.hash("password123"),
        role="admin"
    )
    database_session.add(user)
    database_session.commit()
    return user

def test_user_login(page: Page, test_user):
    # ✗ PROBLEM: Test coupled to User ORM model
    # Database schema changes break tests
    # Hardcoded email causes conflicts in parallel execution
```

**Forbidden Pattern - Hardcoded Test Data:**

```python
# ✗ FORBIDDEN: Hardcoded data violates determinism
def test_user_login(page: Page):
    page.goto(f"{BASE_URL}/login")
    page.get_by_label("Email").fill("admin@test.com")  # ✗ Hardcoded
    page.get_by_label("Password").fill("password123")  # ✗ Hardcoded
    
    # ✗ PROBLEM: User may not exist, password may be wrong
    # Tests fail unpredictably based on database state
```

**Implementation Architecture:**

```python
# MCP Client abstraction for test fixtures
class MCPClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, token: str):
        self.client = httpx.Client(
            base_url=base_url,
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
            timeout=30.0
        )
    
    def seed_user(self, role: str, email: str = None) -> dict:
        """Create test user via MCP."""
        response = self.client.post(
            "/tools/seed_user",
            json={"role": role, "email": email}
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()
    
    def build_payload(self, template: str, **params) -> dict:
        """Generate API payload from template."""
        response = self.client.post(
            "/tools/build_payload",
            json={"template": template, "parameters": params}
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()["payload"]
    
    def reset_env(self):
        """Reset test environment to clean state."""
        response = self.client.post("/tools/reset_env")
        response.raise_for_status()

#### pytest fixture provides MCP client
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def mcp_client() -> MCPClient:
    return MCPClient(
        base_url=os.getenv("FASTAPI_MCP_URL", "http://localhost:8000"),
        token=os.getenv("FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN", "dev_token")
    )
```

**Performance Considerations:**

MCP-based data management adds network latency (\~10-20ms per call), but benefits outweigh cost:

- **Caching:** MCP server caches common templates and user profiles reducing generation time
- **Batch Operations:** MCP supports batch user creation for data-intensive tests
- **Parallel Execution:** MCP server handles concurrent requests from pytest-xdist workers efficiently

**Justification:**

MCP-based test data management provides centralized data logic (single source of truth), API-based access (decoupling from database schema), deterministic reset capabilities (known-good starting states), and eliminates hardcoded test data. The framework's explicit requirement for "deterministic data via FastAPI MCP instead of fixture-level database seeding" makes this the mandatory data management strategy.

### 5.3.3 CI/CD Environment Configuration Decisions

#### 5.3.3.1 FastAPI MCP in CI, Playwright MCP Development-Only

**Decision:** FastAPI MCP server runs in all CI/CD pipelines; Playwright MCP server is development-only with explicit opt-in for CI

**Rationale:**

MCP server deployment strategies impact CI resource utilization, test execution determinism, and development workflow flexibility. Three deployment strategies were evaluated:

| Strategy | Advantages | Disadvantages | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **FastAPI MCP Always, Playwright MCP Opt-In (Selected)** | Minimal CI resources, deterministic CI runs, flexible dev workflow | Playwright MCP not tested in CI by default | Determinism and resource efficiency outweigh testing gap |
| **Both MCP Servers Always in CI** | Comprehensive testing of all components | Higher CI resource usage, slower CI runs, unnecessary for most tests | Wasteful: Playwright MCP needed for &lt;5% of scenarios |
| **Both MCP Servers Optional** | Maximum flexibility, lowest resource usage | Tests may fail if MCP unavailable, non-deterministic behavior | Unacceptable: Violates determinism requirement |

**FastAPI MCP Always, Playwright MCP Opt-In Selected Because:**

1. **FastAPI MCP Mandatory for Deterministic Test Data:** All tests depend on MCP-generated users and payloads:

   ```yaml
   # .github/workflows/test.yml
   services:
     fastapi-mcp:
       image: python:3.11
       ports:
         - 8000:8000
       env:
         FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN }}
       
       # FastAPI MCP always available in CI
   ```

2. **Playwright MCP Development-Only by Default:** LLM exploration not required for standard test execution:

   ```yaml
   # .github/workflows/test.yml
   env:
     FASTAPI_MCP_URL: http://localhost:8000
     FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN }}
     PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED: false  # Disabled by default
   
   # Playwright MCP only started if PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED=true
   ```

3. **Explicit Opt-In for Playwright MCP in CI:** Enable Playwright MCP for specific workflow runs:

   ```yaml
   # .github/workflows/exploratory-test.yml
   name: LLM Exploration Tests
   
   on:
     workflow_dispatch:  # Manual trigger only
   
   jobs:
     explore:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       
       services:
         fastapi-mcp:
           # FastAPI MCP always present
         
         playwright-mcp:
           image: python:3.11
           ports:
             - 8001:8001
           env:
             PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED: true  # Explicit opt-in
   ```

4. **Resource Optimization:** Playwright MCP consumes significant CI resources (browser binaries, WebSocket connections):

   ```bash
   # Resource comparison per CI run:
   # FastAPI MCP only: 512MB RAM, 0.5 CPU cores
   # Both MCP servers: 2GB RAM, 2 CPU cores
   # 
   # Cost savings: 75% reduction by running FastAPI MCP only
   ```

**Local Development Configuration:**

Developers control MCP server startup locally via environment variables:

```bash
# .env (local development)

#### FastAPI MCP: Always enabled locally
FASTAPI_MCP_URL=http://localhost:8000
FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN=dev_token
FASTAPI_MCP_ENABLED=true

#### Playwright MCP: Opt-in for exploration sessions
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL=http://localhost:8001
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED=false  # Enable when needed

#### LLM Configuration: Local or hosted
LLM_PROVIDER=ollama  # or openai
LLM_MODEL=llama2     # or gpt-4
```

**Startup Scripts for Development:**

```bash
# scripts/start-mcp-servers.sh

#!/bin/bash

#### Start FastAPI MCP (always)
echo "Starting FastAPI MCP server..."
uvicorn mcp_servers.fastapi_mcp.main:app --port 8000 --reload &
FASTAPI_MCP_PID=$!

#### Start Playwright MCP (if enabled)
if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
    echo "Starting Playwright MCP server..."
    uvicorn mcp_servers.playwright_mcp.main:app --port 8001 --reload &
    PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PID=$!
fi

#### Wait for servers to be ready
sleep 5

echo "MCP servers ready. FastAPI MCP: http://localhost:8000/docs"
if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
    echo "Playwright MCP: http://localhost:8001/docs"
fi
```

**Test Framework MCP Client Handling:**

MCP client gracefully handles missing Playwright MCP server:

```python
# tests/conftest.py

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def playwright_mcp_client() -> Optional[PlaywrightMCPClient]:
    """Playwright MCP client (optional)."""
    if not os.getenv("PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED", "false") == "true":
        return None  # Playwright MCP disabled
    
    mcp_url = os.getenv("PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL", "http://localhost:8001")
    
    try:
        client = PlaywrightMCPClient(mcp_url)
        client.health_check()  # Verify server availability
        return client
    except httpx.ConnectError:
        pytest.skip("Playwright MCP server not available")
```

**Justification:**

The FastAPI MCP always-on, Playwright MCP opt-in strategy optimizes CI resource utilization (75% reduction in RAM/CPU usage), ensures deterministic test execution (FastAPI MCP mandatory for data management), and provides development workflow flexibility (Playwright MCP available when needed). The framework's explicit requirement for "In CI, only the FastAPI MCP runs; the Playwright MCP is dev-only" makes this the mandatory CI/CD configuration.

#### 5.3.3.2 Externalized Environment Configuration

**Decision:** All runtime behavior controlled via environment variables; no hardcoded configuration in source code

**Rationale:**

Configuration management strategies impact deployment flexibility, security posture, and environment consistency. Three configuration approaches were evaluated:

| Approach | Advantages | Disadvantages | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Environment Variables (Selected)** | 12-factor app compliance, secure secrets management, environment-agnostic code | Requires .env files or CI secrets management | Industry best practice for cloud-native apps |
| **Configuration Files (config.yaml)** | Structured configuration, type validation | Requires file management, version control risk for secrets | Unacceptable: Secrets in version control |
| **Hardcoded Configuration** | Simplest implementation, no dependencies | Insecure, environment-specific code changes | Forbidden: Violates 12-factor principles |

**Environment Variables Selected Because:**

1. **Security:** Secrets never committed to version control:

   ```bash
   # .env (gitignored, not committed)
   FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN=secret_token_here
   LLM_API_KEY=sk-your-openai-key-here
   
   # .gitignore
   .env
   .env.*
   !.env.example
   ```

2. **Environment Agnostic:** Same codebase runs in local, staging, production:

   ```python
   # No environment-specific code branches
   BASE_URL = os.getenv("BASE_URL")  # Works in all environments
   
   # ✗ AVOID: Environment-specific branches
   # if ENV == "production":
   #     BASE_URL = "https://prod.example.com"
   # elif ENV == "staging":
   #     BASE_URL = "https://staging.example.com"
   ```

3. **CI/CD Integration:** GitHub Actions secrets injected as environment variables:

   ```yaml
   # .github/workflows/test.yml
   env:
     BASE_URL: https://staging.example.com
     API_BASE_URL: https://staging.example.com/api
     FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN }}
     LLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LLM_API_KEY }}
   ```

4. **Type-Safe Configuration:** Pydantic validates environment variables:

   ```python
   # config.py
   from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings
   
   class Settings(BaseSettings):
       # Application URLs
       base_url: str = Field(default="http://localhost:3000", alias="BASE_URL")
       api_base_url: str = Field(default="http://localhost:3000/api", alias="API_BASE_URL")
       
       # Browser configuration
       headless: bool = Field(default=True, alias="HEADLESS")
       browser: Literal["chromium", "firefox", "webkit"] = Field(default="chromium", alias="BROWSER")
       
       # MCP server configuration
       fastapi_mcp_url: str = Field(alias="FASTAPI_MCP_URL")
       fastapi_mcp_token: str = Field(alias="FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN")
       playwright_mcp_url: str = Field(default=None, alias="PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL")
       playwright_mcp_enabled: bool = Field(default=False, alias="PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED")
       
       # LLM configuration
       llm_provider: Literal["ollama", "openai"] = Field(default="ollama", alias="LLM_PROVIDER")
       llm_model: str = Field(default="llama2", alias="LLM_MODEL")
       llm_api_key: str = Field(default=None, alias="LLM_API_KEY")
       llm_base_url: str = Field(default=None, alias="LLM_BASE_URL")
       
       model_config = {
           "env_file": ".env",
           "env_file_encoding": "utf-8"
       }
   
   # Singleton settings instance
   settings = Settings()
   ```

**Minimum Required Environment Variables:**

The framework defines minimum required configuration for all environments:

| Variable | Required | Default | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BASE_URL` | Yes | `http://localhost:3000` | Web application base URL | `https://app.example.com` |
| `API_BASE_URL` | Yes | `http://localhost:3000/api` | REST API base URL | `https://api.example.com` |
| `HEADLESS` | No | `true` | Browser headless mode | `false` (local debug) |
| `BROWSER` | No | `chromium` | Browser engine selection | `firefox`, `webkit` |
| `FASTAPI_MCP_URL` | Yes | `http://localhost:8000` | FastAPI MCP server URL | `http://mcp-server:8000` |
| `FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN` | Yes | (none) | MCP authentication token | `Bearer secret123` |

| Variable | Required | Default | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL` | No | (none) | Playwright MCP server URL | `http://localhost:8001` |
| `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENABLED` | No | `false` | Enable Playwright MCP | `true` (development only) |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | No | `ollama` | LLM service provider | `openai` |
| `LLM_MODEL` | No | `llama2` | LLM model identifier | `gpt-4`, `codellama` |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | Conditional | (none) | LLM API key (OpenAI only) | `sk-abc123...` |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | No | (provider default) | Custom LLM endpoint | `http://localhost:11434` |

**Local Development Setup:**

  API_BASE_URL: https://staging.example.com/api
  HEADLESS: true
