### 6.3.1 Implementation Status and Context

**Current Implementation Status**: This Integration Architecture section documents the **planned integration design** for the <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest-based test automation framework centered on two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and GitHub Actions CI/CD infrastructure</span>. The repository currently contains only a README.md file with no code implementation. All integration patterns, <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP server architectures, test framework configurations, and CI/CD pipeline definitions</span> described below represent the approved baseline design pending stakeholder validation and implementation.

**Repository Evidence**:
- Total implementation files: 1 (README.md only - single "# playwright" heading)
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP server infrastructure code: None (FastAPI MCP server, Playwright MCP server pending creation)</span>

**Architectural Approach**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The framework employs a test-runner-centric integration architecture where pytest serves as the sole test execution engine, orchestrating Playwright browser automation, API testing via httpx, and Gherkin BDD scenario execution. Two FastAPI-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers run as supporting services: the FastAPI MCP Server provides deterministic test data management (seed_user, build_payload, reset_env tools) ensuring reproducible test execution, while the Playwright MCP Server enables LLM-driven browser exploration for AI-assisted Gherkin scenario generation (development-only). The architecture deliberately maintains clear separation of concerns—pytest executes tests, MCP servers provide auxiliary data/exploration capabilities, and no test execution logic resides in MCP endpoints.</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Infrastructure Execution Environment**: The test automation infrastructure operates exclusively in local development environments or GitHub Actions CI/CD runners—not on AWS ECS, Lambda, or other production cloud infrastructure. This is a test framework, not a deployed application backend. Development mode runs pytest, FastAPI MCP Server, and Playwright MCP Server on localhost; CI/CD mode executes pytest within GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runners with FastAPI MCP Server started as a service container. Any cloud resources referenced in this architecture must directly support test execution infrastructure:</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Permissible Cloud Integrations** (Test Infrastructure Support Only):</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Playwright Browser Binaries**: Downloaded from Microsoft CDN via `playwright install` command (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**LLM Providers**: Optional OpenAI API, Anthropic API, or Together AI for test scenario generation (development-time assistance)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Allure Report Hosting**: Optional GitHub Pages, self-hosted Allure Docker, or AWS S3 static site for HTML test report publishing</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**GitHub Actions**: Mandatory CI/CD orchestration platform for automated test execution and artifact retention</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Out-of-Scope Cloud Services**: The test framework does NOT integrate with application-level infrastructure such as Auth0 (authentication), MongoDB Atlas (databases), Redis Cloud (caching), or AWS ECS/Lambda (compute). If the Application Under Test (AUT) uses these services, project implementers abstract them behind MCP tool endpoints (e.g., Auth0 login logic within FastAPI MCP's `seed_user` tool; database seeding within `reset_env` tool). The framework provides MCP tool abstractions; implementers provide AUT-specific integration code.</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The integration architecture centers on three primary integration domains:</span>

1. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Test Execution Integration**: pytest 8.4.2 serves as the sole test orchestration engine, integrating pytest-bdd 8.1.0 for Gherkin execution, pytest-playwright 0.6.2 for browser lifecycle management, and pytest-xdist 3.6.1 for parallel distribution across CPU cores. All test flows originate from pytest discovery and fixture management—MCP servers provide supporting services only, never executing tests autonomously.</span>

2. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**MCP Service Integration**: Two FastAPI 0.118.0-based Model Context Protocol servers provide supporting capabilities: **FastAPI MCP Server** (mandatory, all environments) delivers deterministic test data management via JSON-RPC 2.0 tools (seed_user creates test users, build_payload constructs API request bodies, reset_env restores known-good state); **Playwright MCP Server** (development-only, optional) enables LLM-driven browser exploration for scenario discovery via HTTP/WebSocket endpoints (navigate, click, screenshot, get_page_structure, generate_gherkin). Both run as independent HTTP services on localhost (dev) or GitHub Actions service containers (CI), accessed via httpx client fixtures with bearer token authentication.</span>

3. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**LLM-Assisted Generation Integration**: Optional integration with local Ollama models (llama2, mistral) or hosted OpenAI-compatible APIs (GPT-4, Claude) enables test scenario generation from browser exploration sessions captured by Playwright MCP Server. LLM agents invoke Playwright MCP tools to control browsers, analyze page structures via accessibility trees, and generate draft Gherkin scenarios requiring mandatory human review before commit to tests/features/. This integration serves as an authoring assistant for developers, never executing tests autonomously—pytest remains the definitive test runner.</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Cross-cutting integration patterns include: httpx 0.28.1 async HTTP client for REST API testing and MCP server communication; Pydantic 2.10.5 for request/response validation across API clients and MCP tool endpoints; Allure-pytest 2.15.0 for comprehensive test reporting with automatic screenshot, trace, and log attachment; python-dotenv 1.0.1 for environment-based configuration enabling seamless transitions between local development, CI/CD, and staging environments; tenacity 9.0.0 for automatic retry logic on transient failures (network timeouts, browser automation flakiness).</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**CI/CD Pipeline Architecture**: GitHub Actions workflows orchestrate test execution with matrix strategy for parallel execution across Python versions (3.9, 3.11, 3.12) and browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). The test.yml workflow starts FastAPI MCP Server as a service container, installs Playwright browsers via official Docker images, executes pytest with pytest-xdist parallel distribution, captures failure diagnostics (screenshots, traces, console logs), and uploads Allure results as artifacts. The allure-report.yml workflow generates HTML reports from test results and publishes to GitHub Pages for stakeholder review. All runtime configuration (BASE_URL, API_BASE_URL, FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN, LLM_API_KEY) flows through GitHub Secrets and environment variables, enabling environment-agnostic test execution.</span>

The architecture maintains clear separation of concerns: pytest and Playwright remain the definitive test execution stack; MCP servers function solely as auxiliary data/exploration services; no test logic resides in MCP endpoints; all generated LLM content requires explicit human approval. This test-runner-centric design ensures the framework tests applications without becoming an application itself.

### 6.3.2 API Design

The test automation framework provides two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers implementing JSON-RPC 2.0 and HTTP/WebSocket protocols for deterministic test data management and LLM-driven browser exploration. These services run as supporting infrastructure alongside pytest test execution, not as replacements for the test runner.

#### 6.3.2.1 Protocol Specifications

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The framework exposes two distinct MCP server API surfaces optimized for different test automation workflows: FastAPI MCP Server for deterministic data/state management using JSON-RPC 2.0, and Playwright MCP Server for LLM-controlled browser exploration using HTTP and WebSocket protocols.</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP Server Architecture Overview</span>**:

| Server | Protocol | Purpose | Default Environment |
|--------|----------|---------|---------------------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**FastAPI MCP Server**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTPS</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic test data seeding, payload construction, environment state management</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Production + CI + Local</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Playwright MCP Server**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">JSON over HTTP + WebSocket</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM-controlled browser exploration, page structure analysis, Gherkin generation</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Development only (opt-in for CI)</span> |

#### 6.3.2.2 Authentication Methods

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The MCP servers implement simplified bearer token authentication optimized for deterministic test execution. This approach eliminates OAuth/OIDC complexity while maintaining secure service-to-service communication between pytest tests and MCP infrastructure.</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Authentication Strategy: Simple Bearer Token</span>**

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP servers validate static bearer tokens passed via HTTP Authorization header, enabling predictable authentication in CI/CD pipelines without external identity providers.</span>

**Authentication Configuration**:

| Environment | Token Source | Security Level |
|-------------|--------------|----------------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Local Development**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">`.env` file (`FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN`)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Low (predictable token)</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**CI/CD (GitHub Actions)**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">GitHub Secrets</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Medium (repository secret)</span> |
| **Staging/Production** | AWS Secrets Manager / Vault | High (centralized secrets) |

**Authentication Flow**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Test as pytest Test
    participant Fixture as MCP Client Fixture
    participant MCP as FastAPI MCP Server
    participant Auth as Bearer Token Validator
    participant Service as Tool Service

    Test->>Fixture: Request mcp_client fixture
    Fixture->>Fixture: Load FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN from env
    Fixture->>Fixture: Create httpx client with Authorization header
    Fixture-->>Test: Return MCPClient instance
    
    Test->>Fixture: mcp_client.seed_user(role="admin")
    Fixture->>MCP: POST /tools/seed_user<br/>Authorization: Bearer <token>
    MCP->>Auth: Validate bearer token
    
    alt Valid Token
        Auth-->>MCP: Token valid
        MCP->>Service: Execute seed_user tool
        Service-->>MCP: User created
        MCP-->>Fixture: JSON-RPC success response
        Fixture-->>Test: Return user data
    else Invalid Token
        Auth-->>MCP: Token invalid
        MCP-->>Fixture: 401 Unauthorized
        Fixture-->>Test: Raise HTTPError
    end
```

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Bearer Token Validation</span>** (FastAPI Dependency):

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI dependency injection validates bearer tokens on every MCP tool request:</span>

```python

# mcp_servers/fastapi_mcp/auth/bearer.py
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPBearer, HTTPAuthorizationCredentials
import os

security = HTTPBearer()

async def validate_bearer_token(
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = Depends(security)
) -> str:
    """
    Validate bearer token against FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN environment variable.
    
    For deterministic test execution, uses static token comparison.
    Production deployments should integrate with secrets management.
    """
    expected_token = os.getenv("FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN")
    
    if not expected_token:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
            detail="FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN not configured"
        )
    
    if credentials.credentials != expected_token:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid bearer token",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    
    return credentials.credentials

#### Usage in MCP tool endpoints
@app.post("/tools/seed_user")
async def seed_user_tool(
    request: SeedUserRequest,
    token: str = Depends(validate_bearer_token)
):
    """Create test user - requires valid bearer token."""
    pass
```

**Request Format with Authentication**:

```http
POST /tools/seed_user HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8000
Authorization: Bearer test-token-12345
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "seed_user",
  "params": {
    "role": "admin",
    "email": "admin@test.com"
  },
  "id": "req_001"
}
```

**Unauthenticated Request Response**:

```http
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "detail": "Invalid bearer token"
}
```

### 6.3.3 Message Processing

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The test automation framework operates through **synchronous message processing** exclusively, with no asynchronous queue processing, event-driven workflows, or batch job scheduling. All test data management and browser automation interactions execute inline within the pytest process via direct Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls.</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Architectural Approach: Deterministic Inline Execution</span>**

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Unlike traditional backend systems requiring message queues (AWS SQS, Redis Lists), event processing (AWS Lambda, CloudWatch Events), or batch scheduling (cron jobs), this test automation framework prioritizes **deterministic, reproducible test execution** through immediate request-response communication patterns.</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Message Processing Characteristics</span>**:

| Characteristic | Implementation | Rationale |
|---------------|----------------|-----------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Processing Model**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Synchronous request-response</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Tests require immediate data; no async complexity</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Test Data Provisioning**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP JSON-RPC calls (inline)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic data generation without queue delays</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Browser Automation**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright API (synchronous)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Immediate browser control within test process</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**State Management**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Isolated browser contexts per test</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Fresh state for every test execution</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Error Handling**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Immediate retry or fail-fast</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">No dead letter queues or deferred processing</span> |

#### 6.3.3.1 Synchronous Test Execution Flow (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Core Processing Pattern**: Every test scenario follows a deterministic sequence where pytest orchestrates fixture setup, MCP tool calls, browser interactions, API requests, and assertions—all executing synchronously within a single test process.</span>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pytest as pytest Test
    participant Fixture as conftest.py Fixture
    participant MCP as FastAPI MCP Server
    participant Page as Page Object
    participant Browser as Playwright Browser
    participant AUT as Application Under Test

    Note over Pytest,AUT: Synchronous Test Execution (No Async Queues)

    Pytest->>Fixture: Request test_user fixture
    Fixture->>MCP: POST /tools/seed_user (JSON-RPC)<br/>Inline call, immediate response
    MCP-->>Fixture: User data (100-500ms)
    Fixture-->>Pytest: Return user object
    
    Pytest->>Page: Navigate to login page
    Page->>Browser: page.goto(BASE_URL)
    Browser->>AUT: HTTP GET /login
    AUT-->>Browser: HTML response
    Browser-->>Page: Navigation complete
    
    Pytest->>Page: login_as(user_email, password)
    Page->>Browser: page.get_by_label("Email").fill()
    Page->>Browser: page.get_by_role("button").click()
    Browser->>AUT: HTTP POST /api/auth/login
    AUT-->>Browser: 200 OK + token
    Browser-->>Page: Login complete
    
    Pytest->>Page: assert_logged_in()
    Page->>Browser: page.get_by_text("Welcome").is_visible()
    Browser-->>Page: Element visible
    Page-->>Pytest: Assertion passed
    
    Note over Pytest: Test Complete<br/>Total execution: 3-8 seconds<br/>All operations synchronous
```

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Flow Characteristics</span>**:

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No Queuing**: MCP tool calls execute immediately; pytest waits for response before proceeding</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No Events**: No S3 upload triggers, CloudWatch schedules, or Lambda invocations</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No Batching**: Each test execution is independent; no deferred batch processing</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Predictable Timing**: Total test execution time deterministic (3-8 seconds typical for UI tests)</span>

**Test Data Provisioning Example**:

```python

# mcp_servers/fastapi_mcp/models.py
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Dict, Any

class SeedUserRequest(BaseModel):
    """
    Request to create a deterministic test user.
    
    All test users should be created via this tool to avoid hardcoded data.
    """
    role: str = Field(
        description="User role: admin, user, or guest",
        examples=["admin", "user", "guest"]
    )
    email: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Email address. Auto-generated if not provided."
    )
    attributes: Dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Additional user attributes (name, department, etc.)"
    )

class SeedUserResponse(BaseModel):
    """Successful user creation response with authentication token."""
    user_id: str = Field(description="Unique user identifier")
    email: str = Field(description="User email address")
    role: str = Field(description="Assigned role")
    token: str = Field(description="Bearer token for user authentication")
    created_at: str = Field(description="ISO 8601 timestamp")

#### FastAPI endpoint with automatic documentation
@app.post(
    "/tools/seed_user",
    response_model=SeedUserResponse,
    summary="Create deterministic test user",
    description="""
    Creates a test user with specified role and attributes.
    
    **Usage in Tests:**
    ```python
    user = mcp_client.seed_user(role="admin", email="admin@test.com")
    ```
    
    **Authentication:** Requires valid bearer token in Authorization header.
    """,
    tags=["MCP Tools"]
)
async def seed_user_tool(
    request: SeedUserRequest,
    token: str = Depends(validate_bearer_token)
) -> SeedUserResponse:
    pass
```

def test_admin_login_success(mcp_client, page, base_url):
    """

    admin_user = mcp_client.seed_user(
        role="admin",
        email="admin@test.com"

    page.get_by_label("Password").fill("Test123!")

#### 6.3.3.2 MCP Tool Invocation (Inline JSON-RPC) (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**FastAPI MCP Server Integration**: Tests invoke MCP tools via synchronous httpx client calls with JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol. The MCP server responds immediately with deterministic test data, eliminating hardcoded fixtures and enabling reproducible test execution.</span>

**Synchronous Tool Call Flow**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[pytest Test] -->|1. Call fixture| B[mcp_client Fixture]
    B -->|2. Build JSON-RPC request| C[httpx Client]
    C -->|3. HTTP POST<br/>synchronous, 30s timeout| D[FastAPI MCP Server]
    D -->|4. Execute tool logic| E[MCP Tool: seed_user]
    E -->|5. Generate data| F[Deterministic User Object]
    F -->|6. JSON-RPC response| D
    D -->|7. HTTP 200 OK| C
    C -->|8. Parse response| B
    B -->|9. Return data| A
    
    style A fill:#5b39f3,color:#fff
    style D fill:#2ecc71
    style E fill:#2ecc71
```

**MCP Client Implementation** (Synchronous):

```python

# tests/conftest.py
import pytest
import httpx
import os

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def mcp_client():
    """FastAPI MCP client for deterministic test data management."""
    class MCPClient:
        def __init__(self, base_url: str, token: str):
            self.client = httpx.Client(
                base_url=base_url,
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
                timeout=30.0
            )
        
        def seed_user(self, role: str, email: str = None, **attributes) -> dict:
            """Create deterministic test user via JSON-RPC."""
            response = self.client.post(
                "/tools/seed_user",
                json={
                    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                    "method": "seed_user",
                    "params": {
                        "role": role,
                        "email": email or f"{role}@test.com",
                        "attributes": attributes
                    },
                    "id": f"seed_user_{id(self)}"
                }
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            return response.json()["result"]
        
        def build_payload(self, template: str, **parameters) -> dict:
            """Generate API request payload from template."""
            response = self.client.post(
                "/tools/build_payload",
                json={
                    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                    "method": "build_payload",
                    "params": {
                        "template": template,
                        "parameters": parameters
                    },
                    "id": f"build_payload_{id(self)}"
                }
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            return response.json()["result"]["payload"]
        
        def reset_env(self):
            """Reset test environment to known-good state."""
            response = self.client.post(
                "/tools/reset_env",
                json={
                    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                    "method": "reset_env",
                    "params": {},
                    "id": "reset_env_request"
                }
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
    
    return MCPClient(
        base_url=os.getenv("FASTAPI_MCP_URL", "http://localhost:8000"),
        token=os.getenv("FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN", "dev-token-12345")
    )

## tests/step_defs/test_user_steps.py
from pytest_bdd import given, when, then

@given("an admin user exists")
def admin_user_exists(mcp_client, context):
    """Create admin user via MCP tool (no hardcoded data)."""
    user = mcp_client.seed_user(role="admin", name="Test Admin")
    context["admin_user"] = user
    context["admin_token"] = user["token"]

@given("a valid order payload")
def valid_order_payload(mcp_client, context):
    """Generate order payload via MCP tool."""
    payload = mcp_client.build_payload(
        template="order",
        product_id=123,
        quantity=2,
        shipping_address="123 Test St"
    )
    context["order_payload"] = payload

**Worker Isolation**:

- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Independent Execution**: Each worker runs tests synchronously without inter-worker communication</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Isolated State**: Separate browser contexts and MCP client instances per worker</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No Shared Queues**: No message queues coordinating work distribution (pytest-xdist handles scheduling)</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Thread-Safe MCP**: FastAPI MCP server handles concurrent requests from multiple workers safely</span>

#### 6.3.3.4 Scope Boundaries: What is NOT Implemented (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Explicitly Out of Scope** (per Agent Action Plan Section 0.6.4):</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The following asynchronous processing patterns found in traditional backend systems are **intentionally excluded** from this test automation framework:</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Message Queue Processing (NOT Implemented)</span>**:

- ❌ AWS SQS / Redis Lists for queued operations
- ❌ Background workers consuming from queues
- ❌ Retry queues or dead letter queues
- ❌ FIFO ordering guarantees for async operations
- ❌ Visibility timeouts and deferred message handling

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Event-Driven Architecture (NOT Implemented)</span>**:

- ❌ AWS Lambda functions triggered by events
- ❌ S3 event notifications (ObjectCreated, ObjectDeleted)
- ❌ CloudWatch Events / EventBridge rules
- ❌ SNS pub/sub messaging
- ❌ Event sourcing or CQRS patterns

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Batch Processing (NOT Implemented)</span>**:

- ❌ Scheduled batch jobs (cron, CloudWatch schedules)
- ❌ Data aggregation batch workflows
- ❌ Nightly backup/cleanup jobs
- ❌ Distributed lock management for batch operations
- ❌ Large dataset processing in chunks

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Circuit Breakers and Fallback Strategies (NOT Implemented)</span>**:

- ❌ Circuit breaker pattern for failing services
- ❌ Graceful degradation with stale cache fallbacks
- ❌ Retry with exponential backoff (beyond Playwright's built-in auto-wait)
- ❌ Bulkhead isolation for resource protection

**Rationale for Exclusion**:

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This is a **test automation framework**, not a production backend system. Test execution requirements differ fundamentally:</span>

1. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Determinism**: Tests require predictable, reproducible behavior—asynchronous queue processing introduces non-determinism</span>
2. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Fast Feedback**: Tests need immediate results (<15 minutes in CI/CD)—batch jobs delay feedback</span>
3. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Simplicity**: Synchronous patterns eliminate debugging complexity of distributed async systems</span>
4. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Isolation**: Each test runs independently—no shared state requiring event coordination</span>

**What IS Implemented**:

- ✅ Synchronous MCP tool calls (JSON-RPC over HTTP)
- ✅ Playwright's built-in auto-wait and retry for element interactions
- ✅ Parallel test execution via pytest-xdist (multi-process, not async)
- ✅ Immediate error reporting with Allure diagnostics
- ✅ Fresh browser contexts per test for isolation

#### 6.3.3.5 Testing Asynchronous Application Behavior (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Important Distinction**: While the **test framework** operates synchronously, it is fully capable of **testing applications** that use asynchronous patterns (message queues, background jobs, webhooks).</span>

**Example: Testing Async Application Features**:

```python

# tests/test_async_order_processing.py
import pytest
import time

def test_order_processing_async_flow(mcp_client, page, api_client, base_url):
    """
    Test an application that processes orders asynchronously.
    
    The test framework executes synchronously,
    but tests the application's async behavior via polling.
    """
    # 1. Create test user (synchronous MCP call)
    user = mcp_client.seed_user(role="customer", email="customer@test.com")
    
    # 2. Submit order via API (synchronous HTTP POST)
    order_response = api_client.create_order(
        user_token=user["token"],
        items=[{"product_id": "prod_123", "quantity": 2}]
    )
    order_id = order_response["order_id"]
    
    # 3. Application processes order asynchronously (background job)
    # Test waits and polls for completion (synchronous polling)
    max_wait_time = 30  # seconds
    poll_interval = 2   # seconds
    
    for elapsed in range(0, max_wait_time, poll_interval):
        order_status = api_client.get_order(order_id)
        
        if order_status["status"] == "completed":
            break
        
        time.sleep(poll_interval)
    else:
        pytest.fail(f"Order {order_id} not completed within {max_wait_time}s")
    
    # 4. Verify order completion in UI (synchronous browser interaction)
    page.goto(f"{base_url}/orders/{order_id}")
    assert page.get_by_text("Order Completed").is_visible()
```

**Pattern**: The test framework remains synchronous (no async/await, no message queues), but tests async application behavior through **synchronous polling** and **timeout-based waits**.

#### 6.3.3.6 Summary: Synchronous Processing Philosophy (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The test automation framework prioritizes **deterministic, reproducible test execution** through synchronous message processing patterns. This architectural decision aligns with test automation best practices:</span>

**Core Principles**:

1. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Immediate Feedback**: All operations (MCP tool calls, browser interactions, API requests) return results immediately within test execution timeframe</span>
2. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Predictable Timing**: Test execution time deterministic and bounded (no unpredictable queue delays)</span>
3. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Clear Attribution**: Test failures map directly to specific test steps, not deferred async operations</span>
4. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Simplified Debugging**: Synchronous stack traces and linear execution flow simplify failure diagnosis</span>

**Integration Architecture Alignment**:

| Component | Processing Model | Rationale |
|-----------|------------------|-----------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**pytest Test Runner**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Synchronous execution, sequential steps</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Clear test flow, predictable outcomes</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**FastAPI MCP Server**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Synchronous JSON-RPC endpoints</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Immediate test data provisioning</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Playwright Browser Automation**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Synchronous API with auto-wait</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Stable interactions without manual polling</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**httpx API Client**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Synchronous HTTP requests</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Immediate API response validation</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**pytest-xdist Parallelism**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Multi-process (not async/await)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Fast execution without async complexity</span> |

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This synchronous processing architecture ensures the test automation framework remains simple, maintainable, and reliable—avoiding the operational complexity of distributed asynchronous systems while delivering fast, deterministic test execution for CI/CD pipelines.</span>

### 6.3.4 External Systems

#### 6.3.4.1 Third-Party Integration Patterns (updated)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The test automation framework integrates with a minimal set of external systems focused exclusively on test execution infrastructure. The framework purposely does NOT integrate with Auth0, MongoDB, Redis, or other application-level services—any Application Under Test (AUT) authentication or data sources are abstracted behind MCP tools and left to project implementers.</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Architectural Principle: Test Framework vs. Application Concerns**</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">This is a test automation framework, not a web application backend. External integrations serve test execution needs (browsers, LLM assistants, CI/CD, reporting) rather than business application needs (databases, authentication providers, message queues). The framework tests applications; it does not replicate application infrastructure.</span>

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">External System Integration Map</span>**:

| External System | Purpose | Integration Type | Environment |
|-----------------|---------|------------------|-------------|

| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**FastAPI MCP Server**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic test data/state management</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local HTTP JSON-RPC service (env: `FASTAPI_MCP_URL`)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local + CI/CD (mandatory)</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Playwright MCP Server**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM-driven browser exploration</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local HTTP + WebSocket service (env: `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL`)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local dev only (optional)</span> |

| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**GitHub Actions**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">CI/CD orchestration and test execution</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">GitHub Workflows, Docker services</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">CI/CD only (mandatory)</span> |

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Critical Note: MCP Servers are Local/CI Services**</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP Server and Playwright MCP Server are NOT managed cloud services like AWS Lambda or Azure Functions. They are in-repository Python applications that run as:</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Local Development**: Started via `uvicorn mcp_servers.fastapi_mcp.main:app` on localhost ports</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**CI/CD Environment**: Started as background services in GitHub Actions workflows or Docker Compose services</span>
- <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**No External Hosting**: No AWS ECS, Lambda, or cloud provider deployments required</span>

| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Redis / Caching**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">NOT integrated directly</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP tools abstract cache management; implementers add cache control to `reset_env` tool</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**External APIs**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">NOT integrated directly</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Tests verify AUT behavior; API mocking handled by AUT or test fixtures, not framework</span> |

##### 6.3.4.1.1 Playwright Browser Binaries Integration

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Purpose**: Playwright downloads and manages browser binaries (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) for cross-browser test execution. These binaries are external system dependencies installed via the Playwright CLI.</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Installation Method**</span>:

```bash

# Install Playwright Python package (from pyproject.toml)
pip install playwright==1.55.0

#### Download browser binaries (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)
playwright install chromium firefox webkit

#### Verify installation
playwright --version
```

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Browser Binary Storage Locations**</span>:

| Platform | Storage Path | Size (All 3 Browsers) |
|----------|--------------|----------------------|
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**macOS**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">~1.2 GB</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Linux**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">`~/.cache/ms-playwright`</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">~1.2 GB</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Windows**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">`%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\ms-playwright`</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">~1.2 GB</span> |
| <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**CI/CD (Docker)**</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">`/ms-playwright` (baked into image)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Included in base image</span> |

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Usage in LLM Exploration**</span>:

```python

# llm/exploration_agent.py
import os
import httpx
from openai import OpenAI

def explore_application(base_url: str, exploration_goal: str):
    """
    LLM agent explores application and generates draft Gherkin scenarios.
    
    IMPORTANT: This is a development-time authoring assistant ONLY.
    Generated scenarios require human review before pytest execution.
    """
    # Initialize LLM client
    llm_client = OpenAI(
        api_key=os.getenv("LLM_API_KEY"),
        base_url=os.getenv("LLM_BASE_URL")
    )
    
    # Initialize Playwright MCP client
    playwright_mcp = httpx.Client(
        base_url=os.getenv("PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL", "http://localhost:8001"),
        timeout=60.0
    )
    
    exploration_log = []
    
    # LLM instructs Playwright MCP to navigate
    response = playwright_mcp.post(
        "/tools/navigate",
        json={"url": base_url}
    )
    exploration_log.append({"action": "navigate", "result": response.json()})
    
    # LLM analyzes page structure
    response = playwright_mcp.post("/tools/get_page_structure", json={})
    page_structure = response.json()
    exploration_log.append({"action": "get_page_structure", "result": page_structure})
    
    # LLM generates prompt for next action
    prompt = f"""
    You are exploring a web application to generate test scenarios.
    Goal: {exploration_goal}
    
    Current page structure:
    {page_structure}
    
    What action should you take next? Respond with a JSON object:
    {{"tool": "click|type|screenshot", "params": {{...}}}}
    """
    
    llm_response = llm_client.chat.completions.create(
        model=os.getenv("LLM_MODEL", "gpt-4-turbo-preview"),
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        temperature=0.7
    )
    
    next_action = llm_response.choices[0].message.content
    # ... (continue exploration loop)
    
    # Generate Gherkin from exploration log
    gherkin_response = playwright_mcp.post(
        "/tools/generate_gherkin",
        json={"exploration_log": exploration_log}
    )
    
    draft_gherkin = gherkin_response.json()["gherkin"]
    
    # Write draft scenario to file (REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW)
    with open("tests/features/_drafts/generated_scenario.feature", "w") as f:
        f.write(draft_gherkin)
        f.write("\n\n# DRAFT SCENARIO - REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW BEFORE COMMIT\n")
        f.write("# LLM Assumptions: [List any assumptions made during exploration]\n")
        f.write("# Open Questions: [List questions for human reviewer]\n")
    
    print("Draft scenario generated: tests/features/_drafts/generated_scenario.feature")
    print("REVIEW REQUIRED: Human must approve before pytest execution")
    
    return draft_gherkin

#### CLI usage:
#### python -m llm.exploration_agent --url http://localhost:3000 --goal "Test login flow"
```

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Critical Constraints for LLM Integration</span>**:

1. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP is NOT a Test Runner</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP Server provides browser automation tools to LLM agents for exploration; it does not execute production tests</span>
2. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Human Approval is Mandatory</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All LLM-generated scenarios must be reviewed, validated, and explicitly approved by developers before integration into the test suite</span>
3. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Development-Only Service</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright MCP Server runs only in local development environments; not deployed to CI/CD by default</span>
4. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest is the ONLY Test Runner</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM generates scenarios for pytest execution; LLM agents do not autonomously execute tests</span>
5. **Exploration Transparency**: All LLM exploration logs and generated scenarios include metadata documenting assumptions, open questions, and areas requiring human judgment

#### 6.3.5.3 <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Integration Architecture Summary

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The test automation framework implements a clear separation of concerns across three integration layers:</span>

```mermaid

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Integration Layer Responsibilities</span>**:

| Layer | Components | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Primary Responsibility</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment</span> |
|-------|------------|----------------------|------------|
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test Execution</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest, conftest.py, step definitions, page objects</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test orchestration, browser automation, assertion validation</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local + CI/CD</span> |
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Supporting Services</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP (mandatory), Playwright MCP (dev-only)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic data management, LLM browser exploration</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Local + CI/CD (FastAPI), Local only (Playwright)</span> |
| **External Systems** | Playwright browsers, Application Under Test, LLM providers | Browser execution, target application, AI-assisted authoring | All environments (browsers/AUT), Local + optional CI (LLM) |

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Key Architectural Principles</span>**:

1. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest is the ONLY Test Runner</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All test execution flows originate from pytest; MCP servers provide supporting services exclusively</span>
2. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP Servers are Supporting Services</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP and Playwright MCP do not execute tests; they provide deterministic data management and exploration capabilities</span>
3. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic Test Data Management</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Zero hardcoded test data; all users, payloads, and state retrieved from FastAPI MCP tools</span>
4. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM as Authoring Assistant</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">LLM agents generate draft scenarios requiring human approval; no autonomous test execution</span>
5. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test Isolation via Browser Contexts</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Each test receives a fresh Playwright context with isolated storage, cookies, and cache</span>
6. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Stable Locator Strategies</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Page objects use ARIA roles and data-testid attributes; no brittle CSS/XPath selectors</span>
7. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment-Based Configuration</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">All runtime behavior controlled via .env files and environment variables</span>

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Python Client Integration**</span>:

```python

# llm/llm_client.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

def get_llm_client():
    """Factory function for LLM client based on environment configuration."""
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER", "ollama")
    
    if provider == "openai":
        return OpenAI(
            api_key=os.getenv("LLM_API_KEY"),
            base_url=os.getenv("LLM_BASE_URL"),
            timeout=int(os.getenv("LLM_TIMEOUT", "60"))
        )
    elif provider == "anthropic":
        # Anthropic via OpenAI-compatible proxy
        return OpenAI(
            api_key=os.getenv("LLM_API_KEY"),
            base_url="https://anthropic-proxy.example.com/v1"
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported LLM provider: {provider}")
```

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">**Local LLM Integration (Ollama)**</span>:

LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1     # Ollama API endpoint
```

### 6.3.5 Integration Flows and Diagrams

This section documents the <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">primary integration flows for the pytest-based test automation framework, emphasizing the clear separation between pytest as the sole test runner and MCP servers as supporting services</span>. <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The framework integrates with two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers—FastAPI MCP for deterministic test data management and Playwright MCP for LLM-driven browser exploration—while maintaining pytest as the definitive test execution engine.</span>

#### 6.3.5.1 <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test Execution Integration Flow (pytest → FastAPI MCP → Application Under Test)

<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">The primary integration pattern for test execution demonstrates how pytest orchestrates deterministic test scenarios by retrieving test data from FastAPI MCP Server, executing test logic via Playwright page objects or httpx API clients, and validating behavior against the Application Under Test (AUT). This flow emphasizes that pytest is the ONLY test runner; FastAPI MCP provides supporting data management services exclusively.</span>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pytest as pytest Test Runner<br/>(ONLY Test Orchestrator)
    participant Fixtures as conftest.py Fixtures<br/>(Browser Context & MCP Client)
    participant MCP as FastAPI MCP Server<br/>(JSON-RPC 2.0 Supporting Service)
    participant Tools as MCP Tools<br/>(seed_user, build_payload,<br/>reset_env, query_state)
    participant PageObj as Page Object<br/>(Playwright Automation)
    participant Browser as Browser<br/>(Chromium/Firefox/WebKit)
    participant AUT as Application Under Test<br/>(Web UI + REST API)

    Note over Pytest,AUT: Test Setup Phase - Deterministic Data Preparation
    
    Pytest->>Fixtures: Request mcp_client fixture
    Fixtures->>MCP: Establish JSON-RPC connection
    MCP-->>Fixtures: Connection established
    
    Pytest->>Fixtures: Call mcp_client.seed_user(role="admin")
    Fixtures->>MCP: POST /tools/seed_user<br/>JSON-RPC: {"method": "seed_user", "params": {"role": "admin"}}
    MCP->>Tools: Invoke seed_user tool
    Tools->>Tools: Generate deterministic test user<br/>(no hardcoded data)
    Tools-->>MCP: User data + auth token
    MCP-->>Fixtures: JSON-RPC response: {"result": {"user_id": "...", "token": "..."}}
    Fixtures-->>Pytest: Return test user object
    
    Pytest->>Fixtures: Call mcp_client.build_payload("order", product_id=123)
    Fixtures->>MCP: POST /tools/build_payload<br/>JSON-RPC: {"method": "build_payload", "params": {...}}
    MCP->>Tools: Invoke build_payload tool
    Tools->>Tools: Generate request payload from template
    Tools-->>MCP: Structured payload
    MCP-->>Fixtures: JSON-RPC response: {"result": {"payload": {...}}}
    Fixtures-->>Pytest: Return API request payload
    
    Note over Pytest,AUT: Test Execution Phase - UI and API Validation
    
    Pytest->>Fixtures: Request browser_context fixture
    Fixtures-->>Pytest: Return isolated Playwright context
    
    Pytest->>PageObj: Navigate to login page
    PageObj->>Browser: page.goto(BASE_URL + "/login")
    Browser->>AUT: HTTP GET /login
    AUT-->>Browser: Render login UI
    Browser-->>PageObj: Page loaded
    
    Pytest->>PageObj: login_as(test_user)
    PageObj->>Browser: page.get_by_label("Email").fill(test_user.email)
    PageObj->>Browser: page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
    Browser->>AUT: HTTP POST /api/auth/login
    AUT-->>Browser: 200 OK + JWT token + redirect
    Browser->>AUT: HTTP GET /dashboard
    AUT-->>Browser: Render dashboard UI
    Browser-->>PageObj: Navigation complete
    PageObj-->>Pytest: Login successful
    
    Pytest->>PageObj: Assert dashboard visible
    PageObj->>Browser: page.get_by_text("Welcome").is_visible()
    Browser-->>PageObj: Element visible: true
    PageObj-->>Pytest: Assertion passed
    
    Note over Pytest,AUT: Test Cleanup Phase
    
    Pytest->>Fixtures: Teardown browser_context
    Fixtures->>Browser: Close isolated context
    Browser-->>Fixtures: Context closed
    
    Pytest->>MCP: Optional: Call reset_env for next test
    MCP->>Tools: Invoke reset_env tool
    Tools->>Tools: Reset environment state
    Tools-->>MCP: Environment reset complete
    MCP-->>Pytest: JSON-RPC response: {"result": {"status": "success"}}
```

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Integration Flow Characteristics</span>**:

| Component | Responsibility | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Protocol</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Latency</span> |
|-----------|---------------|-----------|----------|
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest Test Runner</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Test discovery, orchestration, fixture management, assertion validation</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Python function calls</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">< 1ms</span> |
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">conftest.py Fixtures</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP client wrapper, browser context lifecycle, test data retrieval</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">pytest fixture injection</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">< 10ms</span> |
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP Server</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic test data generation ONLY (not a test runner)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">100-500ms</span> |
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP Tools</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">seed_user, build_payload, reset_env, query_state implementations</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Internal service calls</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">50-300ms</span> |
| **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Page Objects</span>** | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">UI interaction abstraction with stable locators (ARIA, data-testid)</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Playwright Python API</span> | <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">< 5ms</span> |
| **Playwright Browser** | Cross-browser automation (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) | Browser DevTools Protocol | 50-200ms per action |
| **Application Under Test** | Target web application or REST API being validated | HTTP/HTTPS | Variable (AUT-dependent) |

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Key Integration Patterns</span>**:

1. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Deterministic Data Management</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Tests never contain hardcoded data; all test users, payloads, and state retrieved from FastAPI MCP Server tools ensuring reproducible test execution</span>
2. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">JSON-RPC Communication</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">MCP client fixtures invoke tools via standard JSON-RPC 2.0 requests with structured error handling for invalid parameters or server failures</span>
3. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Isolated Browser Contexts</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Each test receives a fresh Playwright browser context with isolated cookies, storage, and cache preventing test interference</span>
4. **<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Page Object Delegation</span>**: <span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Step definitions remain concise (1-5 lines) by delegating UI interactions to page object methods that encapsulate stable locator strategies</span>
5. **Synchronous Execution**: All test flows execute synchronously with immediate responses; no asynchronous queues or background processing

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">Environment Configuration</span>**:

```bash

# .env file - Local Development
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000                     # Application Under Test URL
API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000/api            # REST API base endpoint
HEADLESS=false                                     # Browser mode (true for CI)
FASTAPI_MCP_URL=http://localhost:8000             # FastAPI MCP Server endpoint
FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN=dev-token-local-12345           # Bearer authentication token

## .env.ci file - GitHub Actions CI/CD
BASE_URL=${TEST_ENV_BASE_URL}                     # Staging/test environment URL
API_BASE_URL=${TEST_ENV_API_BASE_URL}             # Staging API endpoint
HEADLESS=true                                      # Always headless in CI
FASTAPI_MCP_URL=http://fastapi-mcp:8000           # Docker Compose service name
FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN=${FASTAPI_MCP_TOKEN}            # GitHub Secrets injection
```

**<span style="background-color: rgba(91, 57, 243, 0.2)">FastAPI MCP Tool Usage Examples</span>**:

```python

# .env file - Local Development with Ollama (Free)
LLM_PROVIDER=ollama                                # Local LLM provider
LLM_MODEL=llama2                                   # Model from `ollama list`
LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1            # Ollama API endpoint
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL=http://localhost:8001          # Playwright MCP Server

# .env file - Development with OpenAI (Cloud)
LLM_PROVIDER=openai                                # Cloud LLM provider
LLM_MODEL=gpt-4-turbo-preview                     # OpenAI model identifier
LLM_API_KEY=sk-proj-abc123xyz...                  # OpenAI API key
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_URL=http://localhost:8001          # Playwright MCP Server

#### CI/CD: Playwright MCP is NOT started by default (dev-only service)
```
